7.s: rājadharmān pravakṣyāmi yathāvṛtto bhavennṛpaḥ saṃbhavaśca yathā tasya siddhiśca paramā yathā
7.d: राजधर्मान् प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावृत्तो भवेन्नृपः संभवश्च यथा तस्य सिद्धिश्च परमा यथा
7.e: I am going to expound the duties of Kings; how the Lord of Men should conduct himself, how he came into existence and how excellent success accrues to him.

7.s: brāhmaṃ prāptena saṃskāraṃ kṣatriyeṇa yathāvidhi sarvasyāsya yathānyāyaṃ kartavyaṃ parirakṣaṇam
7.d: ब्राह्मं प्राप्तेन संस्कारं क्षत्रियेण यथाविधि सर्वस्यास्य यथान्यायं कर्तव्यं परिरक्षणम्
7.e: The protection of all this shall be done according to law, by the Kṣatriya who has received the Vedic training in due form.

7.s: arājake hi loke 'smin sarvato vidruto bhayāt rakṣārthamasya sarvasya rājānamasṛjat prabhuḥ
7.d: अराजके हि लोके ऽस्मिन् सर्वतो विद्रुतो भयात् रक्षार्थमस्य सर्वस्य राजानमसृजत् प्रभुः
7.e: At a time when the people were without a King, and were utterly perturbed through fear, the Lord created the King for the protection of all this;—(3) taking out the essential constituents of Indra, Vāyu, Yama, Sūrya, Varuṇa, Chandra and Kubera

7.s: indrānilayamārkāṇāmagneśca varuṇasya ca candravitteśayoścaiva mātrā nirhṛtya śāśvatīḥ
7.d: इन्द्रानिलयमार्काणामग्नेश्च वरुणस्य च चन्द्रवित्तेशयोश्चैव मात्रा निर्हृत्य शाश्वतीः
7.e: At a time when the people were without a King, and were utterly perturbed through fear, the Lord created the King for the protection of all this;—(3) taking out the essential constituents of Indra, Vāyu, Yama, Sūrya, Varuṇa, Chandra and Kubera

7.s: yasmādeṣāṃ surendrāṇāṃ mātrābhyo nirmito nṛpaḥ tasmādabhibhavatyeṣa sarvabhūtāni tejasā
7.d: यस्मादेषां सुरेन्द्राणां मात्राभ्यो निर्मितो नृपः तस्मादभिभवत्येष सर्वभूतानि तेजसा
7.e: In as much as the King was created with the constituent elements of these principal Gods, he surpasses all living beings by his glory.

7.s: tapatyādityavaccaiṣa cakṣūṃṣi ca manāṃsi ca na cainaṃ bhuvi śaknoti kaścidapyabhivīkṣitum
7.d: तपत्यादित्यवच्चैष चक्षूंषि च मनांसि च न चैनं भुवि शक्नोति कश्चिदप्यभिवीक्षितुम्
7.e: Like the sun, he burns the eyes and minds (of man); no one on the earth can even gaze at him.

7.s: so 'gnirbhavati vāyuśca so 'rkaḥ somaḥ sa dharmarāṭ sa kuberaḥ sa varuṇaḥ sa mahendraḥ prabhāvataḥ sa caindraḥ svaprabhāvataḥ]
7.d: सो ऽग्निर्भवति वायुश्च सो ऽर्कः सोमः स धर्मराट् स कुबेरः स वरुणः स महेन्द्रः प्रभावतः स चैन्द्रः स्वप्रभावतः]
7.e: On account of his puissance he is Agni, Vāyu and Sūrya; he is Soma and Yama; he is Kubera, he is Varuṇa and he is Indra.

7.s: bālo 'pi nāvamāntavyo manuṣya iti bhūmipaḥ mahatī devatā hyeṣā nararūpeṇa tiṣṭhati
7.d: बालो ऽपि नावमान्तव्यो मनुष्य इति भूमिपः महती देवता ह्येषा नररूपेण तिष्ठति
7.e: Even though an infant, the King shall not be despised as if he were merely human; because he is a great divinity in human form.

7.s: ekameva dahatyagnirnaraṃ durupasarpiṇam kulaṃ dahati rājā 'gniḥ sapaśudravyasañcayam
7.d: एकमेव दहत्यग्निर्नरं दुरुपसर्पिणम् कुलं दहति राजा ऽग्निः सपशुद्रव्यसञ्चयम्
7.e: Fire burns only one man who may happen to approach it carelessly; the fire of the King, on the other hand, consumes the entire family, along with its cattle and hoard of wealth.

7.s: kāryaṃ so 'vekṣya śaktiṃ ca deśakālau ca tattvataḥ kurute dharmasiddhyarthaṃ viśvarūpaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
7.d: कार्यं सो ऽवेक्ष्य शक्तिं च देशकालौ च तत्त्वतः कुरुते धर्मसिद्ध्यर्थं विश्वरूपं पुनः पुनः
7.e: For the proper fulfilment of his duty, he assumes many forms re peatedly, after having carefully considered the nature of his business, his power and the conditions of time and place.

7.s: yasya prasāde padmā śrīrvijayaśca parākrame mṛtyuśca vasati krodhe sarvatejomayo hi saḥ
7.d: यस्य प्रसादे पद्मा श्रीर्विजयश्च पराक्रमे मृत्युश्च वसति क्रोधे सर्वतेजोमयो हि सः
7.e: He indeed contains in himself the splendour of all, in whose favour dwells the Goddess of Fortune, in whose valour rests victory and in whose anger abides death.

7.s: taṃ yastu dveṣṭi saṃmohāt sa vinaśyatyasaṃśayam tasya hyāśu vināśāya rājā prakurute manaḥ
7.d: तं यस्तु द्वेष्टि संमोहात् स विनश्यत्यसंशयम् तस्य ह्याशु विनाशाय राजा प्रकुरुते मनः
7.e: He, who, through folly, is hostile towards him, doubtlessly perishes; because the King makes up his mind for his quick destruction.

7.s: tasmāddharmaṃ yamiṣṭeṣu sa vyavasyennarādhipaḥ aniṣṭaṃ cāpyaniṣṭeṣu taṃ dharmaṃ na vicālayet
7.d: तस्माद्धर्मं यमिष्टेषु स व्यवस्येन्नराधिपः अनिष्टं चाप्यनिष्टेषु तं धर्मं न विचालयेत्
7.e: For this reason no one should transgress that favourable decree which the King should ordain in favour of his favourites, or that unfavourable decree that he should ordain against those in his disfavour.

7.s: tasyārthe sarvabhūtānāṃ goptāraṃ dharmamātmajam tadarthaṃ brahmatejomayaṃ daṇḍamasṛjat pūrvamīśvaraḥ
7.d: तस्यार्थे सर्वभूतानां गोप्तारं धर्ममात्मजम् तदर्थं ब्रह्मतेजोमयं दण्डमसृजत् पूर्वमीश्वरः
7.e: For his sake, the Lord, at first, created Punishment, which is Law born of the Lord Himself, an incarnation of divine glory and the protector of all creatures.

7.s: tasya sarvāṇi bhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca bhayādbhogāya kalpante svadharmātna calanti ca
7.d: तस्य सर्वाणि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च भयाद्भोगाय कल्पन्ते स्वधर्मात्न चलन्ति च
7.e: It is through fear of him that all living beings, movable as well as immovable, go to subserve the experiences (of men) and do not swerve from their duties.

7.s: taṃ deśakālau śaktiṃ ca vidyāṃ cāvekṣya tattvataḥ yathārhataḥ saṃpraṇayennareṣvanyāyavartiṣu
7.d: तं देशकालौ शक्तिं च विद्यां चावेक्ष्य तत्त्वतः यथार्हतः संप्रणयेन्नरेष्वन्यायवर्तिषु
7.e: To men who act unlawfully, he shall mete it out appropriately, having carefully considered the time and place, as also the strength and learning.

7.s: sa rājā puruṣo daṇḍaḥ sa netā śāsitā ca saḥ caturṇāmāśramāṇāṃ ca dharmasya pratibhūḥ smṛtaḥ
7.d: स राजा पुरुषो दण्डः स नेता शासिता च सः चतुर्णामाश्रमाणां च धर्मस्य प्रतिभूः स्मृतः
7.e: That punishment is the ‘King’, the ‘Man’; that is the ‘Leader’ and the ‘Ruler’ and that has been declared to be the ‘surety’ for the Law of the Four Stages.

7.s: daṇḍaḥ śāsti prajāḥ sarvā daṇḍa evābhirakṣati daṇḍaḥ supteṣu jāgarti daṇḍaṃ dharmaṃ vidurbudhāḥ
7.d: दण्डः शास्ति प्रजाः सर्वा दण्ड एवाभिरक्षति दण्डः सुप्तेषु जागर्ति दण्डं धर्मं विदुर्बुधाः
7.e: Punishment governs all creatures; Punishment alone protects them; Punishment lies awake while all are asleep; the wise regard Punishment as Law itself.

7.s: samīkṣya sa dhṛtaḥ samyak sarvā rañjayati prajāḥ asamīkṣya praṇītastu vināśayati sarvataḥ
7.d: समीक्ष्य स धृतः सम्यक् सर्वा रञ्जयति प्रजाः असमीक्ष्य प्रणीतस्तु विनाशयति सर्वतः
7.e: When meted out properly after due investigation, it makes all people happy; but when meted out without due investigation, it destroys all things.

7.s: yadi na praṇayedrājā daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyeṣvatandritaḥ śūle matsyānivāpakṣyan durbalān balavattarāḥ
7.d: यदि न प्रणयेद्राजा दण्डं दण्ड्येष्वतन्द्रितः शूले मत्स्यानिवापक्ष्यन् दुर्बलान् बलवत्तराः
7.e: If the King did not untiringly mete out punishment to those that deserve punishment, the stronger would have boasted the weaker, like fish, on the spit;

7.s: adyāt kākaḥ puroḍāśaṃ śvā ca lihyāddhavistathā śvā 'valihyādd svāmyaṃ ca na syāt kasmiṃścit pravartetādharauttaram
7.d: अद्यात् काकः पुरोडाशं श्वा च लिह्याद्धविस्तथा श्वा ऽवलिह्याद्द् स्वाम्यं च न स्यात् कस्मिंश्चित् प्रवर्तेताधरौत्तरम्
7.e: The crow would eat the Sacrificial Cake, and the dog would lick the offering-materials; rights of ownership would not remain with any one and there would be a confusion among the high and low.

7.s: sarvo daṇḍajito loko durlabho hi śucirnaraḥ daṇḍasya hi bhayāt sarvaṃ jagadbhogāya kalpate
7.d: सर्वो दण्डजितो लोको दुर्लभो हि शुचिर्नरः दण्डस्य हि भयात् सर्वं जगद्भोगाय कल्पते
7.e: It is by punishment that all people are kept under control; for an absolutely guileless man is hard to find; it is through fear of punishment that the world subserves the experiences (of men).

7.s: devadānavagandharvā rakṣāṃsi patagauragāḥ te 'pi bhogāya kalpante daṇḍenaiva nipīḍitāḥ
7.d: देवदानवगन्धर्वा रक्षांसि पतगौरगाः ते ऽपि भोगाय कल्पन्ते दण्डेनैव निपीडिताः
7.e: It is only when pressed by Punishment that Devas, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Rākṣasas, Birds and Reptiles subserve the experiences (of others).

7.s: duṣyeyuḥ sarvavarṇāśca bhidyeran sarvasetavaḥ sarvalokaprakopaśca bhaveddaṇḍasya vibhramāt
7.d: दुष्येयुः सर्ववर्णाश्च भिद्येरन् सर्वसेतवः सर्वलोकप्रकोपश्च भवेद्दण्डस्य विभ्रमात्
7.e: All the castes would become corrupt, all barriers would be broken through, and there would be disruption among all the regions,—if there were any mistakes in regard to punishment.

7.s: yatra śyāmo lohitākṣo daṇḍaścarati pāpahā prajāstatra na muhyanti netā cet sādhu paśyati
7.d: यत्र श्यामो लोहिताक्षो दण्डश्चरति पापहा प्रजास्तत्र न मुह्यन्ति नेता चेत् साधु पश्यति
7.e: Where dark-complexioned and red-eyed Punishment stalks about, destroying sins, there the people are not misled, provided that the Governor discerns rightly.

7.s: tasyāhuḥ saṃpraṇetāraṃ rājānaṃ satyavādinam samīkṣyakāriṇaṃ prājñaṃ dharmakāmārthakovidam
7.d: तस्याहुः संप्रणेतारं राजानं सत्यवादिनम् समीक्ष्यकारिणं प्राज्ञं धर्मकामार्थकोविदम्
7.e: They declare that King to be the just governor who is truth ful of speech, who acts after due consideration, who is wise and who knows the essence of virtue, pleasure and wealth.

7.s: taṃ rājā praṇayan samyak trivargeṇābhivardhate kāmātmā viṣamaḥ kṣudro daṇḍenaiva nihanyate kāmāndho
7.d: तं राजा प्रणयन् सम्यक् त्रिवर्गेणाभिवर्धते कामात्मा विषमः क्षुद्रो दण्डेनैव निहन्यते कामान्धो
7.e: The King who metes out punishment in the proper manner prospers in respect of his three aims; he who is blinded by affection, unfair, or mean is destroyed by that same punishment.

7.s: daṇḍo hi sumahattejo durdharaścākṛtātmabhiḥ dharmādvicalitaṃ hanti nṛpameva sabāndhavam
7.d: दण्डो हि सुमहत्तेजो दुर्धरश्चाकृतात्मभिः धर्माद्विचलितं हन्ति नृपमेव सबान्धवम्
7.e: Punishment, which is a tremendous force, hard to be controlled by persons with undisciplined minds, destroys the King who has swerved from duty, along with his relatives.

7.s: tato durgaṃ ca rāṣṭraṃ ca lokaṃ ca sacarācaram antarikṣagatāṃścaiva munīn devāṃśca pīḍayet
7.d: ततो दुर्गं च राष्ट्रं च लोकं च सचराचरम् अन्तरिक्षगतांश्चैव मुनीन् देवांश्च पीडयेत्
7.e: Then it will afflict his fortress and kingdom, the world along with movable and immovable things, as also the sages and the gods inhabiting the heavenly regions.

7.s: so 'sahāyena mūḍhena lubdhenākṛtabuddhinā na śakyo nyāyato netuṃ saktena viṣayeṣu ca
7.d: सो ऽसहायेन मूढेन लुब्धेनाकृतबुद्धिना न शक्यो न्यायतो नेतुं सक्तेन विषयेषु च
7.e: Punishment cannot be justly administered by one who has no assistant, or who is demented, or who is avaricious, or whose mind is not disciplined, or who is addicted to sensual objects.

7.s: śucinā satyasaṃdhena yathāśāstrānusāriṇā praṇetuṃ śakyate daṇḍaḥ susahāyena dhīmatā
7.d: शुचिना सत्यसंधेन यथाशास्त्रानुसारिणा प्रणेतुं शक्यते दण्डः सुसहायेन धीमता
7.e: Punishment can be administered by one who is pube, who is true to his word, who acts according to the Law, who has good assistants and is wise.

7.s: svarāṣṭre nyāyavṛttaḥ syādbhṛśadaṇḍaśca śatruṣu suhṛtsvajihmaḥ snigdheṣu brāhmaṇeṣu kṣamānvitaḥ
7.d: स्वराष्ट्रे न्यायवृत्तः स्याद्भृशदण्डश्च शत्रुषु सुहृत्स्वजिह्मः स्निग्धेषु ब्राह्मणेषु क्षमान्वितः
7.e: In his own kingdom he shall be of just behaviour, and on his enemies he shall inflict rigorous chastisement; with loved friends he shall be straightforward and towards Brāhmaṇas tolerant.

7.s: evaṃvṛttasya nṛpateḥ śilauñchenāpi jīvataḥ vistīryate yaśo loke tailabindurivāmbhasi
7.d: एवंवृत्तस्य नृपतेः शिलौञ्छेनापि जीवतः विस्तीर्यते यशो लोके तैलबिन्दुरिवाम्भसि
7.e: For the King who behaves thus, even though he may subsist up on gleanings, his fame spreads in the world, like the drops of oil on water.

7.s: atastu viparītasya nṛpaterajitātmanaḥ saṅkṣipyate yaśo loke ghṛtabindurivāmbhasi
7.d: अतस्तु विपरीतस्य नृपतेरजितात्मनः सङ्क्षिप्यते यशो लोके घृतबिन्दुरिवाम्भसि
7.e: But for the King who deviates from it having no control over himself, his fame diminishes in the world, like the drop of clarified butter on water.

7.s: sve sve dharme niviṣṭānāṃ sarveṣāmanupūrvaśaḥ varṇānāmāśramāṇāṃ ca rājā sṛṣṭo 'bhirakṣitā
7.d: स्वे स्वे धर्मे निविष्टानां सर्वेषामनुपूर्वशः वर्णानामाश्रमाणां च राजा सृष्टो ऽभिरक्षिता
7.e: The King has been created the protector of all castes and orders, who, in due order, are intent upon their respective duties.

7.s: tena yadyat sabhṛtyena kartavyaṃ rakṣatā prajāḥ tat tadvo 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ
7.d: तेन यद्यत् सभृत्येन कर्तव्यं रक्षता प्रजाः तत् तद्वो ऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावदनुपूर्वशः
7.e: Whatever should be done by him and his servants, for the protecting of his people, all that I am going to explain to you precisely and in due order

7.s: brāhmaṇān paryupāsīta prātarutthāya pārthivaḥ traividyavṛddhān viduṣastiṣṭhet teṣāṃ ca śāsane
7.d: ब्राह्मणान् पर्युपासीत प्रातरुत्थाय पार्थिवः त्रैविद्यवृद्धान् विदुषस्तिष्ठेत् तेषां च शासने
7.e: After rising in the morning, the King shall wait upon the Brāhmaṇas, who are accomplished students of the Threefold Science and learned; and shall follow their advice.

7.s: vṛddhāṃśca nityaṃ seveta viprān vedavidaḥ śucīn vṛddhasevī hi satataṃ rakṣobhirapi pūjyate
7.d: वृद्धांश्च नित्यं सेवेत विप्रान् वेदविदः शुचीन् वृद्धसेवी हि सततं रक्षोभिरपि पूज्यते
7.e: Every day he shall wait upon elderly persons, Brāhmaṇas, pure and learned in the Vedas; he who constantly waits upon elderly persons is honoured even by Rākṣasas.

7.s: tebhyo 'dhigacchedvinayaṃ vinītātmā 'pi nityaśaḥ vinītātmā hi nṛpatirna vinaśyati karhi cit
7.d: तेभ्यो ऽधिगच्छेद्विनयं विनीतात्मा ऽपि नित्यशः विनीतात्मा हि नृपतिर्न विनश्यति कर्हि चित्
7.e: Though his mind be already disciplined, he shall always learn discipline from them; the King with a disciplined mind never perishes.

7.s: bahavo 'vinayātnaṣṭā rājānaḥ saparicchadāḥ saparigrahāḥ vanasthā api rājyāni vinayāt pratipedire
7.d: बहवो ऽविनयात्नष्टा राजानः सपरिच्छदाः सपरिग्रहाः वनस्था अपि राज्यानि विनयात् प्रतिपेदिरे
7.e: Many Kings, along with their belongings, have perished through want of discipline; while, on account of discipline, many, even though living in forests, have obtained Kingdoms.

7.s: veno vinaṣṭo 'vinayātnahuṣaścaiva pārthivaḥ sudāḥ paijavanaścaiva sumukho nimireva ca
7.d: वेनो विनष्टो ऽविनयात्नहुषश्चैव पार्थिवः सुदाः पैजवनश्चैव सुमुखो निमिरेव च
7.e: It was through want of discipline that Vena perished, as also King Nahuṣa, Sudās, Paijavana, Sumukha and Nimi.

7.s: pṛthustu vinayādrājyaṃ prāptavān manureva ca kuberaśca dhanaiśvaryaṃ brāhmaṇyaṃ caiva gādhijaḥ
7.d: पृथुस्तु विनयाद्राज्यं प्राप्तवान् मनुरेव च कुबेरश्च धनैश्वर्यं ब्राह्मण्यं चैव गाधिजः
7.e: But through discipline Pṛthu and Manu obtained kingdoms, Kubera obtained the lordship of wealth and the son of Gādhi attained Brāhmaṇahood.

7.s: traividyebhyastrayīṃ vidyāṃ daṇḍanītiṃ ca śāśvatīm trayīṃ vidyāt ānvīkṣikīṃ cātmavidyāṃ vārtārambhāṃśca lokataḥ
7.d: त्रैविद्येभ्यस्त्रयीं विद्यां दण्डनीतिं च शाश्वतीम् त्रयीं विद्यात् आन्वीक्षिकीं चात्मविद्यां वार्तारम्भांश्च लोकतः
7.e: From persons learned in the Threefold Science he shall learn the Triad; as also the ancient Science of Government, the Science of Reasoning and the Science of the Soul; and also the art of commerce from experts

7.s: indriyāṇāṃ jaye yogaṃ samātiṣṭheddivāniśam jitaindriyo hi śaknoti vaśe sthāpayituṃ prajāḥ
7.d: इन्द्रियाणां जये योगं समातिष्ठेद्दिवानिशम् जितैन्द्रियो हि शक्नोति वशे स्थापयितुं प्रजाः
7.e: Day and night he shall put forth an effort to subdue his senses; because he whose senses are subjugated is capable of keeping his subjects under control.

7.s: daśa kāmasamutthāni tathā 'ṣṭau krodhajāni ca vyasanāni dur 'ntāni prayatnena vivarjayet
7.d: दश कामसमुत्थानि तथा ऽष्टौ क्रोधजानि च व्यसनानि दुर् ऽन्तानि प्रयत्नेन विवर्जयेत्
7.e: He shall shun the ten ruinous vices springing from love of plea sure, as also the eight arising from anger.

7.s: kāmajeṣu prasakto hi vyasaneṣu mahīpatiḥ viyujyate 'rthadharmābhyāṃ krodhajeṣvātmanaiva tu
7.d: कामजेषु प्रसक्तो हि व्यसनेषु महीपतिः वियुज्यते ऽर्थधर्माभ्यां क्रोधजेष्वात्मनैव तु
7.e: The king who is addicted to vices springing from the love of pleasure becomes deprived of wealth and virtue; while he who is addicted to those proceeding from anger becomes bereft of his very soul.

7.s: mṛgayā 'kṣo divāsvapnaḥ parivādaḥ striyo madaḥ tauryatrikaṃ vṛthāṭyā ca kāmajo daśako gaṇaḥ
7.d: मृगया ऽक्षो दिवास्वप्नः परिवादः स्त्रियो मदः तौर्यत्रिकं वृथाट्या च कामजो दशको गणः
7.e: Hunting, dice, sleeping during the day, censoriousness, women, intoxication, musical triad and listless wandering constitute the ten-fold set arising from the love of pleasure.

7.s: paiśunyaṃ sāhasaṃ droha īrṣyā 'sūyā 'rthadūṣaṇam vāgdaṇḍajaṃ ca pāruṣyaṃ krodhajo 'pi gaṇo 'ṣṭakaḥ
7.d: पैशुन्यं साहसं द्रोह ईर्ष्या ऽसूया ऽर्थदूषणम् वाग्दण्डजं च पारुष्यं क्रोधजो ऽपि गणो ऽष्टकः
7.e: Tale-bearing, Treachery, Envy, Slandering, Misappropriation of property, Cruelty of speech and of Assault;—these constitute the eightfold set born of Anger.

7.s: dvayorapyetayormūlaṃ yaṃ sarve kavayo viduḥ taṃ yatnena jayetlobhaṃ tajjāvetāvubhau gaṇau
7.d: द्वयोरप्येतयोर्मूलं यं सर्वे कवयो विदुः तं यत्नेन जयेत्लोभं तज्जावेतावुभौ गणौ
7.e: With great effort he shall subdue that Greediness which all wise men regard as the root of both these; both these sets arise out of that.

7.s: pānamakṣāḥ striyaścaiva mṛgayā ca yathākramam etat kaṣṭatamaṃ vidyātcatuṣkaṃ kāmaje gaṇe
7.d: पानमक्षाः स्त्रियश्चैव मृगया च यथाक्रमम् एतत् कष्टतमं विद्यात्चतुष्कं कामजे गणे
7.e: In the set arising from love of pleasure,—drinking, dice, women and hunting are to be regarded as the four most pernicious, in the order in which they are named.

7.s: daṇḍasya pātanaṃ caiva vākpāruṣyārthadūṣaṇe krodhaje 'pi gaṇe vidyāt kaṣṭametat trikaṃ sadā
7.d: दण्डस्य पातनं चैव वाक्पारुष्यार्थदूषणे क्रोधजे ऽपि गणे विद्यात् कष्टमेतत् त्रिकं सदा
7.e: In the set born of Anger,—Assault, Cruelty of speech and Misappropriation of property,—are to be regarded as the three most pernicious.

7.s: saptakasyāsya vargasya sarvatraivānuṣaṅgiṇaḥ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ gurutaraṃ vidyādvyasanamātmavān
7.d: सप्तकस्यास्य वर्गस्य सर्वत्रैवानुषङ्गिणः पूर्वं पूर्वं गुरुतरं विद्याद्व्यसनमात्मवान्
7.e: The self-disciplined man should know that in this set of seven which spreads everywhere, each preceding vice is more serious than the succeeding one.

7.s: vyasanasya ca mṛtyośca vyasanaṃ kaṣṭamucyate vyasanyadho 'dho vrajati svaryātyavyasanī mṛtaḥ
7.d: व्यसनस्य च मृत्योश्च व्यसनं कष्टमुच्यते व्यसन्यधो ऽधो व्रजति स्वर्यात्यव्यसनी मृतः
7.e: Between Vice & Death, Vice is said to be more harmful; the vicious man sinks down and down; but the dead man, without vices, ascends to heaven.

7.s: maulāṃśāstravidaḥ śūrānlabdhalakṣān kulaudbhavān kulaudgatān sacivān sapta cāṣṭau vā prakurvīta parīkṣitān kurvīta suparīkṣitān
7.d: मौलांशास्त्रविदः शूरान्लब्धलक्षान् कुलौद्भवान् कुलौद्गतान् सचिवान् सप्त चाष्टौ वा प्रकुर्वीत परीक्षितान् कुर्वीत सुपरीक्षितान्
7.e: He shall appoint seven or eight ministers, with respectable status, versed in law, of heroic temperament, experienced in business, born of noble families, and thoroughly tested.

7.s: api yat sukaraṃ karma tadapyekena duṣkaram viśeṣato 'sahāyena kiṃ tu rājyaṃ mahaudayam kiṃ nu
7.d: अपि यत् सुकरं कर्म तदप्येकेन दुष्करम् विशेषतो ऽसहायेन किं तु राज्यं महौदयम् किं नु
7.e: Even an undertaking that is easy is difficult to be accomplished by a single man, specially by one who has no assistant; how much more so is the work of the king, which involves great issues!

7.s: taiḥ sārdhaṃ cintayennityaṃ sāmānyaṃ saṃdhivigraham sthānaṃ samudayaṃ guptiṃ labdhapraśamanāni ca
7.d: तैः सार्धं चिन्तयेन्नित्यं सामान्यं संधिविग्रहम् स्थानं समुदयं गुप्तिं लब्धप्रशमनानि च
7.e: With these he shall always discuss all ordinary business relating to peace and war, as also the ‘state’, the sources of revenue, the means of protection, and the consolidation of what has been acquired.

7.s: teṣāṃ svaṃ svamabhiprāyamupalabhya pṛthak pṛthak samastānāṃ ca kāryeṣu vidadhyāddhitamātmanaḥ
7.d: तेषां स्वं स्वमभिप्रायमुपलभ्य पृथक् पृथक् समस्तानां च कार्येषु विदध्याद्धितमात्मनः
7.e: Having ascertained the opinion of each of the ministers individually and also collectively, he shall, in his affairs, do what is beneficial to himself.

7.s: sarveṣāṃ tu viśiṣṭena brāhmaṇena vipaścitā mantrayet paramaṃ mantraṃ rājā ṣāḍguṇyasaṃyutam
7.d: सर्वेषां तु विशिष्टेन ब्राह्मणेन विपश्चिता मन्त्रयेत् परमं मन्त्रं राजा षाड्गुण्यसंयुतम्
7.e: With the learned Brāhmaṇa, however, who is the most distinguished of them all, the king shall discuss the highest secrets pertaining to the six-fold state-craft.

7.s: nityaṃ tasmin samāśvastaḥ sarvakāryāṇi niḥkṣipet nikṣipet tena sārdhaṃ viniścitya tataḥ karma samārabhet
7.d: नित्यं तस्मिन् समाश्वस्तः सर्वकार्याणि निःक्षिपेत् निक्षिपेत् तेन सार्धं विनिश्चित्य ततः कर्म समारभेत्
7.e: He shall always, in full confidence, entrust all business to him; and having, in consultation with him, formed his resolution, he shall do what has to be done.

7.s: anyānapi prakurvīta śucīn prājñānavasthitān samyagarthasamāhartr̥̄namātyān suparīkṣitān
7.d: अन्यानपि प्रकुर्वीत शुचीन् प्राज्ञानवस्थितान् सम्यगर्थसमाहर्त्र्̥̄नमात्यान् सुपरीक्षितान्
7.e: He shall also appoint other ministers, who are pure, wise, firm, experts in collecting revenue and thoroughly tested.

7.s: nirvartetāsya yāvadbhiritikartavyatā nṛbhiḥ tāvato 'tandritān dakṣān prakurvīta vicakṣaṇān
7.d: निर्वर्तेतास्य यावद्भिरितिकर्तव्यता नृभिः तावतो ऽतन्द्रितान् दक्षान् प्रकुर्वीत विचक्षणान्
7.e: He shall appoint as many industrious, clever and skilful men as may be required for the accomplishment of his business.

7.s: teṣāmarthe niyuñjīta śūrān dakṣān kulaudgatān śucīnākarakarmānte bhīrūnantarniveśane
7.d: तेषामर्थे नियुञ्जीत शूरान् दक्षान् कुलौद्गतान् शुचीनाकरकर्मान्ते भीरूनन्तर्निवेशने
7.e: From among them he shall employ the brave, the expert, the high-born and the honest ones in work relating to finance,—such as mines and stores—and timid ones in the interior of the palace.

7.s: dūtaṃ caiva prakurvīta sarvaśāstraviśāradam iṅgitākāraceṣṭajñaṃ śuciṃ dakṣaṃ kulaudgatam
7.d: दूतं चैव प्रकुर्वीत सर्वशास्त्रविशारदम् इङ्गिताकारचेष्टज्ञं शुचिं दक्षं कुलौद्गतम्
7.e: As ambassador he shall appoint one who is well versed in all the sciences, who understands hints, expressions and gestures, who is honest, expert and born of a noble family.

7.s: anuraktaḥ śucirdakṣaḥ smṛtimān deśakālavit vapuṣmān vītabhīrvāgmī dūto rājñaḥ praśasyate
7.d: अनुरक्तः शुचिर्दक्षः स्मृतिमान् देशकालवित् वपुष्मान् वीतभीर्वाग्मी दूतो राज्ञः प्रशस्यते
7.e: That royal ambassador is commended who is loyal, honest, clever, possessed of good memory, conversant with place and time, handsome of body, fearless and eloquent.

7.s: amātye daṇḍa āyatto daṇḍe vainayikī kriyā nṛpatau kośarāṣṭre ca dūte saṃdhiviparyayau
7.d: अमात्ये दण्ड आयत्तो दण्डे वैनयिकी क्रिया नृपतौ कोशराष्ट्रे च दूते संधिविपर्ययौ
7.e: The army is dependent upon the minister (of war); on the army rests the act of ruling; the treasury and the realm are dependent upon the king, and upon the ambassador depend peace and its opposite.

7.s: dūta eva hi saṃdhatte bhinattyeva ca saṃhatān dūtastat kurute karma bhidyante yena mānavaḥ
7.d: दूत एव हि संधत्ते भिनत्त्येव च संहतान् दूतस्तत् कुरुते कर्म भिद्यन्ते येन मानवः
7.e: For it is the Ambassador alone who brings together allies and also alienates them; the Ambassador transacts that business by which people become disunited

7.s: sa vidyādasya kṛtyeṣu nirgūḍhaiṅgitaceṣṭitaiḥ ākāramiṅgitaṃ ceṣṭāṃ bhṛtyeṣu ca cikīrṣitam
7.d: स विद्यादस्य कृत्येषु निर्गूढैङ्गितचेष्टितैः आकारमिङ्गितं चेष्टां भृत्येषु च चिकीर्षितम्
7.e: He shall take up residence in a country which is open, fully supplied with grains, inhabited almost entirely by men of gentle birth, free from diseases, pleasant, where the vassals are obedient and where living is easily found.

7.s: buddhvā ca sarvaṃ tattvena pararājacikīrṣitam tathā prayatnamātiṣṭhedyathā 'tmānaṃ na pīḍayet
7.d: बुद्ध्वा च सर्वं तत्त्वेन परराजचिकीर्षितम् तथा प्रयत्नमातिष्ठेद्यथा ऽत्मानं न पीडयेत्
7.e: He shall take up residence in a country which is open, fully supplied with grains, inhabited almost entirely by men of gentle birth, free from diseases, pleasant, where the vassals are obedient and where living is easily found.

7.s: jāṅgalaṃ sasyasaṃpannamāryaprāyamanāvilam ramyamānatasāmantaṃ svājīvyaṃ deśamāvaset
7.d: जाङ्गलं सस्यसंपन्नमार्यप्रायमनाविलम् रम्यमानतसामन्तं स्वाजीव्यं देशमावसेत्
7.e: He shall take up residence in a country which is open, fully supplied with grains, inhabited almost entirely by men of gentle birth, free from diseases, pleasant, where the vassals are obedient and where living is easily found.

7.s: dhanvadurgaṃ mahīdurgamabdurgaṃ vārkṣameva vā nṛdurgaṃ giridurgaṃ vā samāśritya vaset puram
7.d: धन्वदुर्गं महीदुर्गमब्दुर्गं वार्क्षमेव वा नृदुर्गं गिरिदुर्गं वा समाश्रित्य वसेत् पुरम्
7.e: He shall live in a city, taking up his residence either in a ‘bow-fort’, or in an ‘earthen fort’, or in an ‘aquatic fort,’ or in an ‘arborial fort,’ or in a ‘human fort,’ or in a ‘hilly fort.’

7.s: sarveṇa tu prayatnena giridurgaṃ samāśrayet eṣāṃ hi bāhuguṇyena giridurgaṃ viśiṣyate
7.d: सर्वेण तु प्रयत्नेन गिरिदुर्गं समाश्रयेत् एषां हि बाहुगुण्येन गिरिदुर्गं विशिष्यते
7.e: The first three of these are inhabited by deer, by animals living underground and by aquatic animals, and the last three by monkeys, men and gods.

7.s: triṇyādyānyāśritāstveṣāṃ mṛgagartāśrayāpcarāḥ trīṇyuttarāṇi kramaśaḥ plavaṅgamanarāmarāḥ
7.d: त्रिण्याद्यान्याश्रितास्त्वेषां मृगगर्ताश्रयाप्चराः त्रीण्युत्तराणि क्रमशः प्लवङ्गमनरामराः
7.e: The first three of these are inhabited by deer, by animals living underground and by aquatic animals, and the last three by monkeys, men and gods.

7.s: yathā durgāśritānetānnaupahiṃsanti śatravaḥ tathā 'rayo na hiṃsanti nṛpaṃ durgasamāśritam
7.d: यथा दुर्गाश्रितानेतान्नौपहिंसन्ति शत्रवः तथा ऽरयो न हिंसन्ति नृपं दुर्गसमाश्रितम्
7.e: Just as enemies do not hurt these beings sheltered in their fortresses, so also the enemies do not injure the king protected by his fort.

7.s: ekaḥ śataṃ yodhayati prākārastho dhanurdharaḥ śataṃ daśasahasrāṇi tasmāddurgaṃ vidhīyate
7.d: एकः शतं योधयति प्राकारस्थो धनुर्धरः शतं दशसहस्राणि तस्माद्दुर्गं विधीयते
7.e: A single bow-man, standing on a rampart, can fight against a hundred; and a hundred can fight against ten thousand; it is for the season that fortification has been enjoined.

7.s: tat syādāyudhasaṃpannaṃ dhanadhānyena vāhanaiḥ brāhmaṇaiḥ śilpibhiryantrairyavasenaudakena ca
7.d: तत् स्यादायुधसंपन्नं धनधान्येन वाहनैः ब्राह्मणैः शिल्पिभिर्यन्त्रैर्यवसेनौदकेन च
7.e: It should be folly equipped with weapons, with money and grain, with conveyances, with Brāhmaṇas, with artisans, with machines, with fodder and with water,

7.s: tasya madhye suparyāptaṃ kārayedgṛhamātmanaḥ guptaṃ sarvaṛtukaṃ śubhraṃ jalavṛkṣasamanvitam
7.d: तस्य मध्ये सुपर्याप्तं कारयेद्गृहमात्मनः गुप्तं सर्वऋतुकं शुभ्रं जलवृक्षसमन्वितम्
7.e: In the centre of the fort, he shall get built for himsrlf a spacious palace, well guarded, equipped with all seasons, resplendent, and supplied with water and trees.

7.s: tadadhyāsyaudvahedbhāryāṃ savarṇāṃ lakṣaṇānvitām kule mahati saṃbhūtāṃ hṛdyāṃ rūpaguṇānvītām
7.d: तदध्यास्यौद्वहेद्भार्यां सवर्णां लक्षणान्विताम् कुले महति संभूतां हृद्यां रूपगुणान्वीताम्
7.e: Having occupied it, he shall wed a wife of the same caste as himself, who is equipped with auspicious signs, born in a noble family, charming, and possessed of beauty and excellent qualities.

7.s: purohitaṃ ca kurvīta vṛṇuyādeva caṛtvijaḥ te 'sya gṛhyāṇi karmāṇi kuryurvaitānikāni ca
7.d: पुरोहितं च कुर्वीत वृणुयादेव चऋत्विजः ते ऽस्य गृह्याणि कर्माणि कुर्युर्वैतानिकानि च
7.e: He shall appoint a household priest and select officiating priests; they shall perform his domestic rites, as also the fire-sacrifices.

7.s: yajeta rājā kratubhirvividhairāptadakṣiṇaiḥ dharmārthaṃ caiva viprebhyo dadyādbhogān dhanāni ca
7.d: यजेत राजा क्रतुभिर्विविधैराप्तदक्षिणैः धर्मार्थं चैव विप्रेभ्यो दद्याद्भोगान् धनानि च
7.e: The King shall offer various sacrifices at which large sacrificial fees are paid; and for the purpose of acquiring merit, he shall provide for Brāhmaṇas luxuries and riches.

7.s: sāṃvatsarikamāptaiśca rāṣṭrādāhārayedbalim syāccāmnāyaparo loke varteta pitṛvatnṛṣu
7.d: सांवत्सरिकमाप्तैश्च राष्ट्रादाहारयेद्बलिम् स्याच्चाम्नायपरो लोके वर्तेत पितृवत्नृषु
7.e: He should cause the yearly revenue to be collectbd by trusted men. In his business he shall stick to the scriptures; and towards the people he shall behave like a father.

7.s: adhyakṣān vividhān kuryāt tatra tatra vipaścitaḥ te 'sya sarvāṇyavekṣerannṛṇāṃ kāryāṇi kurvatām
7.d: अध्यक्षान् विविधान् कुर्यात् तत्र तत्र विपश्चितः ते ऽस्य सर्वाण्यवेक्षेरन्नृणां कार्याणि कुर्वताम्
7.e: Here and there he shall appoint several proficient inspectors; they shall supervise all the acts of men working for him.

7.s: āvṛttānāṃ gurukulādviprāṇāṃ pūjako bhavet nṛpāṇāmakṣayo hyeṣa nidhirbrāhmo 'bhidhīyate
7.d: आवृत्तानां गुरुकुलाद्विप्राणां पूजको भवेत् नृपाणामक्षयो ह्येष निधिर्ब्राह्मो ऽभिधीयते
7.e: He shall do honour to those Brāhmaṇas who have returned from their teacher’s house; for kings, this is interminable; and has been called ‘Brahmic treasure’.

7.s: na taṃ stenā na cāmitrā haranti na ca naśyati tasmādrājñā nidhātavyo brāhmaṇeṣvakṣayo nidhiḥ
7.d: न तं स्तेना न चामित्रा हरन्ति न च नश्यति तस्माद्राज्ञा निधातव्यो ब्राह्मणेष्वक्षयो निधिः
7.e: Neither thieves, nor enemies take it away; nor does it perish; hence this inexhaustible treasure shall be deposited by the king with the Brāhmaṇas.

7.s: na skandate na vyathate na vinaśyati karhi cit na skandati na cyavate variṣṭhamagnihotrebhyo brāhmaṇasya mukhe hutam
7.d: न स्कन्दते न व्यथते न विनश्यति कर्हि चित् न स्कन्दति न च्यवते वरिष्ठमग्निहोत्रेभ्यो ब्राह्मणस्य मुखे हुतम्
7.e: What is offered into the mouth of the Brāhmaṇa, which is neither spilt nor spoilt, nor wasted, is far superior to the Fire-offerings.

7.s: samamabrāhmaṇe dānaṃ dviguṇaṃ brāhmaṇabruve prādhīte śatasāhasramanantaṃ vedapārage ācārye śatasāhasram] sahasraguṇamācārye
7.d: सममब्राह्मणे दानं द्विगुणं ब्राह्मणब्रुवे प्राधीते शतसाहस्रमनन्तं वेदपारगे आचार्ये शतसाहस्रम्] सहस्रगुणमाचार्ये
7.e: The gift to a non-Brāhmaṇa is equable; that to a nominal Brāhmaṇa is twofold; that to the Teacher, a hundred-thousand-fold and that to a person thoroughly learned in the Veda, endless.

7.s: pātrasya hi viśeṣeṇa śraddadhānatayaiva ca alpaṃ vā bahu vā pretya dānasya phalamaśnute [deśakālavidhānena dravyaṃ śraddhāsamanvitam ] [pātre pradīyate yat tu taddharmasya prasādhanam ]
7.d: पात्रस्य हि विशेषेण श्रद्दधानतयैव च अल्पं वा बहु वा प्रेत्य दानस्य फलमश्नुते [देशकालविधानेन द्रव्यं श्रद्धासमन्वितम् ] [पात्रे प्रदीयते यत् तु तद्धर्मस्य प्रसाधनम् ]
7.e: For one obtains, after death, the reward, small or great, of his gifts,—according to the peculiar character of the recipient, and also according to his own faith.

7.s: samauttamādhamai rājā tvāhūtaḥ pālayan prajāḥ na nivarteta saṅgrāmāt kṣātraṃ dharmamanusmaran
7.d: समौत्तमाधमै राजा त्वाहूतः पालयन् प्रजाः न निवर्तेत सङ्ग्रामात् क्षात्रं धर्ममनुस्मरन्
7.e: While protecting his people, if the king is challenged by enemies, either equal in strength, or stronger, or weaker, he shall not shrink from battle, bearing in mind the duty of the kṣatriya.

7.s: saṅgrāmeṣvanivartitvaṃ prajānāṃ caiva pālanam śuśrūṣā brāhmaṇānāṃ ca rājñāṃ śreyaskaraṃ param
7.d: सङ्ग्रामेष्वनिवर्तित्वं प्रजानां चैव पालनम् शुश्रूषा ब्राह्मणानां च राज्ञां श्रेयस्करं परम्
7.e: Not shrinking from battle, protecting the people, and attending on brāhmaṇas,—is the best means of securing happiness for kings.

7.s: āhaveṣu mitho 'nyonyaṃ jighāṃsanto mahīkṣitaḥ yudhyamānāḥ paraṃ śaktyā svargaṃ yāntyaparālgmukhāḥ
7.d: आहवेषु मिथो ऽन्योन्यं जिघांसन्तो महीक्षितः युध्यमानाः परं शक्त्या स्वर्गं यान्त्यपराल्ग्मुखाः
7.e: Kings, seeking to slay each other in battle and fighting with gheat energy, without turning back, proceed to heaven.

7.s: na kūṭairāyudhairhanyādyudhyamāno raṇe ripūn na karṇibhirnāpi digdhairnāgnijvalitatejanaiḥ
7.d: न कूटैरायुधैर्हन्याद्युध्यमानो रणे रिपून् न कर्णिभिर्नापि दिग्धैर्नाग्निज्वलिततेजनैः
7.e: While fighting his enemies in battle, he shall hot strike with concealed weapons; nor with arrows that are poisoned, or barbed, or with flaming shafts.

7.s: na ca hanyāt sthalārūḍhaṃ na klībaṃ na kṛtāñjalim na muktakeśaṃ nāsīnaṃ na tavāsmīti vādinam
7.d: न च हन्यात् स्थलारूढं न क्लीबं न कृताञ्जलिम् न मुक्तकेशं नासीनं न तवास्मीति वादिनम्
7.e: He shall hot strike one who is standing on the ground, nor one who is a eunuch, nor the supp?icant (supplicant?) with joined palms, nor one with loosened hair, nor one who is seated, nor one who says ‘i am yours;’

7.s: na suptaṃ na visaṃnāhaṃ na nagnaṃ na nirāyudham nāyudhyamānaṃ paśyantaṃ na pareṇa samāgatam
7.d: न सुप्तं न विसंनाहं न नग्नं न निरायुधम् नायुध्यमानं पश्यन्तं न परेण समागतम्
7.e: Nor one who is sleeping, nor him who is without his armour, nor one who is naked, nor one deprived of his weapons, nor one who is only looking on and not fighting, nor one who is engaged in fighting with ahother person;

7.s: nāyudhavyasanaprāptaṃ nārtaṃ nātiparikṣatam na bhītaṃ na parāvṛttaṃ satāṃ dharmamanusmaran
7.d: नायुधव्यसनप्राप्तं नार्तं नातिपरिक्षतम् न भीतं न परावृत्तं सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन्
7.e: Nor one who has fallen in difficulties regarding weapons; nor one in distress, nor one severely wounded, nor one who is frightened, nor one who has turned back;—the king remembering the duties of honourable men.

7.s: yastu bhītaḥ parāvṛttaḥ saṅgrāme hanyate paraiḥ bharturyadduṣkṛtaṃ kiṃ cit tat sarvaṃ pratipadyate
7.d: यस्तु भीतः परावृत्तः सङ्ग्रामे हन्यते परैः भर्तुर्यद्दुष्कृतं किं चित् तत् सर्वं प्रतिपद्यते
7.e: But the Kṣatriya who, frightened and turned back, is slain by the enemies, takes upon himself all the sin that there may be of his master.

7.s: yatcāsya sukṛtaṃ kiṃ cidamutrārthamupārjitam bhartā tat sarvamādatte parāvṛttahatasya tu
7.d: यत्चास्य सुकृतं किं चिदमुत्रार्थमुपार्जितम् भर्ता तत् सर्वमादत्ते परावृत्तहतस्य तु
7.e: And whatever merit the man slain after having turned back may have earned for the next world,—all that his master takes off.

7.s: rathāśvaṃ hastinaṃ chatraṃ dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ paśūn striyaḥ sarvadravyāṇi kupyaṃ ca yo yaj jayati tasya tat
7.d: रथाश्वं हस्तिनं छत्रं धनं धान्यं पशून् स्त्रियः सर्वद्रव्याणि कुप्यं च यो यज् जयति तस्य तत्
7.e: Chariots and horses, elephants, umbrellas, wealth, grains, animals, women, all goods and baser metals belong to him who wins them.

7.s: rājñaśca dadyuruddhāramityeṣā vaidikī śrutiḥ rājñā ca sarvayodhebhyo dātavyamapṛthagjitam
7.d: राज्ञश्च दद्युरुद्धारमित्येषा वैदिकी श्रुतिः राज्ञा च सर्वयोधेभ्यो दातव्यमपृथग्जितम्
7.e: They shall present to the King the choice portion,—such is the Vedic declaration. what has not been won individually shall be distributed by the king among all the soldiers.

7.s: eṣo 'nupaskṛtaḥ prokto yodhadharmaḥ sanātanaḥ asmāddharmānna cyaveta kṣatriyo ghnan raṇe ripūn
7.d: एषो ऽनुपस्कृतः प्रोक्तो योधधर्मः सनातनः अस्माद्धर्मान्न च्यवेत क्षत्रियो घ्नन् रणे रिपून्
7.e: Thus has been declared the blameless eternal law of warriors; the Kṣatriya, striking his enemies in battle, shall not deviate from this law.

7.s: alabdhaṃ caiva lipseta labdhaṃ rakṣet prayatnataḥ rakṣitaṃ vardhayeccaiva vṛddhaṃ pātreṣu nikṣipet
7.d: अलब्धं चैव लिप्सेत लब्धं रक्षेत् प्रयत्नतः रक्षितं वर्धयेच्चैव वृद्धं पात्रेषु निक्षिपेत्
7.e: He shall strive to obtain what has not been obtained; what he has gained he shall preserve with care; he shall augment what has been preserved and what has been augmented he shall bestow upon suitable recipients

7.s: etaccaturvidhaṃ vidyāt puruṣārthaprayojanam asya nityamanuṣṭhānaṃ samyak kuryādatandritaḥ
7.d: एतच्चतुर्विधं विद्यात् पुरुषार्थप्रयोजनम् अस्य नित्यमनुष्ठानं सम्यक् कुर्यादतन्द्रितः
7.e: What has not been gained he shall seek to obtain by means of force; what has been gained he shall save with careful attention; what has been saved he shall augment by adding to it; and what has been augmented he shall bestow on suitable recipients.

7.s: alabdhamiccheddaṇḍena labdhaṃ rakṣedavekṣayā rakṣitaṃ vardhayedvṛddhyā vṛddhaṃ pātreṣu nikṣipet
7.d: अलब्धमिच्छेद्दण्डेन लब्धं रक्षेदवेक्षया रक्षितं वर्धयेद्वृद्ध्या वृद्धं पात्रेषु निक्षिपेत्
7.e: What has not been gained he shall seek to obtain by means of force; what has been gained he shall save with careful attention; what has been saved he shall augment by adding to it; and what has been augmented he shall bestow on suitable recipients.

7.s: nityamudyatadaṇḍaḥ syānnityaṃ vivṛtapauruṣaḥ nityaṃ saṃvṛtasaṃvāryo nityaṃ chidrānusāryareḥ
7.d: नित्यमुद्यतदण्डः स्यान्नित्यं विवृतपौरुषः नित्यं संवृतसंवार्यो नित्यं छिद्रानुसार्यरेः
7.e: He shall have his force always operative; his manliness always displayed, his secrets constantly concealed, ever following up the weak points of his enemy.

7.s: nityamudyatadaṇḍasya kṛtsnamudvijate jagat tasmāt sarvāṇi bhūtāni daṇḍenaiva prasādhayet
7.d: नित्यमुद्यतदण्डस्य कृत्स्नमुद्विजते जगत् तस्मात् सर्वाणि भूतानि दण्डेनैव प्रसाधयेत्
7.e: Of him who has his force constantly operative, the whole world stands in awe. He shall, therefore, subdue all men by means of force

7.s: amāyayaiva varteta na kathaṃ cana māyayā budhyetāriprayuktāṃ ca māyāṃ nityaṃ susaṃvṛtaḥ
7.d: अमाययैव वर्तेत न कथं चन मायया बुध्येतारिप्रयुक्तां च मायां नित्यं सुसंवृतः
7.e: He shall always behave without guile, and never with guile; well protected himself, he shall fathom the guiles employed by his enemies.

7.s: nāsya chidraṃ paro vidyādvidyātchidraṃ parasya ca gūhet kūrma ivāṅgāni rakṣedvivaramātmanaḥ
7.d: नास्य छिद्रं परो विद्याद्विद्यात्छिद्रं परस्य च गूहेत् कूर्म इवाङ्गानि रक्षेद्विवरमात्मनः
7.e: His enemy should hot know his weak points, but he must know the weak points of the enemy; he should hide the departments (of government) as the tortoise does its limbs; and he should guard his own weak points.

7.s: bakavatcintayedarthān siṃhavatca parākrame vṛkavatcāvalumpeta śaśavatca viniṣpatet
7.d: बकवत्चिन्तयेदर्थान् सिंहवत्च पराक्रमे वृकवत्चावलुम्पेत शशवत्च विनिष्पतेत्
7.e: He shall ponder over his plans like the heron, and like the lion he shall exert his power; he shall snatch like the wolf, and like the hare he shall double in retreat.

7.s: evaṃ vijayamānasya ye 'sya syuḥ paripanthinaḥ tānānayedvaśaṃ sarvān sāmādibhirupakramaiḥ
7.d: एवं विजयमानस्य ये ऽस्य स्युः परिपन्थिनः तानानयेद्वशं सर्वान् सामादिभिरुपक्रमैः
7.e: While he is thus engaged in conquest, if there should be any opponents for him, all these he shall bring under subjugation by means of conciliation and other expedients.

7.s: yadi te tu na tiṣṭheyurupāyaiḥ prathamaistribhiḥ daṇḍenaiva prasahyaitāṃśanakairvaśamānayet
7.d: यदि ते तु न तिष्ठेयुरुपायैः प्रथमैस्त्रिभिः दण्डेनैव प्रसह्यैतांशनकैर्वशमानयेत्
7.e: If however they should not be stopped by means of the first three expedients, then he shall gradually bring them under subjection by force.

7.s: sāmādīnāmupāyānāṃ caturṇāmapi paṇḍitāḥ sāmadaṇḍau praśaṃsanti nityaṃ rāṣṭrābhivṛddhaye
7.d: सामादीनामुपायानां चतुर्णामपि पण्डिताः सामदण्डौ प्रशंसन्ति नित्यं राष्ट्राभिवृद्धये
7.e: For the prosperity of kingdoms the wise ones always recommend Conciliation and Force from among the four expedients, conciliation and the rest.

7.s: yathauddharati nirdātā kakṣaṃ dhānyaṃ ca rakṣati tathā rakṣennṛpo rāṣṭraṃ hanyācca paripanthinaḥ
7.d: यथौद्धरति निर्दाता कक्षं धान्यं च रक्षति तथा रक्षेन्नृपो राष्ट्रं हन्याच्च परिपन्थिनः
7.e: Just as the weeder plucks out the weed and preserves the corn, so shall the King preserve his kingdom and destroy his opponents.

7.s: mohādrājā svarāṣṭraṃ yaḥ karṣayatyanavekṣayā so 'cirādbhraśyate rājyātjīvitātca sabāndhavaḥ
7.d: मोहाद्राजा स्वराष्ट्रं यः कर्षयत्यनवेक्षया सो ऽचिराद्भ्रश्यते राज्यात्जीवितात्च सबान्धवः
7.e: The King, who, through folly, thoughtlessly oppresses his kingdom, becomes, ‘along with his relations’, deprived, without delay, of his kingdom and life.

7.s: śarīrakarṣaṇāt prāṇāḥ kṣīyante prāṇināṃ yathā tathā rājñāmapi prāṇāḥ kṣīyante rāṣṭrakarṣaṇāt
7.d: शरीरकर्षणात् प्राणाः क्षीयन्ते प्राणिनां यथा तथा राज्ञामपि प्राणाः क्षीयन्ते राष्ट्रकर्षणात्
7.e: As the lives of living beings perish by the emasciation of their bodies, so do the lives of Kings perish by oppressing their kingdom

7.s: rāṣṭrasya saṅgrahe nityaṃ vidhānamidamācaret susaṅgṛhītarāṣṭre hi pārthivaḥ sukhamedhate
7.d: राष्ट्रस्य सङ्ग्रहे नित्यं विधानमिदमाचरेत् सुसङ्गृहीतराष्ट्रे हि पार्थिवः सुखमेधते
7.e: In the administration of his kingdom he shall adopt the procedure described below; for the king, whose kingdom is properly administered, prospers easily.

7.s: dvayostrayāṇāṃ pañcānāṃ madhye gulmamadhiṣṭhitam tathā grāmaśatānāṃ ca kuryādrāṣṭrasya saṅgraham
7.d: द्वयोस्त्रयाणां पञ्चानां मध्ये गुल्ममधिष्ठितम् तथा ग्रामशतानां च कुर्याद्राष्ट्रस्य सङ्ग्रहम्
7.e: In the midst of two, three, five or hundred villages he shall appoint an administrator of state supplied with a picket of guards.

7.s: grāmasyādhipatiṃ kuryāddaśagrāmapatiṃ tathā viṃśatīśaṃ śataiśaṃ ca sahasrapatimeva ca
7.d: ग्रामस्याधिपतिं कुर्याद्दशग्रामपतिं तथा विंशतीशं शतैशं च सहस्रपतिमेव च
7.e: He shall appoint the lord of one village, as also the lord of ten villages, the lord of twenty, the lord of hundred and the lord of thousand villages.

7.s: grāmadoṣān samutpannān grāmikaḥ śanakaiḥ svayam śaṃsedgrāmadaśaiśāya daśaiśo viṃśatīśine
7.d: ग्रामदोषान् समुत्पन्नान् ग्रामिकः शनकैः स्वयम् शंसेद्ग्रामदशैशाय दशैशो विंशतीशिने
7.e: Troubles arising in the village, the Village-lord shall himself gently report to the Lord of Ten villages; and the Lord of Ten villages to the Lord of Twenty;—(116)—the Lord of Twenty shall communicate it all to the Lord of Hundred; and the Lord of Hundred himself shall report it to the Lord of Thousand.

7.s: viṃśatīśastu tat sarvaṃ śataiśāya nivedayet śaṃsedgrāmaśataiśastu sahasrapataye svayam
7.d: विंशतीशस्तु तत् सर्वं शतैशाय निवेदयेत् शंसेद्ग्रामशतैशस्तु सहस्रपतये स्वयम्
7.e: Troubles arising in the village, the Village-lord shall himself gently report to the Lord of Ten villages; and the Lord of Ten villages to the Lord of Twenty;—(116)—the Lord of Twenty shall communicate it all to the Lord of Hundred; and the Lord of Hundred himself shall report it to the Lord of Thousand.

7.s: yāni rājapradeyāni pratyahaṃ grāmavāsibhiḥ annapānaindhanādīni grāmikastānyavāpnuyāt
7.d: यानि राजप्रदेयानि प्रत्यहं ग्रामवासिभिः अन्नपानैन्धनादीनि ग्रामिकस्तान्यवाप्नुयात्
7.e: The Village-lord shall get daily those things that ought to be furnished to the King by the villagers, in the shape of food, drink, fuel and the rest.

7.s: daśī kulaṃ tu bhuñjīta viṃśī pañca kulāni ca grāmaṃ grāmaśatādhyakṣaḥ sahasrādhipatiḥ puram
7.d: दशी कुलं तु भुञ्जीत विंशी पञ्च कुलानि च ग्रामं ग्रामशताध्यक्षः सहस्राधिपतिः पुरम्
7.e: The Lord of Ten villages shall enjoy one Kula and the Lord of Twenty villages twenty Kulas; the Lord of Hundred villages one whole village and the Lord of Thousand villages one town.

7.s: teṣāṃ grāmyāṇi kāryāni pṛthakkāryāṇi caiva hi rājño 'nyaḥ sacivaḥ snigdhastāni paśyedatandritaḥ
7.d: तेषां ग्राम्याणि कार्यानि पृथक्कार्याणि चैव हि राज्ञो ऽन्यः सचिवः स्निग्धस्तानि पश्येदतन्द्रितः
7.e: The affairs of these officers pertaining to the villages, as also their individual affairs another minister of the King shall inspect, who is loyal and never idle.

7.s: nagare nagare caikaṃ kuryāt sarvārthacintakam uccaiḥsthānaṃ ghorarūpaṃ nakṣatrāṇāmiva graham
7.d: नगरे नगरे चैकं कुर्यात् सर्वार्थचिन्तकम् उच्चैःस्थानं घोररूपं नक्षत्राणामिव ग्रहम्
7.e: In each town he shall appoint one Superintendent of all works, of high status and awe-inspiring appearance,—he being like a planet among stars.

7.s: sa tānanuparikrāmet sarvāneva sadā svayam teṣāṃ vṛttaṃ pariṇayet samyag rāṣṭreṣu tatcaraiḥ
7.d: स ताननुपरिक्रामेत् सर्वानेव सदा स्वयम् तेषां वृत्तं परिणयेत् सम्यग् राष्ट्रेषु तत्चरैः
7.e: This officer shall always personally supervise in turn all those officers, and thoroughly acquaint himself, through the King’s spies, with their behaviour in their respective jurisdictions.

7.s: rājño hi rakṣādhikṛtāḥ parasvādāyinaḥ śaṭhāḥ bhṛtyā bhavanti prāyeṇa tebhyo rakṣedimāḥ prajāḥ
7.d: राज्ञो हि रक्षाधिकृताः परस्वादायिनः शठाः भृत्या भवन्ति प्रायेण तेभ्यो रक्षेदिमाः प्रजाः
7.e: As the king’s servants, appointed to protect the people, generally become knaves, bent upon seizing the property of others,—he shall protect his people against them

7.s: ye kāryikebhyo 'rthameva gṛhṇīyuḥ pāpacetasaḥ teṣāṃ sarvasvamādāya rājā kuryāt pravāsanam
7.d: ये कार्यिकेभ्यो ऽर्थमेव गृह्णीयुः पापचेतसः तेषां सर्वस्वमादाय राजा कुर्यात् प्रवासनम्
7.e: Those evil-minded persons who would take money from men engaged in business—of these the King shall confiscate the whole property and ordain banishment.

7.s: rājā karmasu yuktānāṃ strīṇāṃ preṣyajanasya ca rājakarmasu pratyahaṃ kalpayedvṛttiṃ sthānaṃ karmānurūpataḥ sthānakarmānurūpataḥ
7.d: राजा कर्मसु युक्तानां स्त्रीणां प्रेष्यजनस्य च राजकर्मसु प्रत्यहं कल्पयेद्वृत्तिं स्थानं कर्मानुरूपतः स्थानकर्मानुरूपतः
7.e: For women employed in the King’s service and also for menial servants, he shall fix daily wages, in proportion to their position and work.

7.s: paṇo deyo 'vakṛṣṭasya ṣaḍutkṛṣṭasya vetanam ṣāṇmāsikastathā 'cchādo dhānyadroṇastu māsikaḥ
7.d: पणो देयो ऽवकृष्टस्य षडुत्कृष्टस्य वेतनम् षाण्मासिकस्तथा ऽच्छादो धान्यद्रोणस्तु मासिकः
7.e: One paṇa shall be paid as the wages of the inferior, and six to the superior servant; as also clothing every sixth month and a Droṇa of grain every month.

7.s: krayavikrayamadhvānaṃ bhaktaṃ ca saparivyayam yogakṣemaṃ ca saṃprekṣya vaṇijo dāpayet karān
7.d: क्रयविक्रयमध्वानं भक्तं च सपरिव्ययम् योगक्षेमं च संप्रेक्ष्य वणिजो दापयेत् करान्
7.e: He should make the traders pay duties, after due investigation of the details of buying and selling, the journey involved, fooding along with its accessories, and the measures of safety.

7.s: yathā phalena yujyeta rājā kartā ca karmaṇām tathā 'vekṣya nṛpo rāṣṭre kalpayet satataṃ karān
7.d: यथा फलेन युज्येत राजा कर्ता च कर्मणाम् तथा ऽवेक्ष्य नृपो राष्ट्रे कल्पयेत् सततं करान्

7.s: yathā 'lpālpamadantyādyaṃ vāryokovatsaṣaṭpadāḥ tathā 'lpālpo grahītavyo rāṣṭrādrājñābdikaḥ karaḥ
7.d: यथा ऽल्पाल्पमदन्त्याद्यं वार्योकोवत्सषट्पदाः तथा ऽल्पाल्पो ग्रहीतव्यो राष्ट्राद्राज्ञाब्दिकः करः
7.e: After due investigation the King shall always levy taxes in his kingdom in such a way that he himself and the man who carries on the business shall both receive their reward.

7.s: pañcāśadbhāga ādeyo rājñā paśuhiraṇyayoḥ dhānyānāmaṣṭamo bhāgaḥ ṣaṣṭho dvādaśa eva vā
7.d: पञ्चाशद्भाग आदेयो राज्ञा पशुहिरण्ययोः धान्यानामष्टमो भागः षष्ठो द्वादश एव वा
7.e: In the case of cattle and gold the fiftieth part shall be taken by the King; and in the case of grains, the eighth, sixth or twelfth part.

7.s: ādadītātha ṣaḍbhāgaṃ drumāṃsamadhusarpiṣām gandhoṣadhirasānāṃ ca puṣpamūlaphalasya ca
7.d: आददीताथ षड्भागं द्रुमांसमधुसर्पिषाम् गन्धोषधिरसानां च पुष्पमूलफलस्य च
7.e: He shall take the sixth part in the case of trees, meat, honey and clarified butter, of perfumes, medicinal herbs and poisons, of flowers, roots and fruits;—(131) of leaves, vegetables and grasses, of skins and cane, of earthenware vessels, and of all things made of stone.

7.s: patraśākatṛṇānāṃ ca carmaṇāṃ vaidalasya ca mṛnmayānāṃ ca bhāṇḍānāṃ sarvasyāśmamayasya ca
7.d: पत्रशाकतृणानां च चर्मणां वैदलस्य च मृन्मयानां च भाण्डानां सर्वस्याश्ममयस्य च
7.e: He shall take the sixth part in the case of trees, meat, honey and clarified butter, of perfumes, medicinal herbs and poisons, of flowers, roots and fruits;—(131) of leaves, vegetables and grasses, of skins and cane, of earthenware vessels, and of all things made of stone.

7.s: mriyamāṇo 'pyādadīta na rājā śrotriyāt karam na ca kṣudhā 'sya saṃsīdetśrotriyo viṣaye vasan
7.d: म्रियमाणो ऽप्याददीत न राजा श्रोत्रियात् करम् न च क्षुधा ऽस्य संसीदेत्श्रोत्रियो विषये वसन्
7.e: Even though dying, the King shall not levy a tax on the Śrotriya; and no Śrotriya living in his kingdom shall suffer from hunger.

7.s: yasya rājñastu viṣaye śrotriyaḥ sīdati kṣudhā tasyāpi tat kṣudhā rāṣṭramacirenaiva sīdati
7.d: यस्य राज्ञस्तु विषये श्रोत्रियः सीदति क्षुधा तस्यापि तत् क्षुधा राष्ट्रमचिरेनैव सीदति
7.e: The kingdom of that King in whose realm the Śrotriya suffers from hunger, shall, ere long, pine with hunger.

7.s: śrutavṛtte viditvā 'sya vṛttiṃ dharmyāṃ prakalpayet saṃrakṣet sarvataścainaṃ pitā putramivaurasam
7.d: श्रुतवृत्ते विदित्वा ऽस्य वृत्तिं धर्म्यां प्रकल्पयेत् संरक्षेत् सर्वतश्चैनं पिता पुत्रमिवौरसम्
7.e: Having ascertained his learning and character, he shall provide for him a fair living; and he shall protect him against all things, even as the father protects his lawful son.

7.s: saṃrakṣyamāṇo rājñā yaṃ kurute dharmamanvaham rājñā 'yaṃ tenāyurvardhate rājño draviṇaṃ rāṣṭrameva ca
7.d: संरक्ष्यमाणो राज्ञा यं कुरुते धर्ममन्वहम् राज्ञा ऽयं तेनायुर्वर्धते राज्ञो द्रविणं राष्ट्रमेव च
7.e: Protected by the King he performs meritorious acts day after dat; and by that the King’s life, wealth and kingdom become augmented.

7.s: yat kiṃ cidapi varṣasya dāpayet karasaṃjñitam vyavahāreṇa jīvantaṃ rājā rāṣṭre pṛthagjanam
7.d: यत् किं चिदपि वर्षस्य दापयेत् करसंज्ञितम् व्यवहारेण जीवन्तं राजा राष्ट्रे पृथग्जनम्
7.e: The King shall make the other people living by business p ay during the year something under the name of “tax”.

7.s: kārukāṃśilpinaścaiva śūdrāṃḥ cātmaupajīvinaḥ ekaikaṃ kārayet karma māsi māsi mahīpatiḥ
7.d: कारुकांशिल्पिनश्चैव शूद्रांः चात्मौपजीविनः एकैकं कारयेत् कर्म मासि मासि महीपतिः
7.e: Mechanics and Artisans, as also shudras who subsist by bodily labour,—the King shall make each of these work for one day every month.

7.s: naucchindyādātmano mūlaṃ pareṣāṃ cātitṛṣṇayā ucchindan hyātmano mūlamāṭmānaṃ tāṃśca pīdayet
7.d: नौच्छिन्द्यादात्मनो मूलं परेषां चातितृष्णया उच्छिन्दन् ह्यात्मनो मूलमाट्मानं तांश्च पीदयेत्
7.e: He shall not cut off his own root, nor that of others, through excessive greed; by cutting off his own root he causes suffering to himself as well as to others.

7.s: tīkṣṇaścaiva mṛduśca syāt kāryaṃ vīkṣya mahīpatiḥ tīkṣṇaścaiva mṛduścaiva rāja bhavati sammataḥ
7.d: तीक्ष्णश्चैव मृदुश्च स्यात् कार्यं वीक्ष्य महीपतिः तीक्ष्णश्चैव मृदुश्चैव राज भवति सम्मतः
7.e: The King shall be severe and mild, after having duly examined the work (of each man); it is only the severe-mild King who is highly respected.

7.s: amātyamukhyaṃ dharmajñaṃ prājñaṃ dāntaṃ kulaudgatam sthāpayedāsane tasmin khinnaḥ kāryaikṣaṇe nṛṇām
7.d: अमात्यमुख्यं धर्मज्ञं प्राज्ञं दान्तं कुलौद्गतम् स्थापयेदासने तस्मिन् खिन्नः कार्यैक्षणे नृणाम्
7.e: When tired with looking after the affairs of men, he shall place in that place his chief minister, who is conversant with the law, wise, self-controlled, and born of a noble family.

7.s: evaṃ sarvaṃ vidhāyaidamitikartavyamātmanaḥ yuktaścaivāpramattaśca parirakṣedimāḥ prajāḥ
7.d: एवं सर्वं विधायैदमितिकर्तव्यमात्मनः युक्तश्चैवाप्रमत्तश्च परिरक्षेदिमाः प्रजाः
7.e: Having thus arranged all his business, he shall protect his people, ever intent and watchful.

7.s: vikrośantyo yasya rāṣṭrādhriyante dasyubhiḥ prajāḥ saṃpaśyataḥ sabhṛtyasya mṛtaḥ sa na tu jīvati
7.d: विक्रोशन्त्यो यस्य राष्ट्राध्रियन्ते दस्युभिः प्रजाः संपश्यतः सभृत्यस्य मृतः स न तु जीवति
7.e: He, from whose territories people are carried off, screaming, by robbers, while he himself, along with his servants is looking on, is dead, not alive.

7.s: kṣatriyasya paro dharmaḥ prājānāmeva pālanam nirdiṣṭaphalabhoktā hi rājā dharmeṇa yujyate
7.d: क्षत्रियस्य परो धर्मः प्राजानामेव पालनम् निर्दिष्टफलभोक्ता हि राजा धर्मेण युज्यते
7.e: The protection of the people is the Kṣatriya’s highest duty; the King, who enjoys the fruits mentioned, becomes endowed with merit.

7.s: utthāya paścime yāme kṛtaśaucaḥ samāhitaḥ hutāgnirbrāhmaṇāṃścārcya praviśet sa śubhāṃ sabhām
7.d: उत्थाय पश्चिमे यामे कृतशौचः समाहितः हुताग्निर्ब्राह्मणांश्चार्च्य प्रविशेत् स शुभां सभाम्
7.e: Having risen during the last watch of the night and performed his ablutions, with collected mind, having poured libations into the Fire, and honoured the Brāhmaṇas, he shall enter the auspicious Hall of Audience.

7.s: tatra sthitaḥ prajāḥ sarvāḥ pratinandya visarjayet visṛjya ca prajāḥ sarvā mantrayet saha mantribhiḥ
7.d: तत्र स्थितः प्रजाः सर्वाः प्रतिनन्द्य विसर्जयेत् विसृज्य च प्रजाः सर्वा मन्त्रयेत् सह मन्त्रिभिः
7.e: Staying there, he shall welcome all his subjects and then send them away. Having sent off all the people, he shall take counsel with his minister.

7.s: giripṛṣṭhaṃ samāruhya prasādaṃ vā rahogataḥ araṇye nisśalāke vā mantrayedavibhāvitaḥ
7.d: गिरिपृष्ठं समारुह्य प्रसादं वा रहोगतः अरण्ये निस्शलाके वा मन्त्रयेदविभावितः
7.e: Having ascended the top of a hill, or a house, and retiring into solitude,—or in a desolate forst he shall hold counsel, unobserved.

7.s: yasya mantraṃ na jānanti samāgamya pṛthagjanāḥ sa kṛtsnāṃ pṛthivīṃ bhuṅkte kośahīno 'pi pārthivaḥ
7.d: यस्य मन्त्रं न जानन्ति समागम्य पृथग्जनाः स कृत्स्नां पृथिवीं भुङ्क्ते कोशहीनो ऽपि पार्थिवः
7.e: That King, whose secret plans other people, coming together, do not know, enjoys the whole earth, even though he be poor in treasure.

7.s: jaḍamūkāndhabadhirāṃstairyagyonān vayo 'tigān strīmlecchavyādhitavyaṅgān mantrakāle 'pasārayet
7.d: जडमूकान्धबधिरांस्तैर्यग्योनान् वयो ऽतिगान् स्त्रीम्लेच्छव्याधितव्यङ्गान् मन्त्रकाले ऽपसारयेत्
7.e: At the time of taking counsel, he shall send away the idiot, the dumb and the deaf, animals, very aged persons, women, foreigners, the sick and the maimed.

7.s: bhindantyavamatā mantraṃ tairyagyonāstathaiva ca striyaścaiva viśeṣeṇa tasmāt tatrādṛto bhavet
7.d: भिन्दन्त्यवमता मन्त्रं तैर्यग्योनास्तथैव च स्त्रियश्चैव विशेषेण तस्मात् तत्रादृतो भवेत्
7.e: Persons who have been disgraced, animals, and particularly women betray secret plans; hence he shall be careful with regard to them.

7.s: madhyaṃdine 'rdharātre vā viśrānto vigataklamaḥ cintayeddharmakāmārthān sārdhaṃ taireka eva vā sārthaṃ
7.d: मध्यंदिने ऽर्धरात्रे वा विश्रान्तो विगतक्लमः चिन्तयेद्धर्मकामार्थान् सार्धं तैरेक एव वा सार्थं
7.e: At mid-day or at mid-night, free from fatigue and dulness, he shall deliberate on matters relating to morality, pleasure and wealth, either with them, or alone by himself;

7.s: parasparaviruddhānāṃ teṣāṃ ca samupārjanam kanyānāṃ saṃpradānaṃ ca kumārāṇāṃ ca rakṣaṇam
7.d: परस्परविरुद्धानां तेषां च समुपार्जनम् कन्यानां संप्रदानं च कुमाराणां च रक्षणम्
7.e: —also on the attainment of these, mutually irreconcilable as they are, on the giving away of daughters and on the guardianship of sons;

7.s: dūtasaṃpreṣaṇaṃ caiva kāryaśeṣaṃ tathaiva ca antaḥpurapracāraṃ ca praṇidhīnāṃ ca ceṣṭitam
7.d: दूतसंप्रेषणं चैव कार्यशेषं तथैव च अन्तःपुरप्रचारं च प्रणिधीनां च चेष्टितम्
7.e: —or the sending of ambassadors, the remaining details of undertakings, on the affairs of the harem, and on the work of spies;

7.s: kṛtsnaṃ cāṣṭavidhaṃ karma pañcavargaṃ ca tattvataḥ anurāgāparāgau ca pracāraṃ maṇḍalasya ca
7.d: कृत्स्नं चाष्टविधं कर्म पञ्चवर्गं च तत्त्वतः अनुरागापरागौ च प्रचारं मण्डलस्य च
7.e: —also upon the entire ‘eight-fold business,’ and on the ‘five-fold group’ in its real character, on affection and disaffection, and on the conduct of his ‘circle’.

7.s: madhyamasya pracāraṃ ca vijīgiṣośca ceṣṭitam udāsīnapracāraṃ ca śatroścaiva prayatnataḥ
7.d: मध्यमस्य प्रचारं च विजीगिषोश्च चेष्टितम् उदासीनप्रचारं च शत्रोश्चैव प्रयत्नतः
7.e: —on the conduct of the ‘intermediary’ oh the doings of the king bent upon conquest, on the action of the neutral king, as also that of his enemy, with special care.

7.s: etāḥ prakṛtayo mūlaṃ maṇḍalasya samāsataḥ aṣṭau cānyāḥ samākhyātā dvādaśaiva tu tāḥ smṛtāḥ
7.d: एताः प्रकृतयो मूलं मण्डलस्य समासतः अष्टौ चान्याः समाख्याता द्वादशैव तु ताः स्मृताः
7.e: These four components are, in brief, the root of the circle; eight others also have been described; these being the twelve that have been spoken op.

7.s: amātyarāṣṭradurgārthadaṇḍākhyāḥ pañca cāparāḥ pratyekaṃ kathitā hyetāḥ saṅkṣepeṇa dvisaptatiḥ
7.d: अमात्यराष्ट्रदुर्गार्थदण्डाख्याः पञ्च चापराः प्रत्येकं कथिता ह्येताः सङ्क्षेपेण द्विसप्ततिः
7.e: There are five others, (1) the minister, (2) the kingdom, (3) the fortress, (4) the treasury and (5) the army—described in connection with each (of the above twelve); these then, briefly, being seventy-two.

7.s: anantaramariṃ vidyādarisevinameva ca areranantaraṃ mitramudāsīnaṃ tayoḥ param
7.d: अनन्तरमरिं विद्यादरिसेविनमेव च अरेरनन्तरं मित्रमुदासीनं तयोः परम्
7.e: He shall regard, as ‘enemy’, his immediate neighbour, as also the person who helps his enemy; the immediate neighbour of his enemy he shall regard as his ‘friend’; and as ‘neutral’ the king who is beyond those two.

7.s: tān sarvānabhisaṃdadhyāt sāmādibhirupakramaiḥ vyastaiścaiva samastaiśca pauruṣeṇa nayena ca
7.d: तान् सर्वानभिसंदध्यात् सामादिभिरुपक्रमैः व्यस्तैश्चैव समस्तैश्च पौरुषेण नयेन च
7.e: All these he shall win over by means of conciliation and the other expedients, severally as well as collectively, as also by prowess and policy.

7.s: saṃdhiṃ ca vigrahaṃ caiva yānamāsanameva ca dvaidhībhāvaṃ saṃśrayaṃ ca ṣaḍguṇāṃścintayet sadā
7.d: संधिं च विग्रहं चैव यानमासनमेव च द्वैधीभावं संश्रयं च षड्गुणांश्चिन्तयेत् सदा
7.e: Alliance, War, March, Halt, Bifurcation and seeking shelter—these six measures of policy he shall constantly ponder over.

7.s: āsanaṃ caiva yānaṃ ca saṃdhiṃ vigrahameva ca kāryaṃ vīkṣya prayuñjīta dvaidhaṃ saṃśrayameva ca
7.d: आसनं चैव यानं च संधिं विग्रहमेव च कार्यं वीक्ष्य प्रयुञ्जीत द्वैधं संश्रयमेव च
7.e: He shall have recourse to Halting, to Marching, to Alliance, to War, to Bifurcation or to Seeking shelter, after having fully considered his business.

7.s: saṃdhiṃ tu dvividhaṃ vidyādrājā vigrahameva ca ubhe yānāsane caiva dvividhaḥ saṃśrayaḥ smṛtaḥ
7.d: संधिं तु द्विविधं विद्याद्राजा विग्रहमेव च उभे यानासने चैव द्विविधः संश्रयः स्मृतः
7.e: Alliance, endowed with future possibilities, is of two kinds—(1) that in which the act of marching is undertaken in common and (2) that; in which it is otherwise.

7.s: samānayānakarmā ca viparītastathaiva ca tadā tvāyatisaṃyuktaḥ saṃdhirjñeyo dvilakṣaṇaḥ
7.d: समानयानकर्मा च विपरीतस्तथैव च तदा त्वायतिसंयुक्तः संधिर्ज्ञेयो द्विलक्षणः
7.e: Alliance, endowed with future possibilities, is of two kinds—(1) that in which the act of marching is undertaken in common and (2) that; in which it is otherwise.

7.s: svayaṅkṛtaśca kāryārthamakāle kāla eva vā mitrasya caivāpakṛte dvividho vigrahaḥ smṛtaḥ
7.d: स्वयङ्कृतश्च कार्यार्थमकाले काल एव वा मित्रस्य चैवापकृते द्विविधो विग्रहः स्मृतः
7.e: War has been declared to be of two kinds:—(1) that which is waged, in season or out of season, by oneself, for his own purpose, and (2) that which is waged on some wrong done to an ally.

7.s: ekākinaścātyayike kārye prāpte yadṛcchayā saṃhatasya ca mitreṇa dvividhaṃ yānamucyate
7.d: एकाकिनश्चात्ययिके कार्ये प्राप्ते यदृच्छया संहतस्य च मित्रेण द्विविधं यानमुच्यते
7.e: Marching is said to be of two kinds—(1) that undertaken by the king by himself alone, on the sudden approach of an emergent occasion, and (2) that undertaken by him accompanied by his ally.

7.s: kṣīṇasya caiva kramaśo daivāt pūrvakṛtena vā mitrasya cānurodhena dvividhaṃ smṛtamāsanam
7.d: क्षीणस्य चैव क्रमशो दैवात् पूर्वकृतेन वा मित्रस्य चानुरोधेन द्विविधं स्मृतमासनम्
7.e: Halting has been declared to be of two kinds:—(1) that which is necessary for one who has become gradually weakened, either by chance or through previous acts, and (2) that which is necessitated by considerations for his ally.

7.s: balasya svāminaścaiva sthitiḥ kāryārthasiddhaye dvividhaṃ kīrtyate dvaidhaṃ ṣāḍguṇyaguṇavedibhiḥ
7.d: बलस्य स्वामिनश्चैव स्थितिः कार्यार्थसिद्धये द्विविधं कीर्त्यते द्वैधं षाड्गुण्यगुणवेदिभिः
7.e: When, for the accomplishment of some purpose, the Master takes up one position and the Force another,—this is what is described as ‘Bifurcation’ by those conversant with the details of the six measures of policy.

7.s: arthasaṃpādanārthaṃ ca pīḍyamānasya śatrubhiḥ sādhuṣu vyapadeśaśca dvividhaḥ saṃśrayaḥ smṛtaḥ
7.d: अर्थसंपादनार्थं च पीड्यमानस्य शत्रुभिः साधुषु व्यपदेशश्च द्विविधः संश्रयः स्मृतः
7.e: ‘Seeking shelter’, with noble people, has been declared to be of two kinds:—(1) that which is done for the sake of accomplishing a useful purpose, when harassed by enemies, and (2) that in the form of a status.

7.s: yadā 'vagacchedāyatyāmādhikyaṃ dhruvamātmanaḥ tadātve cālpikāṃ pīḍāṃ tadā saṃdhiṃ samāśrayet
7.d: यदा ऽवगच्छेदायत्यामाधिक्यं ध्रुवमात्मनः तदात्वे चाल्पिकां पीडां तदा संधिं समाश्रयेत्
7.e: When he knows that his superiority is certain in the future, and at the time there is but little harm done—then he should resort to peace.

7.s: yadā prahṛṣṭā manyeta sarvāstu prakṛtīrbhṛśam atyucchritaṃ tathātmānaṃ tadā kurvīta vigraham
7.d: यदा प्रहृष्टा मन्येत सर्वास्तु प्रकृतीर्भृशम् अत्युच्छ्रितं तथात्मानं तदा कुर्वीत विग्रहम्
7.e: But when he thinks all his people to be highly contented, and himself to be exceedingly prosperous,—then he shall make war.

7.s: yadā manyeta bhāvena hṛṣṭaṃ puṣṭaṃ balaṃ svakam parasya viparītaṃ ca tadā yāyādripuṃ prati
7.d: यदा मन्येत भावेन हृष्टं पुष्टं बलं स्वकम् परस्य विपरीतं च तदा यायाद्रिपुं प्रति
7.e: When he thinks that his own army is happy and strong in condition, and that of the enemy is the reverse, then shall he march against the enemy

7.s: yadā tu syāt parikṣīṇo vāhanena balena ca tadāsīta prayatnena śanakaiḥ sāntvayannarīn
7.d: यदा तु स्यात् परिक्षीणो वाहनेन बलेन च तदासीत प्रयत्नेन शनकैः सान्त्वयन्नरीन्
7.e: But when he happens to be weak in conveyances and soldiers, then he shall sit quiet, gradually conciliating his enemies with special care.

7.s: manyetāriṃ yadā rājā sarvathā balavattaram tadā dvidhā balaṃ kṛtvā sādhayet kāryamātmanaḥ
7.d: मन्येतारिं यदा राजा सर्वथा बलवत्तरम् तदा द्विधा बलं कृत्वा साधयेत् कार्यमात्मनः
7.e: When the king thinks his enemy to be stronger in every respect, then he should bifurcate his force and thus accomplish his own purpose.

7.s: yadā parabalānāṃ tu gamanīyatamo bhavet tadā tu saṃśrayet kṣipraṃ dhārmikaṃ balinaṃ nṛpam
7.d: यदा परबलानां तु गमनीयतमो भवेत् तदा तु संश्रयेत् क्षिप्रं धार्मिकं बलिनं नृपम्
7.e: When he happens to be very much open to attack by the enemy’s forces, then he shall seek shelter with a r ighte ous and powerful King.

7.s: nigrahaṃ prakṛtīnāṃ ca kuryādyo 'ribalasya ca upaseveta taṃ nityaṃ sarvayatnairguruṃ yathā
7.d: निग्रहं प्रकृतीनां च कुर्याद्यो ऽरिबलस्य च उपसेवेत तं नित्यं सर्वयत्नैर्गुरुं यथा
7.e: That king who does the chastisement of his people as also of his enemy’s army,—him he shall ever serve with every effort, like a preceptor.

7.s: yadi tatrāpi saṃpaśyeddoṣaṃ saṃśrayakāritam suyuddhameva tatrāpi nirviśaṅkaḥ samācaret
7.d: यदि तत्रापि संपश्येद्दोषं संश्रयकारितम् सुयुद्धमेव तत्रापि निर्विशङ्कः समाचरेत्
7.e: If even there he should perceive something wrong on the part of his shelterer, then, even in that condition he shall, without hesitation, resort to war.

7.s: sarvaupāyaistathā kuryānnītijñaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ yathā 'syābhyadhikā na syurmitraudāsīnaśatravaḥ
7.d: सर्वौपायैस्तथा कुर्यान्नीतिज्ञः पृथिवीपतिः यथा ऽस्याभ्यधिका न स्युर्मित्रौदासीनशत्रवः
7.e: By means of all the expedients, the politic king shall act in such a manner that his allies, neutrals and enemies do not become superior to himself.

7.s: āyatiṃ sarvakāryāṇāṃ tadātvaṃ ca vicārayet atītānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ guṇadoṣau ca tattvataḥ
7.d: आयतिं सर्वकार्याणां तदात्वं च विचारयेत् अतीतानां च सर्वेषां गुणदोषौ च तत्त्वतः
7.e: He shall fully think over the future and the present condition of all undertakings, as also the good and bad points of all past ones.

7.s: āyatyāṃ guṇadoṣajñastadātve kṣipraniścayaḥ atīte kāryaśeṣajñaḥ śatrubhirnābhibhūyate
7.d: आयत्यां गुणदोषज्ञस्तदात्वे क्षिप्रनिश्चयः अतीते कार्यशेषज्ञः शत्रुभिर्नाभिभूयते
7.e: He, who is alive to the good and bad points in re gard to the future, is quick in his decisions relating to the present, and understands the consequences of his acts in the past, is never overpowered by his enemies.

7.s: yathainaṃ nābhisaṃdadhyurmitraudāsīnaśatravaḥ tathā sarvaṃ saṃvidadhyādeṣa sāmāsiko nayaḥ
7.d: यथैनं नाभिसंदध्युर्मित्रौदासीनशत्रवः तथा सर्वं संविदध्यादेष सामासिको नयः
7.e: He shall arrange everything in such a manner that his allies or neutrals or enemies may not get the better of him; this is the sum-total of state-policy.

7.s: tadā tu yānamātiṣṭhedarirāṣṭraṃ prati prabhuḥ tadānena vidhānena yāyādaripuraṃ śanaiḥ
7.d: तदा तु यानमातिष्ठेदरिराष्ट्रं प्रति प्रभुः तदानेन विधानेन यायादरिपुरं शनैः
7.e: When the king undertakes an expedition against the enemy’s kingdom, he shall advance slowly towards the enemy’s capital, in the following manner.

7.s: mārgaśīrṣe śubhe māsi yāyādyātrāṃ mahīpatiḥ phālgunaṃ vātha caitraṃ vā māsau prati yathābalam
7.d: मार्गशीर्षे शुभे मासि यायाद्यात्रां महीपतिः फाल्गुनं वाथ चैत्रं वा मासौ प्रति यथाबलम्
7.e: The king shall start on his expedition in the auspicious month of Mārgaśīrṣa, or towards the months of Phalguna and Caitra, according to the condition of his forces.

7.s: anyeṣvapi tu kāleṣu yadā paśyeddhruvaṃ jayam tadā yāyādvigṛhyaiva vyasane cautthite ripoḥ
7.d: अन्येष्वपि तु कालेषु यदा पश्येद्ध्रुवं जयम् तदा यायाद्विगृह्यैव व्यसने चौत्थिते रिपोः
7.e: At other times also, if he perceives certain victory, then he shall pick up a quarrel and march forward; also when some trouble has arisen for the enemy.

7.s: kṛtvā vidhānaṃ mūle tu yātrikaṃ ca yathāvidhi upagṛhyāspadaṃ caiva cārān samyag vidhāya ca
7.d: कृत्वा विधानं मूले तु यात्रिकं च यथाविधि उपगृह्यास्पदं चैव चारान् सम्यग् विधाय च
7.e: Having duly made arrangements at the base, as also those pertaining to the expedition, having secured a basis, and having duly deputed his spies,—having cleared the three kinds of roads, and having equipped his own six-fold force,—he shall advance against the enemy’s capital in the manner prescribed for warfare.

7.s: saṃśodhya trividhaṃ mārgaṃ ṣaḍvidhaṃ ca balaṃ svakam sāṃparāyikakalpena yāyādaripuraṃ prati
7.d: संशोध्य त्रिविधं मार्गं षड्विधं च बलं स्वकम् सांपरायिककल्पेन यायादरिपुरं प्रति
7.e: Having duly made arrangements at the base, as also those pertaining to the expedition, having secured a basis, and having duly deputed his spies,—having cleared the three kinds of roads, and having equipped his own six-fold force,—he shall advance against the enemy’s capital in the manner prescribed for warfare.

7.s: śatrusevini mitre ca gūḍhe yuktataro bhavet gatapratyāgate caiva sa hi kaṣṭataro ripuḥ
7.d: शत्रुसेविनि मित्रे च गूढे युक्ततरो भवेत् गतप्रत्यागते चैव स हि कष्टतरो रिपुः
7.e: He shall be very much on his guard against an ally who may be secretly serving the enemy, as also against one who has gone away and returned; as he is the more dangerous enemy.—(1 86)

7.s: daṇḍavyūhena tan mārgaṃ yāyāt tu śakaṭena vā varāhamakarābhyāṃ vā sūcyā vā garuḍena vā
7.d: दण्डव्यूहेन तन् मार्गं यायात् तु शकटेन वा वराहमकराभ्यां वा सूच्या वा गरुडेन वा
7.e: He shall march on this road arraying his army in the form of a staff, or in that of a cart, or a boar, or an alligator, or a needle or the Garuḍa-bird.

7.s: yataśca bhayamāśaṅket tato vistārayedbalam padmena caiva vyūhena niviśeta sadā svayam
7.d: यतश्च भयमाशङ्केत् ततो विस्तारयेद्बलम् पद्मेन चैव व्यूहेन निविशेत सदा स्वयम्
7.e: From where he apprehends danger there he shall extend his forces; and he himself shall always encamp in the ‘lotus-array’

7.s: senāpatibalādhyakṣau sarvadikṣu niveśayet yataśca bhayamāśaṅket prācīṃ tāṃ kalpayeddiśam
7.d: सेनापतिबलाध्यक्षौ सर्वदिक्षु निवेशयेत् यतश्च भयमाशङ्केत् प्राचीं तां कल्पयेद्दिशम्
7.e: The Commander-in-Chief and the General he shall station in all directions; the quarter from which he apprehends danger, that he shall regard as the ‘East’ (Front).

7.s: gulmāṃśca sthāpayedāptān kṛtasaṃjñān samantataḥ sthāne yuddhe ca kuśalānabhīrūnavikāriṇaḥ
7.d: गुल्मांश्च स्थापयेदाप्तान् कृतसंज्ञान् समन्ततः स्थाने युद्धे च कुशलानभीरूनविकारिणः
7.e: On all sides he shall station reliable pickets, with whom signals have been arranged, who are experts in standing firm as also in charging, fearless and loyal.

7.s: saṃhatān yodhayedalpān kāmaṃ vistārayedbahūn sūcyā vajreṇa caivaitān vyūhena vyūhya yodhayet
7.d: संहतान् योधयेदल्पान् कामं विस्तारयेद्बहून् सूच्या वज्रेण चैवैतान् व्यूहेन व्यूह्य योधयेत्
7.e: He shall make a small number of men fight in close formation; but a large number he may extend as he likes. He shall make them fight, arraying them in the form of the ‘needle’ and the ‘thunderbolt.’

7.s: syandanāśvaiḥ same yudhyedanūpe nau dvipaistathā vṛkṣagulmāvṛte cāpairasicarmāyudhaiḥ sthale
7.d: स्यन्दनाश्वैः समे युध्येदनूपे नौ द्विपैस्तथा वृक्षगुल्मावृते चापैरसिचर्मायुधैः स्थले
7.e: On even ground he shall fight with chariots and horses; on marshy ground with boats and elephants; on ground covered with trees and thickets with bows; and on firm ground with swords and shields and other weapons.

7.s: kurukṣetrāṃśca matsyāṃśca pañcālāṃśūrasenajān :kaurakṣetrāṃśca dīrghāṃllaghūṃścaiva narānagrānīkeṣu yojayet
7.d: कुरुक्षेत्रांश्च मत्स्यांश्च पञ्चालांशूरसेनजान् :कौरक्षेत्रांश्च दीर्घांल्लघूंश्चैव नरानग्रानीकेषु योजयेत्
7.e: Men born in the countries of Kurukṣhtra, Matsya, Pañcāla, and Śūrasena.—he shall make these fight in the vanguard; as also those that are tall and light.

7.s: praharṣayedbalaṃ vyūhya tāṃśca samyak parīkṣayet bhṛśaṃ parīkṣayet ceṣṭāścaiva vijānīyādarīn yodhayatāmapi
7.d: प्रहर्षयेद्बलं व्यूह्य तांश्च सम्यक् परीक्षयेत् भृशं परीक्षयेत् चेष्टाश्चैव विजानीयादरीन् योधयतामपि
7.e: Having arrayed his forces, he shall encourage them and thoroughly test them; even while they are engaging the enemy, he shall mark their behaviour.

7.s: uparudhyārimāsīta rāṣṭraṃ cāsyaupapīḍayet dūṣayeccāsya satataṃ yavasānnaudakaindhanam
7.d: उपरुध्यारिमासीत राष्ट्रं चास्यौपपीडयेत् दूषयेच्चास्य सततं यवसान्नौदकैन्धनम्
7.e: After having besieged the foe, he shall halt, and proceed to harass his kingdom and continually vitiate his supply of fodder, food, water and fuel.

7.s: bhindyāccaiva taḍāgāni prākāraparikhāstathā samavaskandayeccainaṃ rātrau vitrāsayet tathā
7.d: भिन्द्याच्चैव तडागानि प्राकारपरिखास्तथा समवस्कन्दयेच्चैनं रात्रौ वित्रासयेत् तथा
7.e: He shall destroy the tanks, as also walls and ditches; he shall assail the enemy and shall frighten him—during the night.

7.s: upajapyānupajapedbudhyetaiva ca tatkṛtam yukte ca daive yudhyeta jayaprepsurapetabhīḥ
7.d: उपजप्यानुपजपेद्बुध्येतैव च तत्कृतम् युक्ते च दैवे युध्येत जयप्रेप्सुरपेतभीः
7.e: He shall alienate all who are alienable, keep himself informed of the enemy’s doings, and when fate is propitious, he shall fight, devoid of fear and determined to co nquer.

7.s: sāmnā dānena bhedena samastairatha vā pṛthak vijetuṃ prayatetārīnna yuddhena kadā cana ariṃ
7.d: साम्ना दानेन भेदेन समस्तैरथ वा पृथक् विजेतुं प्रयतेतारीन्न युद्धेन कदा चन अरिं
7.e: By conciliation, by gifts and by dissension,—either severally or collectively,—he shall try to conquer his enemy,—never by war.

7.s: anityo vijayo yasmāddṛśyate yudhyamānayoḥ parājayaśca saṅgrāme tasmādyuddhaṃ vivarjayet
7.d: अनित्यो विजयो यस्माद्दृश्यते युध्यमानयोः पराजयश्च सङ्ग्रामे तस्माद्युद्धं विवर्जयेत्
7.e: Since between two combatants victory is found to be uncertain, as also defeat,—therefore he shall avoid fighting

7.s: trayāṇāmapyupāyānāṃ pūrvauktānāmasaṃbhave tathā yudhyeta saṃpanno vijayeta ripūn yathā
7.d: त्रयाणामप्युपायानां पूर्वौक्तानामसंभवे तथा युध्येत संपन्नो विजयेत रिपून् यथा
7.e: But in the event of the three aforesaid expedients failing, he shall fight in such a manner as to conquer his enemies completely.

7.s: jitvā saṃpūjayeddevān brāhmaṇāṃścaiva dhārmikān pradadyāt parihārārthaṃ khyāpayedabhayāni ca
7.d: जित्वा संपूजयेद्देवान् ब्राह्मणांश्चैव धार्मिकान् प्रदद्यात् परिहारार्थं ख्यापयेदभयानि च
7.e: Having gained victory, he shall worship the gods and the righteous Brāhmaṇas, grant remissions and proclaim amnesties.

7.s: sarveṣāṃ tu viditvaiṣāṃ samāsena cikīrṣitam sthāpayet tatra tadvaṃśyaṃ kuryācca samayakriyām
7.d: सर्वेषां तु विदित्वैषां समासेन चिकीर्षितम् स्थापयेत् तत्र तद्वंश्यं कुर्याच्च समयक्रियाम्
7.e: Having briefly ascertained the wishes of all the people, he shall set up there a member of the same family and then conclude the treaty.

7.s: pramāṇāni ca kurvīta teṣāṃ dharmān yathauditān ratnaiśca pūjayedenaṃ pradhānapuruṣaiḥ saha
7.d: प्रमाणानि च कुर्वीत तेषां धर्मान् यथौदितान् रत्नैश्च पूजयेदेनं प्रधानपुरुषैः सह
7.e: He shall make authoritative all that is declared to have been lawful (in the kingdom), and shall honor with precious gifts the king along with the leading men.

7.s: ādānamapriyakaraṃ dānaṃ ca priyakārakam abhīpsitānāmarthānāṃ kāle yuktam kālayuktaṃ praśasyate
7.d: आदानमप्रियकरं दानं च प्रियकारकम् अभीप्सितानामर्थानां काले युक्तम् कालयुक्तं प्रशस्यते
7.e: The seizing of desirable property is productive of displeasure, and the giving of it is productive of pleasure; each is commended if done at the proper time.

7.s: sarvaṃ karmaidamāyattaṃ vidhāne daivamānuṣe tayordaivamacintyaṃ tu mānuṣe vidyate kriyā [daivena vidhinā yuktaṃ mānuṣyaṃ yat pravartate ] yuktaṃ [parikleśena mahatā tadarthasya samādhakam ] [saṃyuktasyāpi daivena puruṣakāreṇa varjitam ] [vinā puruṣakāreṇa phalaṃ kṣetraṃ prayacchati ] [candrārkādyā grahā vāyuragnirāpastathaiva ca ] [iha daivena sādhyante pauruṣeṇa prayatnataḥ ]
7.d: सर्वं कर्मैदमायत्तं विधाने दैवमानुषे तयोर्दैवमचिन्त्यं तु मानुषे विद्यते क्रिया [दैवेन विधिना युक्तं मानुष्यं यत् प्रवर्तते ] युक्तं [परिक्लेशेन महता तदर्थस्य समाधकम् ] [संयुक्तस्यापि दैवेन पुरुषकारेण वर्जितम् ] [विना पुरुषकारेण फलं क्षेत्रं प्रयच्छति ] [चन्द्रार्काद्या ग्रहा वायुरग्निरापस्तथैव च ] [इह दैवेन साध्यन्ते पौरुषेण प्रयत्नतः ]
7.e: All this undertaking is dependent upon the ordering of Destiny and of Human Exertion; of these two, Destiny is incomprehensible, and action is possible only in regard to Human Exertion.

7.s: saha vā 'pi vrajedyuktaḥ saṃdhiṃ kṛtvā prayatnataḥ mitraṃ hiraṇyaṃ bhūmiṃ vā saṃpaśyaṃstrividhaṃ phalam
7.d: सह वा ऽपि व्रजेद्युक्तः संधिं कृत्वा प्रयत्नतः मित्रं हिरण्यं भूमिं वा संपश्यंस्त्रिविधं फलम्
7.e: Gentlemanliness, knowledge of men, bravery, compassionate disposition, and constant liberality are the qualities to be sought for in a Neutral.

7.s: pārṣṇigrāhaṃ ca saṃprekṣya tathākrandaṃ ca maṇḍale mitrādathāpyamitrādvā yātrāphalamavāpnuyāt
7.d: पार्ष्णिग्राहं च संप्रेक्ष्य तथाक्रन्दं च मण्डले मित्रादथाप्यमित्राद्वा यात्राफलमवाप्नुयात्
7.e: Gentlemanliness, knowledge of men, bravery, compassionate disposition, and constant liberality are the qualities to be sought for in a Neutral.

7.s: hiraṇyabhūmisaṃprāptyā pārthivo na tathaidhate yathā mitraṃ dhruvaṃ labdhvā kṛśamapyāyatikṣamam
7.d: हिरण्यभूमिसंप्राप्त्या पार्थिवो न तथैधते यथा मित्रं ध्रुवं लब्ध्वा कृशमप्यायतिक्षमम्
7.e: Gentlemanliness, knowledge of men, bravery, compassionate disposition, and constant liberality are the qualities to be sought for in a Neutral.

7.s: dharmajñaṃ ca kṛtajñaṃ ca tuṣṭaprakṛtimeva ca anuraktaṃ sthirārambhaṃ laghumitraṃ praśasyate
7.d: धर्मज्ञं च कृतज्ञं च तुष्टप्रकृतिमेव च अनुरक्तं स्थिरारम्भं लघुमित्रं प्रशस्यते
7.e: Gentlemanliness, knowledge of men, bravery, compassionate disposition, and constant liberality are the qualities to be sought for in a Neutral.

7.s: prājñaṃ kulīnaṃ śūraṃ ca dakṣaṃ dātārameva ca kṛtajñaṃ dhṛtimantaṃ ca kaṣṭamāhurariṃ budhāḥ
7.d: प्राज्ञं कुलीनं शूरं च दक्षं दातारमेव च कृतज्ञं धृतिमन्तं च कष्टमाहुररिं बुधाः
7.e: Gentlemanliness, knowledge of men, bravery, compassionate disposition, and constant liberality are the qualities to be sought for in a Neutral.

7.s: āryatā puruṣajñānaṃ śauryaṃ karuṇaveditā sthaulalakṣyaṃ ca satatamudāsīnaguṇaudayaḥ
7.d: आर्यता पुरुषज्ञानं शौर्यं करुणवेदिता स्थौललक्ष्यं च सततमुदासीनगुणौदयः
7.e: Gentlemanliness, knowledge of men, bravery, compassionate disposition, and constant liberality are the qualities to be sought for in a Neutral.

7.s: ksemyāṃ sasyapradāṃ nityaṃ paśuvṛddhikarīmapi parityajennṛpo bhūmimātmārthamavicārayan
7.d: क्सेम्यां सस्यप्रदां नित्यं पशुवृद्धिकरीमपि परित्यजेन्नृपो भूमिमात्मार्थमविचारयन्
7.e: Even though the land (occupied by him) be safe, fertile and conducive to the increase of cattle, yet he shall quit it,—not minding his own selfish interests.

7.s: āpadarthaṃ dhanaṃ rakṣeddārān rakṣeddhanairapi āpadarthe ātmānaṃ satataṃ rakṣeddārairapi dhanairapi
7.d: आपदर्थं धनं रक्षेद्दारान् रक्षेद्धनैरपि आपदर्थे आत्मानं सततं रक्षेद्दारैरपि धनैरपि
7.e: He shall save his wealth for the sake of trouble; his wife he shall protect even with his wealth; and himself he shall constantly protect, even with his wife and his wealth.

7.s: saha sarvāḥ samutpannāḥ prasamīkṣyāpado bhṛśam saṃyuktāṃśca viyuktāṃśca sarvaupāyān sṛjedbudhaḥ
7.d: सह सर्वाः समुत्पन्नाः प्रसमीक्ष्यापदो भृशम् संयुक्तांश्च वियुक्तांश्च सर्वौपायान् सृजेद्बुधः
7.e: Seeing all kinds of troubles frequently cropping up simutaneously, the wise person shall employ all the expedients, collectively as well as severally.

7.s: upetāramupeyaṃ ca sarvaupāyāṃśca kṛtsnaśaḥ etat trayaṃ samāśritya prayatetārthasiddhaye
7.d: उपेतारमुपेयं च सर्वौपायांश्च कृत्स्नशः एतत् त्रयं समाश्रित्य प्रयतेतार्थसिद्धये
7.e: (a) The employer of the expedients, (b) the end to be attained by the expedients and (c) the expedients themselves,—taking his stand upon all these three, he shall strive for the accomplishment of his purpose.

7.s: evaṃ sarvamidaṃ rājā saha sammantrya mantribhiḥ vyāyamyāplutya madhyāhne bhoktumantaḥpuraṃ viśet
7.d: एवं सर्वमिदं राजा सह सम्मन्त्र्य मन्त्रिभिः व्यायम्याप्लुत्य मध्याह्ने भोक्तुमन्तःपुरं विशेत्
7.e: Having thus discussed all this with his ministers, the king shall take exercise at midday; and having bathed, shall enter the inner apartment for the purpose of taking his food.

7.s: tatrātmabhūtaiḥ kālajñairahāryaiḥ paricārakaiḥ suparīkṣitamannādyamadyān mantrairviṣāpahaiḥ
7.d: तत्रात्मभूतैः कालज्ञैरहार्यैः परिचारकैः सुपरीक्षितमन्नाद्यमद्यान् मन्त्रैर्विषापहैः
7.e: There he shall eat the food that has been thoroughly tested by such servants as are his own very self, as are conversant with the peculiarities of time, and are uncorruptible,—with such sacred texts as are destructive of poison,

7.s: viṣaghnairagadaiścāsya sarvadravyāṇi yojayet viṣaghnairudakaiścāsya sarvadravyāṇi śodhayet viṣaghnāni ca ratnāni niyato dhārayet sadā
7.d: विषघ्नैरगदैश्चास्य सर्वद्रव्याणि योजयेत् विषघ्नैरुदकैश्चास्य सर्वद्रव्याणि शोधयेत् विषघ्नानि च रत्नानि नियतो धारयेत् सदा
7.e: He shall purify all his things by means of liquids destructive of poisons; and he shall be careful to wear always such gems as are antidotes against poison.

7.s: parīkṣitāḥ striyaścainaṃ vyajanaudakadhūpanaiḥ veṣābharaṇasaṃśuddhāḥ spṛśeyuḥ susamāhitāḥ
7.d: परीक्षिताः स्त्रियश्चैनं व्यजनौदकधूपनैः वेषाभरणसंशुद्धाः स्पृशेयुः सुसमाहिताः
7.e: Thoroughly tested women, whose toilet and ornaments have been examined, shall serve him attentively with fans, water and incense.

7.s: evaṃ prayatnaṃ kurvīta yānaśayyā ''sanāśane snāne prasādhane caiva sarvālaṅkārakeṣu ca
7.d: एवं प्रयत्नं कुर्वीत यानशय्या 'ऽसनाशने स्नाने प्रसाधने चैव सर्वालङ्कारकेषु च
7.e: He shall exercise similar caution with regard to conveyances, beds, seats and food, as also to bath, toilet and all kinds of ornaments

7.s: bhuktavān vihareccaiva strībhirantaḥpure saha vihṛtya tu yathākālaṃ punaḥ kāryāṇi cintayet
7.d: भुक्तवान् विहरेच्चैव स्त्रीभिरन्तःपुरे सह विहृत्य तु यथाकालं पुनः कार्याणि चिन्तयेत्
7.e: Having dined, he shall amuse himself in the inner apartment, in the company of the ladies; and having amused himself, he shall in due time again attend to business.

7.s: alaṅkṛtaśca saṃpaśyedāyudhīyaṃ punarjanam vāhanāni ca sarvāṇi śastrāṇyābharaṇāni ca
7.d: अलङ्कृतश्च संपश्येदायुधीयं पुनर्जनम् वाहनानि च सर्वाणि शस्त्राण्याभरणानि च
7.e: Duly robed, he shall again inspect the fighting men, as also all kinds of conveyances, weapons and accoutrements.
