7.s: saṃdhyāṃ caupāsya śṛṇuyādantarveśmani śastrabhṛt rahasyākhyāyināṃ caiva praṇidhīnāṃ ca ceṣṭitam
7.d: संध्यां चौपास्य शृणुयादन्तर्वेश्मनि शस्त्रभृत् रहस्याख्यायिनां चैव प्रणिधीनां च चेष्टितम्
7.e: Having attended to his twilight devotions, he shall, well- armed, listen, in an inner room, to the doings of persons making eecret reports, and also of his spies.

7.s: gatvā kakṣāntaraṃ tvanyat samanujñāpya taṃ janam praviśedbhojanārthaṃ ca strīvṛto 'ntaḥpuraṃ punaḥ
7.d: गत्वा कक्षान्तरं त्वन्यत् समनुज्ञाप्य तं जनम् प्रविशेद्भोजनार्थं च स्त्रीवृतो ऽन्तःपुरं पुनः
7.e: Repairing to another apartment, and having dismissed those people, he shall again enter the inner apartment, surrounded by the women, for the purpose of taking his food.

7.s: tatra bhuktvā punaḥ kiṃ cit tūryaghoṣaiḥ praharṣitaḥ saṃviśet taṃ yathākālamuttiṣṭhecca gataklamaḥ
7.d: तत्र भुक्त्वा पुनः किं चित् तूर्यघोषैः प्रहर्षितः संविशेत् तं यथाकालमुत्तिष्ठेच्च गतक्लमः
7.e: Then, having eaten a little again, and having been recreated by the sound of musical instruments, he shall sleep and rise at the proper time, freed from fatigue.

7.s: etadvidhānamātiṣṭhedarogaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ asvasthaḥ sarvametat tu bhṛtyeṣu viniyojayet
7.d: एतद्विधानमातिष्ठेदरोगः पृथिवीपतिः अस्वस्थः सर्वमेतत् तु भृत्येषु विनियोजयेत्

8.s: vyavahārān didṛkṣustu brāhmaṇaiḥ saha pārthivaḥ mantrajñairmantribhiścaiva vinītaḥ praviśet sabhām
8.d: व्यवहारान् दिदृक्षुस्तु ब्राह्मणैः सह पार्थिवः मन्त्रज्ञैर्मन्त्रिभिश्चैव विनीतः प्रविशेत् सभाम्
8.e: Desirous of investigating cases, the king shall enter the court, with a dignified demeanour, along with Brāhmaṇas and councillors, versed in counsel.

8.s: tatrāsīnaḥ sthito vā 'pi pāṇimudyamya dakṣiṇam vinītaveṣābharaṇaḥ paśyet kāryāṇi kāryiṇām
8.d: तत्रासीनः स्थितो वा ऽपि पाणिमुद्यम्य दक्षिणम् विनीतवेषाभरणः पश्येत् कार्याणि कार्यिणाम्
8.e: There, either seated or standing, raising his right hand, subdued in dress and ornaments, he shall look into the suits of the suitors.

8.s: pratyahaṃ deśadṛṣṭaiśca śāstradṛṣṭaiśca hetubhiḥ aṣṭādaśasu mārgeṣu nibaddhāni pṛthak pṛthak
8.d: प्रत्यहं देशदृष्टैश्च शास्त्रदृष्टैश्च हेतुभिः अष्टादशसु मार्गेषु निबद्धानि पृथक् पृथक्
8.e: [He shall look into the suits]—day after day, one by one,—falling as they do under eighteen heads,—according to principles deduced from local usage and from the scriptures.

8.s: teṣāmādyaṃ ṛṇādānaṃ nikṣepo 'svāmivikrayaḥ saṃbhūya ca samutthānaṃ dattasyānapakarma ca
8.d: तेषामाद्यं ऋणादानं निक्षेपो ऽस्वामिविक्रयः संभूय च समुत्थानं दत्तस्यानपकर्म च
8.e: Of these the first is (1) Non-payment of Debt; (then) (2) Deposits, (3) Selling without ownership, (4) Joint concerns, (5) Non-delivery of what has been given away,—[4]—(6) Non-payment of wages, (7) Breach of Contract, (8) Recision of Sale and Purchase, (9) Dispute between the Owner and the Keeper,—[5]—(10) Disputes regarding Boundaries, (11) and (12) Assault, physical and verbal, (13) Theft, (14) Violence, (15) Adultery,—[6]—(16) Duties of man and wife, (17) Partition, and (18) Gambling and Betting;—these are the eighteen topics that form the basis of law-suits.

8.s: vetanasyaiva cādānaṃ saṃvidaśca vyatikramaḥ krayavikrayānuśayo vivādaḥ svāmipālayoḥ
8.d: वेतनस्यैव चादानं संविदश्च व्यतिक्रमः क्रयविक्रयानुशयो विवादः स्वामिपालयोः
8.e: Of these the first is (1) Non-payment of Debt; (then) (2) Deposits, (3) Selling without ownership, (4) Joint concerns, (5) Non-delivery of what has been given away,—[4]—(6) Non-payment of wages, (7) Breach of Contract, (8) Recision of Sale and Purchase, (9) Dispute between the Owner and the Keeper,—[5]—(10) Disputes regarding Boundaries, (11) and (12) Assault, physical and verbal, (13) Theft, (14) Violence, (15) Adultery,—[6]—(16) Duties of man and wife, (17) Partition, and (18) Gambling and Betting;—these are the eighteen topics that form the basis of law-suits.

8.s: sīmāvivādadharmaśca pāruṣye daṇḍavācike steyaṃ ca sāhasaṃ caiva strīsaṅgrahaṇameva ca
8.d: सीमाविवादधर्मश्च पारुष्ये दण्डवाचिके स्तेयं च साहसं चैव स्त्रीसङ्ग्रहणमेव च
8.e: Of these the first is (1) Non-payment of Debt; (then) (2) Deposits, (3) Selling without ownership, (4) Joint concerns, (5) Non-delivery of what has been given away,—[4]—(6) Non-payment of wages, (7) Breach of Contract, (8) Recision of Sale and Purchase, (9) Dispute between the Owner and the Keeper,—[5]—(10) Disputes regarding Boundaries, (11) and (12) Assault, physical and verbal, (13) Theft, (14) Violence, (15) Adultery,—[6]—(16) Duties of man and wife, (17) Partition, and (18) Gambling and Betting;—these are the eighteen topics that form the basis of law-suits.

8.s: strīpuṃdharmo vibhāgaśca dyūtamāhvaya eva ca padānyaṣṭādaśaitāni vyavahārasthitāviha
8.d: स्त्रीपुंधर्मो विभागश्च द्यूतमाह्वय एव च पदान्यष्टादशैतानि व्यवहारस्थिताविह
8.e: Of these the first is (1) Non-payment of Debt; (then) (2) Deposits, (3) Selling without ownership, (4) Joint concerns, (5) Non-delivery of what has been given away,—[4]—(6) Non-payment of wages, (7) Breach of Contract, (8) Recision of Sale and Purchase, (9) Dispute between the Owner and the Keeper,—[5]—(10) Disputes regarding Boundaries, (11) and (12) Assault, physical and verbal, (13) Theft, (14) Violence, (15) Adultery,—[6]—(16) Duties of man and wife, (17) Partition, and (18) Gambling and Betting;—these are the eighteen topics that form the basis of law-suits.

8.s: eṣu sthāneṣu bhūyiṣṭhaṃ vivādaṃ caratāṃ nṛṇām dharmaṃ śāśvatamāśritya kuryāt kāryavinirṇayam
8.d: एषु स्थानेषु भूयिष्ठं विवादं चरतां नृणाम् धर्मं शाश्वतमाश्रित्य कुर्यात् कार्यविनिर्णयम्
8.e: Taking his stand upon eternal morality, he shall form his decision on the suits of men who mostly carry on disputes in regard to the aforesaid points.

8.s: yadā svayaṃ na kuryāt tu nṛpatiḥ kāryadarśanam tadā niyuñjyādvidvāṃsaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ kāryadarśane
8.d: यदा स्वयं न कुर्यात् तु नृपतिः कार्यदर्शनम् तदा नियुञ्ज्याद्विद्वांसं ब्राह्मणं कार्यदर्शने
8.e: When he himself may not carry on the investigation of suits, he shall appoint a learned Brāhmaṇa to do the work of investigation.

8.s: so 'sya kāryāṇi saṃpaśyet sabhyaireva tribhirvṛtaḥ sabhāmeva praviśyāgryāmāsīnaḥ sthita eva vā
8.d: सो ऽस्य कार्याणि संपश्येत् सभ्यैरेव त्रिभिर्वृतः सभामेव प्रविश्याग्र्यामासीनः स्थित एव वा
8.e: That man, accompanied by three assessors, shall enter the excellent Court, and either seated or standing, shall investigate the suits on behalf of the king.

8.s: yasmin deśe niṣīdanti viprā vedavidastrayaḥ rājñaścādhikṛto vidvān brahmaṇastāṃ sabhāṃ viduḥ
8.d: यस्मिन् देशे निषीदन्ति विप्रा वेदविदस्त्रयः राज्ञश्चाधिकृतो विद्वान् ब्रह्मणस्तां सभां विदुः
8.e: That place, where three Brāhmaṇas learned in the Veda sit, as also the learned Brāhmaṇa appointed by the king,—they regard as the ‘Court of Brahman.’

8.s: dharmo viddhastvadharmeṇa sabhāṃ yatraupatiṣṭhate śalyaṃ cāsya na kṛntanti viddhāstatra sabhāsadaḥ
8.d: धर्मो विद्धस्त्वधर्मेण सभां यत्रौपतिष्ठते शल्यं चास्य न कृन्तन्ति विद्धास्तत्र सभासदः
8.e: In a court where Justice is pierced by Injustice, and the members of the Court do not remove that dart, these members also become pierced.

8.s: sabhāṃ vā na praveṣṭavyaṃ vaktavyaṃ vā samañjasam sabhā vā na praveṣṭavyā abruvan vibruvan vā 'pi naro bhavati kilbiṣī
8.d: सभां वा न प्रवेष्टव्यं वक्तव्यं वा समञ्जसम् सभा वा न प्रवेष्टव्या अब्रुवन् विब्रुवन् वा ऽपि नरो भवति किल्बिषी
8.e: One should either not enter the Court at all, or he should speak out what is equitable; one who either spe aks nothing, or speaks falsely, becomes tainted with sin.

8.s: yatra dharmo hyadharmeṇa satyaṃ yatrānṛtena ca hanyate prekṣamāṇānāṃ hatāstatra sabhāsadaḥ
8.d: यत्र धर्मो ह्यधर्मेण सत्यं यत्रानृतेन च हन्यते प्रेक्षमाणानां हतास्तत्र सभासदः
8.e: Where justice is destroyed by injustice, or truth by falsehood, while people are looking on,—there the members of the court also are destroyed.

8.s: dharma eva hato hanti dharmo rakṣati rakṣitaḥ tasmāddharmo na hantavyo mā no dharmo hato 'vadhīt vadhīt
8.d: धर्म एव हतो हन्ति धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः तस्माद्धर्मो न हन्तव्यो मा नो धर्मो हतो ऽवधीत् वधीत्
8.e: Justice, blighted, blights; and justice, preserved, preserves; hence justice should not be blighted, lest blighted justice blight us.

8.s: vṛṣo hi bhagavān dharmastasya yaḥ kurute hyalam tvalam vṛṣalaṃ taṃ vidurdevāstasmāddharmaṃ na lopayet
8.d: वृषो हि भगवान् धर्मस्तस्य यः कुरुते ह्यलम् त्वलम् वृषलं तं विदुर्देवास्तस्माद्धर्मं न लोपयेत्
8.e: For Justice is the revered ‘Vṛṣa,’ Bull; and he who commits the violation, ‘alam,’ of it, him the gods regard as ‘vṛṣala,’ low-born; hence one shall not violate Justice.

8.s: eka eva suhṛddharmo nidhāne 'pyanuyāti yaḥ śarīreṇa samaṃ nāśaṃ sarvamanyaddhi gacchati
8.d: एक एव सुहृद्धर्मो निधाने ऽप्यनुयाति यः शरीरेण समं नाशं सर्वमन्यद्धि गच्छति
8.e: Morality (Justice) is the only friend who follows one even after death; everything else perishes along with the body.

8.s: pādo 'dharmasya kartāraṃ pādaḥ sākṣiṇaṃ ṛcchati pādaḥ sabhāsadaḥ sarvān pādo rājānaṃ ṛcchati
8.d: पादो ऽधर्मस्य कर्तारं पादः साक्षिणं ऋच्छति पादः सभासदः सर्वान् पादो राजानं ऋच्छति
8.e: One quarter of the Injustice falls on the man who commits it, one quarter on the witness, one quarter on the members of the Court and one quarter on the king.

8.s: rājā bhavatyanenāstu mucyante ca sabhāsadaḥ eno gacchati kartāraṃ nindā 'rho yatra nindyate
8.d: राजा भवत्यनेनास्तु मुच्यन्ते च सभासदः एनो गच्छति कर्तारं निन्दा ऽर्हो यत्र निन्द्यते
8.e: Where, however, the person deserving of censure is actually censured, there the king becomes sinless, the members of the court become freed, and the sin falls upon the perpetrator.

8.s: jātimātraupajīvī vā kāmaṃ syādbrāhmaṇabruvaḥ dharmapravaktā nṛpaterna śūdraḥ kathaṃ cana
8.d: जातिमात्रौपजीवी वा कामं स्याद्ब्राह्मणब्रुवः धर्मप्रवक्ता नृपतेर्न शूद्रः कथं चन
8.e: Even a so-called Brāhmaṇa, who makes a living by his caste only, may, at pleasure be the propounder of the Law for the king,—but not a Śūdra under any circumtsances.

8.s: yasya śūdrastu kurute rājño dharmavivecanam tasya sīdati tadrāṣṭraṃ paṅke gauriva paśyataḥ
8.d: यस्य शूद्रस्तु कुरुते राज्ञो धर्मविवेचनम् तस्य सीदति तद्राष्ट्रं पङ्के गौरिव पश्यतः
8.e: The kingdom or that king for whom the investigation of Law is done by a Śūdra, while he himself is looking on, suffers, like the cow in a morass.

8.s: yadrāṣṭraṃ śūdrabhūyiṣṭhaṃ nāstikākrāntamadvijam vinaśyatyāśu tat kṛtsnaṃ durbhikṣavyādhipīḍitam
8.d: यद्राष्ट्रं शूद्रभूयिष्ठं नास्तिकाक्रान्तमद्विजम् विनश्यत्याशु तत् कृत्स्नं दुर्भिक्षव्याधिपीडितम्
8.e: That kingdom where there is a majority of Śūdras, which is infested with non-believers and destitute of twice-born people, quickly perishes entirely, becoming afflicted by famine and disease.

8.s: dharmāsanamadhiṣṭhāya saṃvītāṅgaḥ samāhitaḥ praṇamya lokapālebhyaḥ kāryadarśanamārabhet
8.d: धर्मासनमधिष्ठाय संवीताङ्गः समाहितः प्रणम्य लोकपालेभ्यः कार्यदर्शनमारभेत्
8.e: Having occupied the Judgment-seat, with his body covered and mind collected, he shall salute the Guardian-Deities, and then proceed with the investigation of suits.

8.s: arthānarthāvubhau buddhvā dharmādharmau ca kevalau varṇakrameṇa sarvāṇi paśyet kāryāṇi kāryiṇām
8.d: अर्थानर्थावुभौ बुद्ध्वा धर्माधर्मौ च केवलौ वर्णक्रमेण सर्वाणि पश्येत् कार्याणि कार्यिणाम्
8.e: Understanding both ‘desirable’ and ‘undesirable’ to be only ‘Justice’ and ‘Injustice,’ he shall look into all the suits of the suitors, according to the order of the castes.

8.s: bāhyairvibhāvayetliṅgairbhāvamantargataṃ nṛṇām svaravarṇaiṅgitākāraiścakṣuṣā ceṣṭitena ca
8.d: बाह्यैर्विभावयेत्लिङ्गैर्भावमन्तर्गतं नृणाम् स्वरवर्णैङ्गिताकारैश्चक्षुषा चेष्टितेन च
8.e: He shall discover the internal disposition of men by external signs: by variations in their voice, colour and aspect, as also by means of the eye and by gestures.

8.s: ākārairiṅgitairgatyā ceṣṭayā bhāṣitena ca netravaktravikāraiśca gṛhyate 'ntargataṃ manaḥ
8.d: आकारैरिङ्गितैर्गत्या चेष्टया भाषितेन च नेत्रवक्त्रविकारैश्च गृह्यते ऽन्तर्गतं मनः
8.e: The inner mind is indicated by such variations as those of aspect, gait, gesture, speech, and by changes in the eye and the face.

8.s: bāladāyādikaṃ rikthaṃ tāvadrājā 'nupālayet yāvat sa syāt samāvṛtto yāvatcātītaśaiśavaḥ yāvadvā 'tītaśaiśavaḥ
8.d: बालदायादिकं रिक्थं तावद्राजा ऽनुपालयेत् यावत् स स्यात् समावृत्तो यावत्चातीतशैशवः यावद्वा ऽतीतशैशवः
8.e: The king shall take care of the property owned by a minor, till such time as he may return from the teacher’s house, or till he may have passed his minority.

8.s: vaśā 'putrāsu caivaṃ syādrakṣaṇaṃ niṣkulāsu ca pativratāsu ca strīṣu vidhavāsvāturāsu ca
8.d: वशा ऽपुत्रासु चैवं स्याद्रक्षणं निष्कुलासु च पतिव्रतासु च स्त्रीषु विधवास्वातुरासु च
8.e: There shall be similar protection in the case of barren women, of son-less women, of women devoted to their husbands, and of widows faithful to their husbands,—when their family is extinct, and when they are in distress.

8.s: jīvantīnāṃ tu tāsāṃ ye taddhareyuḥ svabāndhavāḥ tāṃśiṣyātcauradaṇḍena dhārmikaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ
8.d: जीवन्तीनां तु तासां ये तद्धरेयुः स्वबान्धवाः तांशिष्यात्चौरदण्डेन धार्मिकः पृथिवीपतिः
8.e: While these women are alive, if their relatives should appropriate their property,—on them the righteous king shall inflict the punishment of thieves.

8.s: praṇaṣṭasvāmikaṃ rikthaṃ rājā tryabdaṃ nidhāpayet arvāk tryabdāddharet svāmī pareṇa nṛpatirharet
8.d: प्रणष्टस्वामिकं रिक्थं राजा त्र्यब्दं निधापयेत् अर्वाक् त्र्यब्दाद्धरेत् स्वामी परेण नृपतिर्हरेत्
8.e: Property, the owner whereof has disappeared, the King shall keep for three years; up to three years the owner may receive it; but after that the King (shall take it).

8.s: mamaidamiti yo brūyāt so 'nuyojyo yathāvidhi saṃvādya rūpasaṅkhyādīn svāmī taddravyamarhati
8.d: ममैदमिति यो ब्रूयात् सो ऽनुयोज्यो यथाविधि संवाद्य रूपसङ्ख्यादीन् स्वामी तद्द्रव्यमर्हति
8.e: He who says ‘this is mine’ should be questioned in proper form; and the owner ought to receive the property after having correctly described the colour, the number and other details regarding it.

8.s: avedayāno naṣṭasya deśaṃ kālaṃ ca tattvataḥ varṇaṃ rūpaṃ pramāṇaṃ ca tatsamaṃ daṇḍamarhati
8.d: अवेदयानो नष्टस्य देशं कालं च तत्त्वतः वर्णं रूपं प्रमाणं च तत्समं दण्डमर्हति
8.e: If he does not provide a correct account of the place and time, and also the colour, form and size of the lost article, he deserves a fine equal to that article.

8.s: ādadītātha ṣaḍbhāgaṃ pranaṣṭādhigatānnṛpaḥ daśamaṃ dvādaśaṃ vā 'pi satāṃ dharmamanusmaran
8.d: आददीताथ षड्भागं प्रनष्टाधिगतान्नृपः दशमं द्वादशं वा ऽपि सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन्
8.e: Property that has been lost and found should remain in the charge of specially deputed (officials); and the thieves that he may detect in connection with this, the king shall cause to be killed by an elephant.

8.s: pranaṣṭādhigataṃ dravyaṃ tiṣṭhedyuktairadhiṣṭhitam yāṃstatra caurān gṛhṇīyāt tān rājaibhena ghātayet
8.d: प्रनष्टाधिगतं द्रव्यं तिष्ठेद्युक्तैरधिष्ठितम् यांस्तत्र चौरान् गृह्णीयात् तान् राजैभेन घातयेत्
8.e: Out of the property that has been lost and found, the king, remembering the duty of good men, shall take the sixth part, or the tenth, or the twelfth.

8.s: mamāyamiti yo brūyānnidhiṃ satyena mānavaḥ tasyādadīta ṣaḍbhāgaṃ rājā dvādaśameva vā
8.d: ममायमिति यो ब्रूयान्निधिं सत्येन मानवः तस्याददीत षड्भागं राजा द्वादशमेव वा
8.e: In regard to a treasure-trove, if a man says truly ‘this is mine,’—from him the king shall take the sixth part, or only the twelfth part.

8.s: anṛtaṃ tu vadan daṇḍyaḥ svavittasyāṃśamaṣṭamam tasyaiva vā nidhānasya saṅkhyayā 'lpīyasīṃ kalām
8.d: अनृतं तु वदन् दण्ड्यः स्ववित्तस्यांशमष्टमम् तस्यैव वा निधानस्य सङ्ख्यया ऽल्पीयसीं कलाम्
8.e: But he who speaks falsely shall, be fined the eighth part of his property, or a smaller fraction, on calculation, of that same treasure-trove.

8.s: vidvāṃstu brāhmaṇo dṛṣṭvā pūrvaupanihitaṃ nidhim aśeṣato 'pyādadīta sarvasyādhipatirhi saḥ
8.d: विद्वांस्तु ब्राह्मणो दृष्ट्वा पूर्वौपनिहितं निधिम् अशेषतो ऽप्याददीत सर्वस्याधिपतिर्हि सः
8.e: A learned Brāhmaṇa, having found treasure buried by his forefathers, shall take it wholly; as he is the master of everything.

8.s: yaṃ tu paśyennidhiṃ rājā purāṇaṃ nihitaṃ kṣitau tasmāddvijebhyo dattvā 'rdhamardhaṃ kośe praveśayet
8.d: यं तु पश्येन्निधिं राजा पुराणं निहितं क्षितौ तस्माद्द्विजेभ्यो दत्त्वा ऽर्धमर्धं कोशे प्रवेशयेत्
8.e: When the king himself finds a hoard buried of old under the ground, he shall give one-half of it to the Brāhmaṇas and have the other half put in his treasury.

8.s: nidhīnāṃ tu purāṇānāṃ dhātūnāmeva ca kṣitau ardhabhāg rakṣaṇādrājā bhūmeradhipatirhi saḥ
8.d: निधीनां तु पुराणानां धातूनामेव च क्षितौ अर्धभाग् रक्षणाद्राजा भूमेरधिपतिर्हि सः
8.e: Of ancient hoards, as also of minerals under the ground, the king is entitled to his share, by reason of his protecting them,—he being the lord of the soil.

8.s: dātavyaṃ sarvavarṇebhyo rājñā caurairhṛtaṃ dhanam rājā tadupayuñjānaścaurasyāpnoti kilbiṣam
8.d: दातव्यं सर्ववर्णेभ्यो राज्ञा चौरैर्हृतं धनम् राजा तदुपयुञ्जानश्चौरस्याप्नोति किल्बिषम्
8.e: Property stolen by thieves should be restored by the king to men of all castes; by retaining such property, the king imbibes the sin of the thief.

8.s: jātijānapadān dharmān śreṇīdharmāṃśca dharmavit samīkṣya kuladharmāṃśca svadharmaṃ pratipādayet
8.d: जातिजानपदान् धर्मान् श्रेणीधर्मांश्च धर्मवित् समीक्ष्य कुलधर्मांश्च स्वधर्मं प्रतिपादयेत्
8.e: The king knowing his duty shall determine the law for each man, after haying duly examined the provincial laws pertaining to each caste, the law’s of guilds, as also the laws of families.

8.s: svāni karmāṇi kurvāṇā dūre santo 'pi mānavāḥ priyā bhavanti lokasya sve sve karmaṇyavasthitāḥ
8.d: स्वानि कर्माणि कुर्वाणा दूरे सन्तो ऽपि मानवाः प्रिया भवन्ति लोकस्य स्वे स्वे कर्मण्यवस्थिताः
8.e: For men following their respective occupations,—even though living at a distance,—come to be liked by the people, while they remain firm in their own duties.

8.s: nautpādayet svayaṃ kāryaṃ rājā nāpyasya puruṣaḥ na ca prāpitamanyena grasedarthaṃ kathaṃ cana grasetārthaṃ
8.d: नौत्पादयेत् स्वयं कार्यं राजा नाप्यस्य पुरुषः न च प्रापितमन्येन ग्रसेदर्थं कथं चन ग्रसेतार्थं
8.e: Neither the king himself nor any servant of his shall promote a suit; nor shall he suppress a suit that has been brought up by another person.

8.s: yathā nayatyasṛkpātairmṛgasya mṛgayuḥ padam nayet tathā 'numānena dharmasya nṛpatiḥ padam
8.d: यथा नयत्यसृक्पातैर्मृगस्य मृगयुः पदम् नयेत् तथा ऽनुमानेन धर्मस्य नृपतिः पदम्
8.e: Just as the hunter discovers the foot-print of the deer by the drops of blood, so should the king discover the right by means of inference.

8.s: satyamarthaṃ ca saṃpaśyedātmānamatha sākṣiṇaḥ sākṣiṇam deśaṃ rūpaṃ ca kālaṃ ca vyavahāravidhau sthitaḥ
8.d: सत्यमर्थं च संपश्येदात्मानमथ साक्षिणः साक्षिणम् देशं रूपं च कालं च व्यवहारविधौ स्थितः
8.e: When engaged in judicial proceedings, the king shall keep his eye upon the truth, upon the object, upon himself, the witness and upon the place, the time and the aspect.

8.s: sadbhirācaritaṃ yat syāddhārmikaiśca dvijātibhiḥ taddeśakulajātīnāmaviruddhaṃ prakalpayet
8.d: सद्भिराचरितं यत् स्याद्धार्मिकैश्च द्विजातिभिः तद्देशकुलजातीनामविरुद्धं प्रकल्पयेत्
8.e: What may be found to have been observed in practice by the good and the righteous twice-born men, that he shall ordain for countries, families and castes,—provided that it is not antagonistic.

8.s: adhamarṇārthasiddhyarthamuttamarṇena coditaḥ dāpayeddhanikasyārthamadhamarṇādvibhāvitam
8.d: अधमर्णार्थसिद्ध्यर्थमुत्तमर्णेन चोदितः दापयेद्धनिकस्यार्थमधमर्णाद्विभावितम्
8.e: On being prayed by the creditor for the recovery of money from the debtor, he shall make the debtor pay to the creditor the money proved to be due.

8.s: yairyairupāyairarthaṃ svaṃ prāpnuyāduttamarṇikaḥ tairtairupāyaiḥ saṅgṛhya dāpayedadhamarṇikam
8.d: यैर्यैरुपायैरर्थं स्वं प्राप्नुयादुत्तमर्णिकः तैर्तैरुपायैः सङ्गृह्य दापयेदधमर्णिकम्
8.e: Having determined the means by which the debtor may be able to get his money, he shall, by those same means, make the debtor pay up.

8.s: dharmeṇa vyavahāreṇa chalenācaritena ca prayuktaṃ sādhayedarthaṃ pañcamena balena ca
8.d: धर्मेण व्यवहारेण छलेनाचरितेन च प्रयुक्तं साधयेदर्थं पञ्चमेन बलेन च
8.e: He shall make the advanced money repaid by means of (a) good faith, (b) tactful transaction, (c) trick, (d) moral pressure, and (c) force, the fifth.

8.s: yaḥ svayaṃ sādhayedarthamuttamarṇo 'dhamarṇikāt na sa rājñā 'bhiyoktavyaḥ svakaṃ saṃsādhayan dhanam
8.d: यः स्वयं साधयेदर्थमुत्तमर्णो ऽधमर्णिकात् न स राज्ञा ऽभियोक्तव्यः स्वकं संसाधयन् धनम्
8.e: The creditor who shall himself recover his money from the debtor should not be prosecuted by the king, for recovering what is his own property.

8.s: arthe 'pavyayamānaṃ tu karaṇena vibhāvitam dāpayeddhanikasyārthaṃ daṇḍaleśaṃ ca śaktitaḥ
8.d: अर्थे ऽपव्ययमानं तु करणेन विभावितम् दापयेद्धनिकस्यार्थं दण्डलेशं च शक्तितः
8.e: The man who denies a debt shall be made to pay the creditor’s due, proved by evidence, as also a small fine, according to his means.

8.s: apahnave 'dhamarṇasya dehītyuktasya saṃsadi abhiyoktā diśeddeśyaṃ karaṇaṃ vā 'nyaduddiśet
8.d: अपह्नवे ऽधमर्णस्य देहीत्युक्तस्य संसदि अभियोक्ता दिशेद्देश्यं करणं वा ऽन्यदुद्दिशेत्
8.e: On denial by the debtor, when asked in court to pay the debt, the complainant shall produce a witness, or adduce (other) evidence.

8.s: adeśyaṃ yaśca diśati nirdiśyāpahnute ca yaḥ yaścādharauttarānarthān vigītānnāvabudhyate
8.d: अदेश्यं यश्च दिशति निर्दिश्यापह्नुते च यः यश्चाधरौत्तरानर्थान् विगीतान्नावबुध्यते
8.e: He who mentions the wrong place,—or who, having mentioned it, retracts,—or who does not understand that his previous and subsequent statements are contradictory;

8.s: apadiśyāpadeśyaṃ ca punaryastvapadhāvati 'padiśyāpadeśaṃ samyak praṇihitaṃ cārthaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ sannābhinandati
8.d: अपदिश्यापदेश्यं च पुनर्यस्त्वपधावति ऽपदिश्यापदेशं सम्यक् प्रणिहितं चार्थं पृष्टः सन्नाभिनन्दति
8.e: He who, having put forward a statement, subsequently retracts; and who on being questioned regarding a fact (previously) duly alleged, does not support it;

8.s: asaṃbhāṣye sākṣibhiśca deśe saṃbhāṣate mithaḥ nirucyamānaṃ praśnaṃ ca naicchedyaścāpi niṣpatet
8.d: असंभाष्ये साक्षिभिश्च देशे संभाषते मिथः निरुच्यमानं प्रश्नं च नैच्छेद्यश्चापि निष्पतेत्
8.e: He who secretly converses with the witnesses in a place not fit for conversation, or who does not like the question being investigated, or who falls back;

8.s: brūhītyuktaśca na brūyāduktaṃ ca na vibhāvayet na ca pūrvāparaṃ vidyāt tasmādarthāt sa hīyate
8.d: ब्रूहीत्युक्तश्च न ब्रूयादुक्तं च न विभावयेत् न च पूर्वापरं विद्यात् तस्मादर्थात् स हीयते
8.e: —He who, on being ordered to speak, does not speak; or who does not prove what he has asserted;—or who does not grasp the previous and subsequent statements;—such a person fails in that suit.

8.s: sākṣiṇaḥ santi metyuktvā diśaityukto diśenna yaḥ jñātāraḥ santi mety*] * dharmasthaḥ kāraṇairetairhīnaṃ tamapi nirdiśet tamiti nirdiśet
8.d: साक्षिणः सन्ति मेत्युक्त्वा दिशैत्युक्तो दिशेन्न यः ज्ञातारः सन्ति मेत्य्*] * धर्मस्थः कारणैरेतैर्हीनं तमपि निर्दिशेत् तमिति निर्दिशेत्
8.e: Having asserted that he has witnesses, and on being asked to name them, if he does not name them,—him also, on these grounds, the judge shall declare to have failed in his suit.

8.s: abhiyoktā na cedbrūyādbadhyo daṇḍyaśca dharmataḥ bandhyo daṇḍyaśca na cet tripakṣāt prabrūyāddharmaṃ prati parājitaḥ
8.d: अभियोक्ता न चेद्ब्रूयाद्बध्यो दण्ड्यश्च धर्मतः बन्ध्यो दण्ड्यश्च न चेत् त्रिपक्षात् प्रब्रूयाद्धर्मं प्रति पराजितः
8.e: If the complainant does not speak out, he shall be imprisoned and pined, according to law. If the other party does not answer within three fortnights, he becomes defeated according to law.

8.s: yo yāvatnihnuvītārthaṃ mithyā yāvati vā vadet tau nṛpeṇa hyadharmajñau dāpyo taddviguṇaṃ damam
8.d: यो यावत्निह्नुवीतार्थं मिथ्या यावति वा वदेत् तौ नृपेण ह्यधर्मज्ञौ दाप्यो तद्द्विगुणं दमम्
8.e: If one falsely denies a debt, or if the other falsely demands it,—these two, proficient in dishonesty, should be made by the king to pay a fine double that sum.

8.s: pṛṣṭo 'pavyayamānastu kṛtāvastho dhaneṣiṇā tryavaraiḥ sākṣibhirbhāvyo nṛpabrāhmaṇasaṃnidhau
8.d: पृष्टो ऽपव्ययमानस्तु कृतावस्थो धनेषिणा त्र्यवरैः साक्षिभिर्भाव्यो नृपब्राह्मणसंनिधौ
8.e: On having been summoned and questioned, if one denies it,—then he siiall be convicted by the man seeking for his due by means of at least three witnesses, in the presence of the king and the brāhmaṇas.

8.s: yādṛśā dhanibhiḥ kāryā vyavahāreṣu sākṣiṇaḥ tādṛśān saṃpravakṣyāmi yathā vācyaṃ ṛtaṃ ca taiḥ
8.d: यादृशा धनिभिः कार्या व्यवहारेषु साक्षिणः तादृशान् संप्रवक्ष्यामि यथा वाच्यं ऋतं च तैः
8.e: I shall declare now what sort of persons should be made witnesses in suits by wealthy men, and how the truth should be told by them.

8.s: gṛhiṇaḥ putriṇo maulāḥ kṣatraviśśūdrayonayaḥ arthyuktāḥ sākṣyamarhanti na ye ke cidanāpadi
8.d: गृहिणः पुत्रिणो मौलाः क्षत्रविश्शूद्रयोनयः अर्थ्युक्ताः साक्ष्यमर्हन्ति न ये के चिदनापदि
8.e: Householders, men with sons, respectable natives, and men of the kṣatriya, vaiśya and śūdra castes are competent to act as witnesses, when cited by suitors;—and not any and every person, except in emergencies.

8.s: āptāḥ sarveṣu varṇeṣu kāryāḥ kāryeṣu sākṣiṇaḥ sarvadharmavido 'lubdhā viparītāṃstu varjayet
8.d: आप्ताः सर्वेषु वर्णेषु कार्याः कार्येषु साक्षिणः सर्वधर्मविदो ऽलुब्धा विपरीतांस्तु वर्जयेत्
8.e: In all law-suits trustworthy men of all the castes, fully conversant with morality and free from avarice, should be made witnesses; the reverse of these should be avoided.

8.s: nārthasaṃbandhino nāptā na sahāyā na vairiṇaḥ na dṛṣṭadoṣāḥ kartavyā na vyādhyārtā na dūṣitāḥ
8.d: नार्थसंबन्धिनो नाप्ता न सहाया न वैरिणः न दृष्टदोषाः कर्तव्या न व्याध्यार्ता न दूषिताः
8.e: Neither interested persons, nor relations, nor helpers, nor enemies, nor persons of proved corruption, nor those afflicted with disease, nor the corrupted should be made witnesses.

8.s: na sākṣī nṛpatiḥ kāryo na kārukakuśīlavau na śrotriyo na liṅgastho na saṅgebhyo vinirgataḥ
8.d: न साक्षी नृपतिः कार्यो न कारुककुशीलवौ न श्रोत्रियो न लिङ्गस्थो न सङ्गेभ्यो विनिर्गतः
8.e: The king should not be made a witness; nor craftsmen, nor actors, nor a Vedic scholar, nor one in holy orders, nor one who has renounced all attachments.

8.s: nādhyadhīno na vaktavyo na dasyurna vikarmakṛt na vṛddho na śiśurnaiko nāntyo na vikalaindriyaḥ
8.d: नाध्यधीनो न वक्तव्यो न दस्युर्न विकर्मकृत् न वृद्धो न शिशुर्नैको नान्त्यो न विकलैन्द्रियः
8.e: —Not one wholly dependent, nor one under pupilage, nor a paid servant, nor one who adopts forbidden occupations, nor one too old, nor a minor, nor a single person, nor one belonging to the lowest class, nor one with defective organs;

8.s: nārto na matto naunmatto na kṣuttṛṣṇaupapīḍitaḥ na śramārto na kāmārto na kruddho nāpi taskaraḥ
8.d: नार्तो न मत्तो नौन्मत्तो न क्षुत्तृष्णौपपीडितः न श्रमार्तो न कामार्तो न क्रुद्धो नापि तस्करः
8.e: —Nor one afflicted, nor one intoxicated, nor one demented, nor one tormented by hunger and thirst, nor one oppressed by fatigue, nor one tormented by love, nor one who is in a rage, nor a thief.

8.s: strīṇāṃ sākṣyaṃ striyaḥ kuryurdvijānāṃ sadṛśā dvijāḥ śūdrāśca santaḥ śūdrāṇāṃ antyānāmantyayonayaḥ
8.d: स्त्रीणां साक्ष्यं स्त्रियः कुर्युर्द्विजानां सदृशा द्विजाः शूद्राश्च सन्तः शूद्राणां अन्त्यानामन्त्ययोनयः
8.e: —Woman should give evidence for women; and for twice-born persons similar twice-born men, virtuous śūdhas for śūdras, and men of the lowest caste for the lowest men.

8.s: anubhāvī tu yaḥ kaścit kuryāt sākṣyaṃ vivādinām antarveśmanyaraṇye vā śarīrasyāpi cātyaye
8.d: अनुभावी तु यः कश्चित् कुर्यात् साक्ष्यं विवादिनाम् अन्तर्वेश्मन्यरण्ये वा शरीरस्यापि चात्यये
8.e: In the case of anything done in the interior of a house, or in a forest, or in the case of injury to the body,—any person who may be cognisant of the facts may give evidence on behalf of the parties to the suit.

8.s: striyā 'pyasaṃbhāve kāryaṃ bālena sthavireṇa vā śiṣyeṇa bandhunā vā 'pi dāsena bhṛtakena vā
8.d: स्त्रिया ऽप्यसंभावे कार्यं बालेन स्थविरेण वा शिष्येण बन्धुना वा ऽपि दासेन भृतकेन वा
8.e: In the event of (proper witnesses) not forthcoming, evidence may be given by a woman, by a minor, by an aged person, by a pupil, by a relative, by a slave, or by a servant.

8.s: bālavṛddhāturāṇāṃ ca sākṣyeṣu vadatāṃ mṛṣā jānīyādasthirāṃ vācamutsiktamanasāṃ tathā
8.d: बालवृद्धातुराणां च साक्ष्येषु वदतां मृषा जानीयादस्थिरां वाचमुत्सिक्तमनसां तथा
8.e: In the event of minors, aged and diseased persons deposing falsely in their evidence, the Judge should make up his mind regarding the speech being irregular; so also in the case of men with disordered minds.

8.s: sāhaseṣu ca sarveṣu steyasaṅgrahaṇeṣu ca vāgdaṇḍayośca pāruṣye na parīkṣeta sākṣiṇaḥ
8.d: साहसेषु च सर्वेषु स्तेयसङ्ग्रहणेषु च वाग्दण्डयोश्च पारुष्ये न परीक्षेत साक्षिणः
8.e: In all cases of violence, of theft and adultery, and of assault, verbal and corporeal,—he shall not investigate the character of the witnesses.

8.s: bahutvaṃ parigṛhṇīyāt sākṣidvaidhe narādhipaḥ sameṣu tu guṇautkṛṣṭān guṇidvaidhe dvijottamān
8.d: बहुत्वं परिगृह्णीयात् साक्षिद्वैधे नराधिपः समेषु तु गुणौत्कृष्टान् गुणिद्वैधे द्विजोत्तमान्
8.e: On a conflict among witnesses, the king shall accept the majority; in the case of equality (of number) those possessed of superior qualifications; and in the case of conflict between equally qualified witnesses, the best among the twice-born.

8.s: samakṣadarśanāt sākṣyaṃ śravaṇāccaiva sidhyati tatra satyaṃ bruvan sākṣī dharmārthābhyāṃ na hīyate
8.d: समक्षदर्शनात् साक्ष्यं श्रवणाच्चैव सिध्यति तत्र सत्यं ब्रुवन् साक्षी धर्मार्थाभ्यां न हीयते
8.e: Evidence based upon what is directly seen and is heard is admissible; and a witness, telling the truth in such cases, does not fall off from spiritual merit or worldly prosperity.

8.s: sākṣī dṛṣṭaśrutādanyadvibruvannāryasaṃsadi avālg narakamabhyeti pretya svargācca hīyate
8.d: साक्षी दृष्टश्रुतादन्यद्विब्रुवन्नार्यसंसदि अवाल्ग् नरकमभ्येति प्रेत्य स्वर्गाच्च हीयते
8.e: A witness asserting, in an assembly of noble men, anything apart from what he has seen and heard, falls downwards into hell after death and becomes shut out from heaven.

8.s: yatrānibaddho 'pīkṣeta śṛṇuyādvā 'pi kiṃ cana pṛṣṭastatrāpi tadbrūyādyathādṛṣṭaṃ yathāśrutam
8.d: यत्रानिबद्धो ऽपीक्षेत शृणुयाद्वा ऽपि किं चन पृष्टस्तत्रापि तद्ब्रूयाद्यथादृष्टं यथाश्रुतम्
8.e: Even though not put down as a witness, if a person happens to see or hear anything in regard to a case,—when he comes to be questioned about it, he should speak out exactly as he has seen or heard it.

8.s: eko 'lubdhastu sākṣī syādbahvyaḥ śucyo 'pi na striyaḥ tvasākṣī strībuddherasthiratvāt tu doṣaiścānye 'pi ye vṛtāḥ
8.d: एको ऽलुब्धस्तु साक्षी स्याद्बह्व्यः शुच्यो ऽपि न स्त्रियः त्वसाक्षी स्त्रीबुद्धेरस्थिरत्वात् तु दोषैश्चान्ये ऽपि ये वृताः
8.e: A single man, free from covetousness, may be a witness, but not many women, even though pure,—because the understanding of women is not steady,—nor other men who are tainted with defects.

8.s: svabhāvenaiva yadbrūyustadgrāhyaṃ vyāvahārikam ato yadanyadvibrūyurdharmārthaṃ tadapārthakam
8.d: स्वभावेनैव यद्ब्रूयुस्तद्ग्राह्यं व्यावहारिकम् अतो यदन्यद्विब्रूयुर्धर्मार्थं तदपार्थकम्
8.e: What the witnesses state naturally, in relation to the case, should be accepted; apart from this what they state from considerations of righteousness, is useless.

8.s: sabhāntaḥ sākṣiṇaḥ prāptānarthipratyarthisaṃnidhau prāḍvivāko 'nuyuñjīta vidhinā 'nena sāntvayan
8.d: सभान्तः साक्षिणः प्राप्तानर्थिप्रत्यर्थिसंनिधौ प्राड्विवाको ऽनुयुञ्जीत विधिना ऽनेन सान्त्वयन्
8.e: The investigating Judge shall question the witnesses assembled in the court, in the presence of the plaintiff and the defendant, gently exhorting them in the following manner.

8.s: yaddvayoranayorvettha kārye 'smiṃśceṣṭitaṃ mithaḥ tadbrūta sarvaṃ satyena yuṣmākaṃ hyatra sākṣitā
8.d: यद्द्वयोरनयोर्वेत्थ कार्ये ऽस्मिंश्चेष्टितं मिथः तद्ब्रूत सर्वं सत्येन युष्माकं ह्यत्र साक्षिता
8.e: ‘What you know of the mutual transaction between these two persons regarding this suit,—all that may you declare freely; since you are witnesses in this matter.’

8.s: satyaṃ sākṣye bruvan sākṣī lokān āpnoty puṣkalān āpnotyaninditān iha cānuttamāṃ kīrtiṃ vāgeṣā brahmapūjitā
8.d: सत्यं साक्ष्ये ब्रुवन् साक्षी लोकान् आप्नोत्य् पुष्कलान् आप्नोत्यनिन्दितान् इह चानुत्तमां कीर्तिं वागेषा ब्रह्मपूजिता
8.e: ‘The witness, telling the truth in his evidence, attains irreproachable regions, also unsurpassable fame; such speech is honoured by Brahmā himself.—(81)’

8.s: sākṣye 'nṛtaṃ vadan pāśairbadhyate vāruṇairbhṛśam vivaśaḥ śatamājātīstasmāt sākṣyaṃ vadedṛtam
8.d: साक्ष्ये ऽनृतं वदन् पाशैर्बध्यते वारुणैर्भृशम् विवशः शतमाजातीस्तस्मात् साक्ष्यं वदेदृतम्
8.e: ‘Stating the untruth in his evidence, he becomes firmly bound in Varuṇa’s fetters, helpless during a hundred births. One should, therefore, give true evidence.’

8.s: satyena pūyate sākṣī dharmaḥ satyena vardhate tasmāt satyaṃ hi vaktavyaṃ sarvavarṇeṣu sākṣibhiḥ
8.d: सत्येन पूयते साक्षी धर्मः सत्येन वर्धते तस्मात् सत्यं हि वक्तव्यं सर्ववर्णेषु साक्षिभिः
8.e: ‘By truth is the witness purified, by truth does merit grow: hence the truth should be spoken by witnesses of all castes.’

8.s: ātmaiva hyātmanaḥ sākṣī gatirātmā tathā 'tmanaḥ mā 'vamaṃsthāḥ svamātmānaṃ nṛṇāṃ sākṣiṇamuttamam
8.d: आत्मैव ह्यात्मनः साक्षी गतिरात्मा तथा ऽत्मनः मा ऽवमंस्थाः स्वमात्मानं नृणां साक्षिणमुत्तमम्
8.e: ‘The soul itself is the soul’s witness, and the soul itself is the soul’s refuge; disregard not your soul, the best witness of man.’

8.s: manyante vai pāpakṛto na kaścit paśyatīti naḥ tāṃstu devāḥ prapaśyanti svasyaivāntarapūruṣaḥ
8.d: मन्यन्ते वै पापकृतो न कश्चित् पश्यतीति नः तांस्तु देवाः प्रपश्यन्ति स्वस्यैवान्तरपूरुषः
8.e: ‘The sinners indeed think that “no one sees us”; but the gods see them, as also their own inner personality.’

8.s: dyaurbhūmirāpo hṛdayaṃ candrārkāgniyamānilāḥ rātriḥ saṃdhye ca dharmaśca vṛttajñāḥ sarvadehinām
8.d: द्यौर्भूमिरापो हृदयं चन्द्रार्काग्नियमानिलाः रात्रिः संध्ये च धर्मश्च वृत्तज्ञाः सर्वदेहिनाम्
8.e: ‘Heaven, earth, water, heart, moon, sun, fire, death-god, wind, night, the two twilights, and morality know the conduct of all corporeal beings.’

8.s: devabrāhmaṇasāṃnidhye sākṣyaṃ pṛcchedṛtaṃ dvijān udalgmukhān prālgmukhān vā pūrvāhṇe vai śuciḥ śucīn
8.d: देवब्राह्मणसांनिध्ये साक्ष्यं पृच्छेदृतं द्विजान् उदल्ग्मुखान् प्राल्ग्मुखान् वा पूर्वाह्णे वै शुचिः शुचीन्
8.e: In the presence of gods and Brāhmaṇas, during forenoon, the judge, pure himself, shall ask the twice-born persons, who have been purified and are facing either the north or the east, to give evidence.

8.s: brūhīti brāhmaṇaṃ pṛcchet satyaṃ brūhīti pārthivam gobījakāñcanairvaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ sarvaistu pātakaiḥ
8.d: ब्रूहीति ब्राह्मणं पृच्छेत् सत्यं ब्रूहीति पार्थिवम् गोबीजकाञ्चनैर्वैश्यं शूद्रं सर्वैस्तु पातकैः
8.e: He shall question the Brāhmaṇa with the word ‘speak,’ the Kṣatriya with ‘speak out the truth,’ the Vaiśya by sins pertaining to kine, grain and food, and the Śūdra by all the sins.

8.s: brahmaghno ye smṛtā lokā ye ca strībālaghātinaḥ mitradruhaḥ kṛtaghnasya te te syurbruvato mṛṣā
8.d: ब्रह्मघ्नो ये स्मृता लोका ये च स्त्रीबालघातिनः मित्रद्रुहः कृतघ्नस्य ते ते स्युर्ब्रुवतो मृषा
8.e: ‘Whatever regions have been assigned to the slayer of the Brāhmaṇa, to the murderer of women and children, to the betrayer of friends and to the ingrate,—those same shall be thine if thou speakest falsely.’

8.s: janmaprabhṛti yat kiṃ cit puṇyaṃ bhadra tvayā kṛtam tat te sarvaṃ śuno gacchedyadi brūyāstvamanyathā
8.d: जन्मप्रभृति यत् किं चित् पुण्यं भद्र त्वया कृतम् तत् ते सर्वं शुनो गच्छेद्यदि ब्रूयास्त्वमन्यथा
8.e: ‘Whatever merit, good man, you may have acquired since your birth, would go to the dogs, if you speak falsely.’

8.s: eko 'hamasmītyātmānaṃ yastvaṃ kalyāṇa manyase nityaṃ sthitaste hṛdyeṣa puṇyapāpaikṣitā muniḥ
8.d: एको ऽहमस्मीत्यात्मानं यस्त्वं कल्याण मन्यसे नित्यं स्थितस्ते हृद्येष पुण्यपापैक्षिता मुनिः
8.e: ‘You think yourself, blessed man, that “I am alone”; but there ever sits in your heart the silent watcher of virtue and vice.’

8.s: yamo vaivasvato devo yastavaiṣa hṛdi sthitaḥ tena cedavivādaste mā gaṅgāṃ mā kurūn gamaḥ
8.d: यमो वैवस्वतो देवो यस्तवैष हृदि स्थितः तेन चेदविवादस्ते मा गङ्गां मा कुरून् गमः
8.e: ‘The, god Yama, the son of Vivasvat, who sits in your heart,—if you have no quarrel with him, you need not visit the Gaṅgā, nor the Kurus.

8.s: nagno muṇḍaḥ kapālena ca bhikṣārthī kṣutpipāsitaḥ kapālī andhaḥ śatrukulaṃ gacchedyaḥ sākṣyamanṛtaṃ vadet
8.d: नग्नो मुण्डः कपालेन च भिक्षार्थी क्षुत्पिपासितः कपाली अन्धः शत्रुकुलं गच्छेद्यः साक्ष्यमनृतं वदेत्
8.e: ‘He who gives false evidence shall go for alms, with a potsherd, to the house of his enemy,—naked and shorn, tormented with hunger and thirst, and blind.’

8.s: avākṣirāstamasyandhe kilbiṣī narakaṃ vrajet yaḥ praśnaṃ vitathaṃ brūyāt pṛṣṭaḥ san dharmaniścaye
8.d: अवाक्षिरास्तमस्यन्धे किल्बिषी नरकं व्रजेत् यः प्रश्नं वितथं ब्रूयात् पृष्टः सन् धर्मनिश्चये
8.e: ‘Headlong, in blind darkness shall the sinner fall into hell, who, on being interrogated in the course of a judicial investigation, answers the question falsely.

8.s: andho matsyānivāśnāti sa naraḥ kaṇṭakaiḥ saha yo bhāṣate 'rthavaikalyamapratyakṣaṃ sabhāṃ gataḥ
8.d: अन्धो मत्स्यानिवाश्नाति स नरः कण्टकैः सह यो भाषते ऽर्थवैकल्यमप्रत्यक्षं सभां गतः
8.e: ‘He who, having entered the court, bears testimony to what is contrary to facts and what he has not seen, swallows fish along with the bones,—just like a blind man.’

8.s: yasya vidvān hi vadataḥ kṣetrajño nābhiśaṅkate nātiśaṅkate tasmānna devāḥ śreyāṃsaṃ loke 'nyaṃ puruṣaṃ viduḥ
8.d: यस्य विद्वान् हि वदतः क्षेत्रज्ञो नाभिशङ्कते नातिशङ्कते तस्मान्न देवाः श्रेयांसं लोके ऽन्यं पुरुषं विदुः
8.e: ‘The gods do not regard any person in this world as superior to him, whom his knowing soul does not distrust, while he is speaking.’

8.s: yāvato bāndhavān yasmin hanti sākṣye 'nṛtaṃ vadan tāvataḥ saṅkhyayā tasmin śṛṇu saumyānupūrvaśaḥ
8.d: यावतो बान्धवान् यस्मिन् हन्ति साक्ष्ये ऽनृतं वदन् तावतः सङ्ख्यया तस्मिन् शृणु सौम्यानुपूर्वशः
8.e: ‘Listen now, gentle friend, in due order, how many relatives, by number, one destroys by giving false evidence, in what cases.’

8.s: pañca paśuanṛte hanti daśa hanti gavānṛte śatamaśvānṛte hanti sahasraṃ puruṣānṛte
8.d: पञ्च पशुअनृते हन्ति दश हन्ति गवानृते शतमश्वानृते हन्ति सहस्रं पुरुषानृते
8.e: ‘He destroys five by false evidence regarding animals; he destroys ten by false evidence regarding kine; he destroys a hundred by false evidence regarding horses, and a thousand by false evidence regarding men.’

8.s: hanti jātānajātāṃśca hiraṇyārthe 'nṛtaṃ vadan sarvaṃ bhūmianṛte hanti mā sma bhūmianṛtaṃ vadīḥ
8.d: हन्ति जातानजातांश्च हिरण्यार्थे ऽनृतं वदन् सर्वं भूमिअनृते हन्ति मा स्म भूमिअनृतं वदीः
8.e: ‘Deposing falsely in regard to gold, he kills the born as well as the unborn; by false evidence regarding land, he kills all; never tell a lie regarding land.’

8.s: apsu bhūmivadityāhuḥ strīṇāṃ bhoge ca maithune abjeṣu caiva ratneṣu sarveṣvaśmamayeṣu ca
8.d: अप्सु भूमिवदित्याहुः स्त्रीणां भोगे च मैथुने अब्जेषु चैव रत्नेषु सर्वेष्वश्ममयेषु च
8.e: ‘That concerning water they declare to be similar to that concerning land; as also that relating to the sexual enjoyment of women, and to gems, water-born as well as granitic.’

8.s: etān doṣānavekṣya tvaṃ sarvānanṛtabhāṣaṇe yathāśrutaṃ yathādṛṣṭaṃ sarvamevāñjasā vada
8.d: एतान् दोषानवेक्ष्य त्वं सर्वाननृतभाषणे यथाश्रुतं यथादृष्टं सर्वमेवाञ्जसा वद
8.e: ‘Having noticed all these evils proceeding prom perjury, speak out directly everything exactly what you have seen and heard.’

8.s: gorakṣakān vāṇijikāṃḥ tathā kārukuśīlavān vāṇijakāṃs preṣyān vārdhuṣikāṃścaiva viprān śūdravadācaret
8.d: गोरक्षकान् वाणिजिकांः तथा कारुकुशीलवान् वाणिजकांस् प्रेष्यान् वार्धुषिकांश्चैव विप्रान् शूद्रवदाचरेत्
8.e: ‘He shall treat like Śūdras the Brāhmaṇas who tend cattle, who engage in trade, and who are craftsmen, actors, menial servants ok money-lenders.’

8.s: tadvadan dharmato 'rtheṣu jānannapyanythā naraḥ na svargāccyavate lokāddaivīṃ vācaṃ vadanti tām
8.d: तद्वदन् धर्मतो ऽर्थेषु जानन्नप्यन्य्था नरः न स्वर्गाच्च्यवते लोकाद्दैवीं वाचं वदन्ति ताम्
8.e: In some cases, a man who, though knowing the truth, deposes otherwise, through piety, does not fall off from heaven. This is a divine assertion that they reproduce.

8.s: śūdraviśkṣatraviprāṇāṃ yatraṛtauktau bhavedvadhaḥ tatra vaktavyamanṛtaṃ taddhi satyādviśiṣyate
8.d: शूद्रविश्क्षत्रविप्राणां यत्रऋतौक्तौ भवेद्वधः तत्र वक्तव्यमनृतं तद्धि सत्याद्विशिष्यते
8.e: Where the telling of the truth would lead to the death of a Śūdra, a Vaiśva, a Kṣatriya or a Brāhmaṇa,—in that case falsehood should be spoken; as that is preferable to truth.

8.s: vācdaivatyaiśca carubhiryajeraṃste sarasvatīm anṛtasyainasastasya kurvāṇā niṣkṛtiṃ parām
8.d: वाच्दैवत्यैश्च चरुभिर्यजेरंस्ते सरस्वतीम् अनृतस्यैनसस्तस्य कुर्वाणा निष्कृतिं पराम्
8.e: They should offer sacrifices to Sarasvati with half-boiled rice dedicated to the speech-goddess,—doing the best expiation for the sin of untruthfulness.

8.s: kūṣmāṇḍairvā 'pi juhuyādghṛtamagnau yathāvidhi udity ṛcā vā vāruṇyā tṛcenāpdaivatena vā
8.d: कूष्माण्डैर्वा ऽपि जुहुयाद्घृतमग्नौ यथाविधि उदित्य् ऋचा वा वारुण्या तृचेनाप्दैवतेन वा
8.e: Or he shall offer according to rule, clarified butter into the fire, with the ‘kuṣmāṇḍa’-texts or with the verse ‘ut, etc.’ sacred to varuṇa, or with the three verses sacred to the waters.

8.s: tripakṣādabruvan sākṣyaṃ ṛṇādiṣu naro 'gadaḥ tadṛṇaṃ prāpnuyāt sarvaṃ daśabandhaṃ ca sarvataḥ
8.d: त्रिपक्षादब्रुवन् साक्ष्यं ऋणादिषु नरो ऽगदः तदृणं प्राप्नुयात् सर्वं दशबन्धं च सर्वतः
8.e: The man, who, without being ill, does not give evidence for three fortnights, in regard to debts and other matters, should hear that entire debt, as also a penalty of the tenth part in all cases.

8.s: yasya dṛśyeta saptāhāduktavākyasya sākṣiṇaḥ rogo 'gnirjñātimaraṇaṃ ṛṇaṃ dāpyo damaṃ ca saḥ
8.d: यस्य दृश्येत सप्ताहादुक्तवाक्यस्य साक्षिणः रोगो ऽग्निर्ज्ञातिमरणं ऋणं दाप्यो दमं च सः
8.e: That witness,—who may be found, within a week of having given evidence, to suffer from sickness, fire or the death of a relative,—should be made to pay the debt and also the penalty.

8.s: asākṣikeṣu tvartheṣu mitho vivādamānayoḥ avindaṃstattvataḥ satyaṃ śapathenāpi lambhayet
8.d: असाक्षिकेषु त्वर्थेषु मिथो विवादमानयोः अविन्दंस्तत्त्वतः सत्यं शपथेनापि लम्भयेत्
8.e: In witness-less cases, if he cannot get at the truth between the two disputants by any means, he should discover it by means of oath.

8.s: maharṣibhiśca devaiśca kāryārthaṃ śapathāḥ kṛtāḥ vasiṣṭhaścāpi śapathaṃ śepe paijavane nṛpe
8.d: महर्षिभिश्च देवैश्च कार्यार्थं शपथाः कृताः वसिष्ठश्चापि शपथं शेपे पैजवने नृपे
8.e: By the great sages, as well as by the Gods, oaths have been taken for the purposes of a case; Vasiṣṭha even swore an oath before the King Paijavana.

8.s: na vṛthā śapathaṃ kuryāt svalpe 'pyarthe naro budhaḥ vṛthā hi śapathaṃ kurvan pretya caiha ca naśyati
8.d: न वृथा शपथं कुर्यात् स्वल्पे ऽप्यर्थे नरो बुधः वृथा हि शपथं कुर्वन् प्रेत्य चैह च नश्यति
8.e: The wise man shall not take an oath improperly; taking an improper oath, one becomes ruined here as well as after death.

8.s: kāminīṣu vivāheṣu gavāṃ bhakṣye tathaindhane brāhmaṇābhyupapattau ca śapathe nāsti pātakam
8.d: कामिनीषु विवाहेषु गवां भक्ष्ये तथैन्धने ब्राह्मणाभ्युपपत्तौ च शपथे नास्ति पातकम्
8.e: There is no serious offence in swearing to women, or in connection with marriages, fodder for cows, or fuel, or for the sake of a Brāhmaṇa.

8.s: satyena śāpayedvipraṃ kṣatriyaṃ vāhanāyudhaiḥ gobījakāñcanairvaiśyaṃ śūdraṃ sarvaistu pātakaiḥ
8.d: सत्येन शापयेद्विप्रं क्षत्रियं वाहनायुधैः गोबीजकाञ्चनैर्वैश्यं शूद्रं सर्वैस्तु पातकैः
8.e: The Brāhmaṇa should be made to swear by truth, the Kṣatriya by conveyances and weapons, the Vaiśya by cattle, grains and gold, and the Śūdra by all sins.

8.s: agniṃ vā 'hārayedenamapsu cainaṃ nimajjayet putradārasya vā 'pyenaṃ śirāṃsi sparśayet pṛthak
8.d: अग्निं वा ऽहारयेदेनमप्सु चैनं निमज्जयेत् पुत्रदारस्य वा ऽप्येनं शिरांसि स्पर्शयेत् पृथक्
8.e: Or, he may make him fetch fire, or make him dive under water, or make him touch the heads of his son and wife severally.

8.s: yamiddho na dahatyagnirāpo naunmajjayanti ca na cārtiṃ ṛcchati kṣipraṃ sa jñeyaḥ śapathe śuciḥ
8.d: यमिद्धो न दहत्यग्निरापो नौन्मज्जयन्ति च न चार्तिं ऋच्छति क्षिप्रं स ज्ञेयः शपथे शुचिः
8.e: He whom the blazing fire burns not, or whom the water does not throw up, or who does not speedily suffer some misfortune, should be regarded as pure on his oath.

8.s: vatsasya hyabhiśastasya purā bhrātrā yavīyasā nāgnirdadāha romāpi satyena jagataḥ spaśaḥ
8.d: वत्सस्य ह्यभिशस्तस्य पुरा भ्रात्रा यवीयसा नाग्निर्ददाह रोमापि सत्येन जगतः स्पशः
8.e: Formerly when Vatsa was accused by his younger brother, fire, the world’s spy, did not burn even a hair of his, because of truth.

8.s: yasmin yasmin vivāde tu kauṭasākṣyaṃ kṛtaṃ bhavet tat tat kāryaṃ nivarteta kṛtaṃ cāpyakṛtaṃ bhavet
8.d: यस्मिन् यस्मिन् विवादे तु कौटसाक्ष्यं कृतं भवेत् तत् तत् कार्यं निवर्तेत कृतं चाप्यकृतं भवेत्
8.e: In whatever suit false evidence should have been given, the effect of that shall cease, and what has been done shall be undone.

8.s: lobhātmohādbhayātmaitrāt kāmāt krodhāt tathaiva ca ajñānādbālabhāvātca sākṣyaṃ vitathamucyate
8.d: लोभात्मोहाद्भयात्मैत्रात् कामात् क्रोधात् तथैव च अज्ञानाद्बालभावात्च साक्ष्यं वितथमुच्यते
8.e: Evidence is called ‘false,’ when it is due to greed, or embarrassment, or fright, or friendship, or lust, or anger, or ignorance, ok childishness.

8.s: eṣāmanyatame sthāne yaḥ sākṣyamanṛtaṃ vadet tasya daṇḍaviśeṣāṃstu pravakṣyāmyanupūrvaśaḥ
8.d: एषामन्यतमे स्थाने यः साक्ष्यमनृतं वदेत् तस्य दण्डविशेषांस्तु प्रवक्ष्याम्यनुपूर्वशः
8.e: I am going to explain, in due order, the particular punishments for him who should give false evidence from any one of these causes.

8.s: lobhāt sahasraṃ daṇḍyastu mohāt pūrvaṃ tu sāhasam bhayāddvau madhyamau daṇḍau maitrāt pūrvaṃ caturguṇam
8.d: लोभात् सहस्रं दण्ड्यस्तु मोहात् पूर्वं तु साहसम् भयाद्द्वौ मध्यमौ दण्डौ मैत्रात् पूर्वं चतुर्गुणम्
8.e: If through greed, he should be fined a thousand; if through embarrassment, the lowest amercement; if through fear, two middlling ones; if through friendship, four times the first.

8.s: kāmāddaśaguṇaṃ pūrvaṃ krodhāt tu triguṇaṃ param ajñānāddve śate pūrṇe bāliśyātśatameva tu
8.d: कामाद्दशगुणं पूर्वं क्रोधात् तु त्रिगुणं परम् अज्ञानाद्द्वे शते पूर्णे बालिश्यात्शतमेव तु
8.e: If through lust, ten times the first; if through anger, three times the next; if through ignorance, full two hundred; and if through childishness, only a hundred.

8.s: etānāhuḥ kauṭasākṣye proktān daṇḍān manīṣibhiḥ dharmasyāvyabhicārārthamadharmaniyamāya ca
8.d: एतानाहुः कौटसाक्ष्ये प्रोक्तान् दण्डान् मनीषिभिः धर्मस्याव्यभिचारार्थमधर्मनियमाय च
8.e: They declare these penalties for false evidence to have been prescribed by the wise, for the purpose that justice may not fail and injustice hay be prevented.

8.s: kauṭasākṣyaṃ tu kurvāṇāṃstrīn varṇān dhārmiko nṛpaḥ pravāsayeddaṇḍayitvā brāhmaṇaṃ tu vivāsayet
8.d: कौटसाक्ष्यं तु कुर्वाणांस्त्रीन् वर्णान् धार्मिको नृपः प्रवासयेद्दण्डयित्वा ब्राह्मणं तु विवासयेत्
8.e: The king shall however fine and then banish the three castes giving false evidence; but the Brāhmaṇa he shall deprive of his clothes (and dwelling).

8.s: daśa sthānāni daṇḍasya manuḥ svayaṃbhuvo 'bravīt triṣu varṇeṣu yāni syurakṣato brāhmaṇo vrajet
8.d: दश स्थानानि दण्डस्य मनुः स्वयंभुवो ऽब्रवीत् त्रिषु वर्णेषु यानि स्युरक्षतो ब्राह्मणो व्रजेत्
8.e: Manu Svāyambhuva has named ten places for punishment, where it should be inflicted in the case of the three castes; but the Brāhmaṇa shall depart unscathed.

8.s: upasthamudaraṃ jihvā hastau pādau ca pañcamam cakṣurnāsā ca karṇau ca dhanaṃ dehastathaiva ca
8.d: उपस्थमुदरं जिह्वा हस्तौ पादौ च पञ्चमम् चक्षुर्नासा च कर्णौ च धनं देहस्तथैव च
8.e: (1) The genital organ, (2) the stomach, (3) the tongue, (4) the hands, (5) the feet, (6) the eye, (7) the nose, (8) the ears, (9) the property and (10) the body.

8.s: anubandhaṃ parijñāya deśakālau ca tattvataḥ sārāparādho cālokya daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyeṣu pātayet
8.d: अनुबन्धं परिज्ञाय देशकालौ च तत्त्वतः सारापराधो चालोक्य दण्डं दण्ड्येषु पातयेत्
8.e: Having duly ascertained the motive and the time and place, and having taken into consideration the condition (of the accused) and the nature of the offence,—he shall inflict punishment upon those deserving punishment.

8.s: adharmadaṇḍanaṃ loke yaśoghnaṃ kīrtināśanam asvargyaṃ ca paratrāpi tasmāt tat parivarjayet
8.d: अधर्मदण्डनं लोके यशोघ्नं कीर्तिनाशनम् अस्वर्ग्यं च परत्रापि तस्मात् तत् परिवर्जयेत्
8.e: Unjust punishment is destructive of reputation among men and subversive of fame; in the other world also it leads to loss of heaven; he shall therefore avoid it.

8.s: adaṇḍyān daṇḍayan rājā daṇḍyāṃścaivāpyadaṇḍayan ayaśo mahadāpnoti narakaṃ caiva gacchati
8.d: अदण्ड्यान् दण्डयन् राजा दण्ड्यांश्चैवाप्यदण्डयन् अयशो महदाप्नोति नरकं चैव गच्छति
8.e: The king, punishing those who do not deserve to be punished, and not punishing those who deserve to be punished, attains great ill-fame and goes to hell.

8.s: vāgdaṇḍaṃ prathamaṃ kuryāddhigdaṇḍaṃ tadanantaram tṛtīyaṃ dhanadaṇḍaṃ tu vadhadaṇḍamataḥ param
8.d: वाग्दण्डं प्रथमं कुर्याद्धिग्दण्डं तदनन्तरम् तृतीयं धनदण्डं तु वधदण्डमतः परम्
8.e: First of all, he shall inflict punishment in the form of reprimand, then in the form of reproach, thirdly in the form of fine, and after that the death-penalty.

8.s: vadhenāpi yadā tvetānnigrahītuṃ na śaknuyāt tadaiṣu sarvamapyetat prayuñjīta catuṣṭayam
8.d: वधेनापि यदा त्वेतान्निग्रहीतुं न शक्नुयात् तदैषु सर्वमप्येतत् प्रयुञ्जीत चतुष्टयम्
8.e: When however he is not able to restrain them even by the ‘death-penalty,’—then he should inflict on them all these four.

8.s: lokasaṃvyavahārārthaṃ yāḥ saṃjñāḥ prathitā bhuvi tāmrarūpyasuvarṇānāṃ tāḥ pravakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ
8.d: लोकसंव्यवहारार्थं याः संज्ञाः प्रथिता भुवि ताम्ररूप्यसुवर्णानां ताः प्रवक्ष्याम्यशेषतः
8.e: I am going to describe fully, for the sake of business-transactions, those technical terms that are used in the world in connection with silver and gold.

8.s: jālāntaragate bhānau yat sūkṣmaṃ dṛśyate rajaḥ prathamaṃ tat pramāṇānāṃ trasareṇuṃ pracakṣate
8.d: जालान्तरगते भानौ यत् सूक्ष्मं दृश्यते रजः प्रथमं तत् प्रमाणानां त्रसरेणुं प्रचक्षते
8.e: The small mote that is seen when the sun shines through a lattice-hole they declare to be the ‘triad,’ the very first of measures.

8.s: trasareṇavo 'ṣṭau vijñeyā likṣaikā parimāṇataḥ tā rājasarṣapastisraste trayo gaurasarṣapaḥ
8.d: त्रसरेणवो ऽष्टौ विज्ञेया लिक्षैका परिमाणतः ता राजसर्षपस्तिस्रस्ते त्रयो गौरसर्षपः
8.e: Eight Triads should be known as one ‘Louse-egg’ in measure; three of these as one ‘Black Mustard’; and three of these latter as a ‘White Mustard.’

8.s: sarṣapāḥ ṣaḍ yavo madhyastriyavaṃ tvekakṛṣṇalam pañcakṛṣṇalako māṣaste suvarṇastu ṣoḍaśa
8.d: सर्षपाः षड् यवो मध्यस्त्रियवं त्वेककृष्णलम् पञ्चकृष्णलको माषस्ते सुवर्णस्तु षोडश
8.e: Six ‘mustards’ make one middling ‘barley-corn’; three of these make one ‘guñjā-berry’; a ‘bean’ is made of five ‘guñja-berries;’ and sixteen ‘beans’ make one ‘gold-piece.’

8.s: palaṃ suvarṇāścatvāraḥ palāni dharaṇaṃ daśa dve kṛṣṇale samadhṛte vijñeyo raupyamāṣakaḥ rūpyamāṣakaḥ
8.d: पलं सुवर्णाश्चत्वारः पलानि धरणं दश द्वे कृष्णले समधृते विज्ञेयो रौप्यमाषकः रूप्यमाषकः
8.e: Four ‘gold-pieces’ make one ‘pala,’ ten palas one ‘dharaṇa’; and two ‘guñja-berries’ of equal weight should be known as one ‘silver-bean.’

8.s: te ṣoḍaśa syāddharaṇaṃ purāṇaścaiva rājataḥ kārṣāpaṇastu vijñeyastāmrikaḥ kārṣikaḥ paṇaḥ
8.d: ते षोडश स्याद्धरणं पुराणश्चैव राजतः कार्षापणस्तु विज्ञेयस्ताम्रिकः कार्षिकः पणः
8.e: Sixteen of these latter make one ‘silver-dharaṇa’ or ‘purāṇa’; and a ‘karṣa’ of copper is to be known as ‘kārṣāpaṇa’ or ‘paṇa.’

8.s: dharaṇāni daśa jñeyaḥ śatamānastu rājataḥ catuḥsauvarṇiko niṣko vijñeyastu pramāṇataḥ
8.d: धरणानि दश ज्ञेयः शतमानस्तु राजतः चतुःसौवर्णिको निष्को विज्ञेयस्तु प्रमाणतः
8.e: Ten ‘dharaṇas’ are to be known as the ‘silver śatamāna’ (centimetre); and the ‘niṣka’ should be understood as four ‘gold-pieces’ in weight.

8.s: paṇānāṃ dve śate sārdhe prathamaḥ sāhasaḥ smṛtaḥ madhyamaḥ pañca vijñeyaḥ sahasraṃ tveva cauttamaḥ
8.d: पणानां द्वे शते सार्धे प्रथमः साहसः स्मृतः मध्यमः पञ्च विज्ञेयः सहस्रं त्वेव चौत्तमः
8.e: The first amercement has been declared to be two hundred and fifty paṇas; the middling is to be known as five hundred; and the highest as a thousand.

8.s: ṛṇe deye pratijñāte pañcakaṃ śatamarhati apahnave taddviguṇaṃ tan manoranuśāsanam
8.d: ऋणे देये प्रतिज्ञाते पञ्चकं शतमर्हति अपह्नवे तद्द्विगुणं तन् मनोरनुशासनम्
8.e: On the debt being admitted to be due, the debtor deserves (a fine of) five per cent.; and in the case of denial, twice as much; such is the ordinance of manu.

8.s: vasiṣṭhavihitāṃ vṛddhiṃ sṛjedvittavivardhinīm aśītibhāgaṃ gṛhṇīyān māsādvārdhuṣikaḥ śate
8.d: वसिष्ठविहितां वृद्धिं सृजेद्वित्तविवर्धिनीम् अशीतिभागं गृह्णीयान् मासाद्वार्धुषिकः शते
8.e: The money-lender shall stipulate an interest sanctioned by Vasiṣṭha, for increasing the capital. He shall take monthly the eightieth part of a hundred.

8.s: dvikaṃ śataṃ vā gṛhṇīyāt satāṃ dharmamanusmaran dvikaṃ śataṃ hi gṛhṇāno na bhavatyarthakilbiṣī
8.d: द्विकं शतं वा गृह्णीयात् सतां धर्ममनुस्मरन् द्विकं शतं हि गृह्णानो न भवत्यर्थकिल्बिषी
8.e: Or, remembering the duty of the righteous, he may take two in the hundred; by taking two per cent. he does not incur the sin of extortion.

8.s: dvikaṃ trikaṃ catuṣkaṃ ca pañcakaṃ ca śataṃ samam māsasya vṛddhiṃ gṛhṇīyādvarṇānāmanupūrvaśaḥ
8.d: द्विकं त्रिकं चतुष्कं च पञ्चकं च शतं समम् मासस्य वृद्धिं गृह्णीयाद्वर्णानामनुपूर्वशः
8.e: He may charge just two, three, four or five per cent. per month from the four castes respectively.

8.s: na tvevādhau saupakāre kausīdīṃ vṛddhimāpnuyāt na cādheḥ kālasaṃrodhātnisargo 'sti na vikrayaḥ
8.d: न त्वेवाधौ सौपकारे कौसीदीं वृद्धिमाप्नुयात् न चाधेः कालसंरोधात्निसर्गो ऽस्ति न विक्रयः
8.e: But when there is profitable pledge, he shall receive no interest on the loan; and there shall be neither transference nor sale of the pledge, merely by the lapse of time.

8.s: na bhoktavyo balādādhirbhuñjāno vṛddhimutsṛjet mūlyena toṣayeccainamādhisteno 'nyathā bhavet
8.d: न भोक्तव्यो बलादाधिर्भुञ्जानो वृद्धिमुत्सृजेत् मूल्येन तोषयेच्चैनमाधिस्तेनो ऽन्यथा भवेत्
8.e: The pledge shall not be used by force; using it thus, he shall renounce the interest; he shall satisfy the other party with its pr ice; otherwise he would be a stealer of the pledge.

8.s: ādhiścaupanidhiścaubhau na kālātyayamarhataḥ avahāryau bhavetāṃ tau dīrghakālamavasthitau
8.d: आधिश्चौपनिधिश्चौभौ न कालात्ययमर्हतः अवहार्यौ भवेतां तौ दीर्घकालमवस्थितौ
8.e: Pledges and Deposits should not suffer much lapse of time; for being left over for a long time, they would be liable to appropriation.

8.s: saṃprītyā bhujyamānāni na naśyanti kadā cana dhenuruṣṭro vahannaśvo yaśca damyaḥ prayujyate
8.d: संप्रीत्या भुज्यमानानि न नश्यन्ति कदा चन धेनुरुष्ट्रो वहन्नश्वो यश्च दम्यः प्रयुज्यते
8.e: Things used through favour are never forfeited; such as a milch cow, a camel, an ox or the animal that is made over for breaking in.

8.s: yat kiṃ ciddaśavarṣāṇi saṃnidhau prekṣate dhanī bhujyamānaṃ paraistūṣṇīṃ na sa tatlabdhumarhati
8.d: यत् किं चिद्दशवर्षाणि संनिधौ प्रेक्षते धनी भुज्यमानं परैस्तूष्णीं न स तत्लब्धुमर्हति
8.e: Whatever thing the owner meekly sees being used by others in his presence, for ten years,—that thing he does not deserve to recover.

8.s: ajaḍaścedapogaṇḍo viṣaye cāsya bhujyate bhagnaṃ tadvyavahāreṇa bhoktā taddravyamarhati taddhanamarhati
8.d: अजडश्चेदपोगण्डो विषये चास्य भुज्यते भग्नं तद्व्यवहारेण भोक्ता तद्द्रव्यमर्हति तद्धनमर्हति
8.e: If the owner is neither an idiot nor a minor, and the property is used in his own country,—it becomes frustrated in law, and the user becomes entitled to the property.

8.s: ādhiḥ sīmā bāladhanaṃ nikṣepaupanidhiḥ striyaḥ nikṣepaupanidhī rājasvaṃ śrotriyasvaṃ ca na bhogena praṇaśyati
8.d: आधिः सीमा बालधनं निक्षेपौपनिधिः स्त्रियः निक्षेपौपनिधी राजस्वं श्रोत्रियस्वं च न भोगेन प्रणश्यति
8.e: A pledge, a boundary, minor’s property, a deposit, a property enjoyed by favour, women, king’s property, and the property of a vedic scholar are not lost by adverse possession.

8.s: yaḥ svāminā 'nanujñātamādhiṃ bhūṅkte 'vicakṣaṇaḥ tenārdhavṛddhirmoktavyā tasya bhogasya niṣkṛtiḥ
8.d: यः स्वामिना ऽननुज्ञातमाधिं भूङ्क्ते ऽविचक्षणः तेनार्धवृद्धिर्मोक्तव्या तस्य भोगस्य निष्कृतिः
8.e: The fool, who, without the owner’s permission, uses a deposit, shall have to remit half the amount of the interest, as compensation for such use.

8.s: kusīdavṛddhirdvaiguṇyaṃ nātyeti sakṛdāhṛtā sakṛdāhitā dhānye sade lave vāhye nātikrāmati pañcatām
8.d: कुसीदवृद्धिर्द्वैगुण्यं नात्येति सकृदाहृता सकृदाहिता धान्ये सदे लवे वाह्ये नातिक्रामति पञ्चताम्
8.e: Interest on money-loans stipulated at one time shall not exceed the double; in the case of grains, fruits, wool and beasts of burden, it shall not go beyond the quintuple.

8.s: kṛtānusārādadhikā vyatiriktā na sidhyati kusīdapathamāhustaṃ pañcakaṃ śatamarhati
8.d: कृतानुसारादधिका व्यतिरिक्ता न सिध्यति कुसीदपथमाहुस्तं पञ्चकं शतमर्हति
8.e: Interest, stipulated in contravention of the law, being excessive, is not payable. They declare this to be the usurer’s way. It is only five per cent. to which the man is entitled.

8.s: nātisāṃvatsarīṃ vṛddhiṃ na cādṛṣṭāṃ punarharet vinirharet cakravṛddhiḥ kālavṛddhiḥ kāritā kāyikā ca yā
8.d: नातिसांवत्सरीं वृद्धिं न चादृष्टां पुनर्हरेत् विनिर्हरेत् चक्रवृद्धिः कालवृद्धिः कारिता कायिका च या
8.e: One shall not pay or receive an interest beyond the annual, or what is unapproved (or unaccumulated); nor compound interest, nor periodical interest, nor that which is (privately) stipulated, nor corporeal.

8.s: ṛṇaṃ dātumaśakto yaḥ kartumicchet punaḥ kriyām sa dattvā nirjitāṃ vṛddhiṃ karaṇaṃ parivartayet
8.d: ऋणं दातुमशक्तो यः कर्तुमिच्छेत् पुनः क्रियाम् स दत्त्वा निर्जितां वृद्धिं करणं परिवर्तयेत्
8.e: He who, unable to repay the debt, wishes to renew the contract, shall change the bond, after paying the accrued interest.

8.s: adarśayitvā tatraiva hiraṇyaṃ parivartayet yāvatī saṃbhavedvṛddhistāvatīṃ dātumarhati
8.d: अदर्शयित्वा तत्रैव हिरण्यं परिवर्तयेत् यावती संभवेद्वृद्धिस्तावतीं दातुमर्हति
8.e: Not having brought forward the gold, he should renew the bond; and he should pay as much interest as may be possible.

8.s: cakravṛddhiṃ samārūḍho deśakālavyavasthitaḥ atikrāman deśakālau na tatphalamavāpnuyāt
8.d: चक्रवृद्धिं समारूढो देशकालव्यवस्थितः अतिक्रामन् देशकालौ न तत्फलमवाप्नुयात्
8.e: When a man has entered into a ‘wheel-contract’ wtth reference to a particular place or time,—if he fails in regard to the place or time, he shall not suffer its reward.

8.s: samudrayānakuśalā deśakālārthadarśinaḥ sthāpayanti tu yāṃ vṛddhiṃ sā tatrādhigamaṃ prati
8.d: समुद्रयानकुशला देशकालार्थदर्शिनः स्थापयन्ति तु यां वृद्धिं सा तत्राधिगमं प्रति
8.e: As regards the exact amount to be paid, the interest shall be that which is fixed by persons expert in sea-voyages, and those capable of calculating the profits in connection with a particular place and time.

8.s: yo yasya pratibhūstiṣṭheddarśanāyaiha mānavaḥ adarśayan sa taṃ tasya prayacchet svadhanādṛṇam tasya yateta
8.d: यो यस्य प्रतिभूस्तिष्ठेद्दर्शनायैह मानवः अदर्शयन् स तं तस्य प्रयच्छेत् स्वधनादृणम् तस्य यतेत
8.e: When a man stands surety for the appearance of a person, if he does not produce him, he shall pay his debt out of his own property.

8.s: prātibhāvyaṃ vṛthādānamākṣikaṃ saurikāṃ ca yat daṇḍaśulkāvaśeṣaṃ ca na putro dātumarhati
8.d: प्रातिभाव्यं वृथादानमाक्षिकं सौरिकां च यत् दण्डशुल्कावशेषं च न पुत्रो दातुमर्हति
8.e: But the son shall not be liable to pay the surety-money, or a futile gift, or gambling deists, or debts due to liquor, or the balance of fines and duties.

8.s: darśanaprātibhāvye tu vidhiḥ syāt pūrvacoditaḥ dānapratibhuvi prete dāyādānapi dāpayet
8.d: दर्शनप्रातिभाव्ये तु विधिः स्यात् पूर्वचोदितः दानप्रतिभुवि प्रेते दायादानपि दापयेत्
8.e: The law laid down in the preceding verse shall apply to the case of ‘Surety for appearance’; in the case of the death of the ‘Surety for payment’ however, the king shall make the heirs also to pay up.

8.s: adātari punardātā vijñātaprakṛtāvṛṇam paścāt pratibhuvi prete parīpset kena hetunā
8.d: अदातरि पुनर्दाता विज्ञातप्रकृतावृणम् पश्चात् प्रतिभुवि प्रेते परीप्सेत् केन हेतुना
8.e: “By what means then would the creditor seek to obtain his dues, in the event of the death of the surety other than that for ‘payment,’ whose character is fully known?”

8.s: nirādiṣṭadhanaścet tu pratibhūḥ syādalaṃdhanaḥ svadhanādeva taddadyānnirādiṣṭa iti sthitiḥ
8.d: निरादिष्टधनश्चेत् तु प्रतिभूः स्यादलंधनः स्वधनादेव तद्दद्यान्निरादिष्ट इति स्थितिः
8.e: If the surety were one to whom money had been made over and who had enough money,—then he to whom it had been made over shall pay it out ok his own property; such is the settled rule.

8.s: mattaunmattārtādhyadhīnairbālena sthavireṇa vā asaṃbaddhakṛtaścaiva vyāvahāro na sidhyati
8.d: मत्तौन्मत्तार्ताध्यधीनैर्बालेन स्थविरेण वा असंबद्धकृतश्चैव व्यावहारो न सिध्यति
8.e: A transaction is not valid when effected by one who is drunk, or insane, or distressed, or wholly dependent, or minor, or senile, or unauthorised

8.s: satyā na bhāṣā bhavati yadyapi syāt pratiṣṭhitā bahiścedbhāṣyate dharmātniyatādvyavahārikāt
8.d: सत्या न भाषा भवति यद्यपि स्यात् प्रतिष्ठिता बहिश्चेद्भाष्यते धर्मात्नियताद्व्यवहारिकात्
8.e: No contract, even though substantiated, is valid, if what is contracted for is contrary to law or to established custom.

8.s: yogādhamanavikrītaṃ yogadānapratigraham yatra vā 'pyupadhiṃ paśyet tat sarvaṃ vinivartayet
8.d: योगाधमनविक्रीतं योगदानप्रतिग्रहम् यत्र वा ऽप्युपधिं पश्येत् तत् सर्वं विनिवर्तयेत्
8.e: Fraudulent mortgages and sales, fraudelent gifts and acceptances, as also all wherein he detects fraud—he shall nullify.

8.s: grahītā yadi naṣṭaḥ syāt kuṭumbārthe kṛto vyayaḥ kuṭumbe ca dātavyaṃ bāndhavaistat syāt pravibhaktairapi svataḥ
8.d: ग्रहीता यदि नष्टः स्यात् कुटुम्बार्थे कृतो व्ययः कुटुम्बे च दातव्यं बान्धवैस्तत् स्यात् प्रविभक्तैरपि स्वतः
8.e: When the borrower is lost, and the expenditure was incurred by the family, the debt is to be paid by the relatives out of their own property, even though these may have been separated.

8.s: kuṭumbārthe 'dhyadhīno 'pi vyavahāraṃ yamācaret svadeśe vā videśe vā taṃ jyāyānna vicālayet
8.d: कुटुम्बार्थे ऽध्यधीनो ऽपि व्यवहारं यमाचरेत् स्वदेशे वा विदेशे वा तं ज्यायान्न विचालयेत्
8.e: Should even a servant effect a transaction for the sake of the family,—the master, whether in his own country or abroad, should not repudiate it.

8.s: balāddattaṃ balādbhuktaṃ balādyaccāpi lekhitam sarvān balakṛtānarthānakṛtān manurabravīt
8.d: बलाद्दत्तं बलाद्भुक्तं बलाद्यच्चापि लेखितम् सर्वान् बलकृतानर्थानकृतान् मनुरब्रवीत्
8.e: What is given by force, what is ennjoyed by force, what has been caused to be written by force,—all thansactions effected by force Manu has declared to be void.

8.s: trayaḥ parārthe kliśyanti sākṣiṇaḥ pratibhūḥ kulam catvārastūpacīyante vipra āḍhyo vaṇilg nṛpaḥ
8.d: त्रयः परार्थे क्लिश्यन्ति साक्षिणः प्रतिभूः कुलम् चत्वारस्तूपचीयन्ते विप्र आढ्यो वणिल्ग् नृपः
8.e: Three persons suffer for the sake of others: witnesses, surety and the judge: while four persons prosper: the brāhmaṇa, the affluent, the merchant and the king.

8.s: anādeyaṃ nādadīta parikṣīṇo 'pi pārthivaḥ na cādeyaṃ samṛddho 'pi sūkṣmamapyarthamutsṛjet
8.d: अनादेयं नाददीत परिक्षीणो ऽपि पार्थिवः न चादेयं समृद्धो ऽपि सूक्ष्ममप्यर्थमुत्सृजेत्
8.e: Even though reduced (in circumstances), the King shall not take what ought not to be taken; and even though affluent, he shall not relinquish what ought to be taken, be it ever so small.

8.s: anādeyasya cādānādādeyasya ca varjanāt daurbalyaṃ khyāpyate rājñaḥ sa pretyaiha ca naśyati
8.d: अनादेयस्य चादानादादेयस्य च वर्जनात् दौर्बल्यं ख्याप्यते राज्ञः स प्रेत्यैह च नश्यति
8.e: By the taking of what he ought not to take and by the relinquishing of what he ought to take the king’s weakness becomes proclaimed, and he becomes ruined here as also after death.

8.s: svādānādvarṇasaṃsargāt tvabalānāṃ ca rakṣaṇāt balaṃ sañjāyate rājñaḥ sa pretyaiha ca vardhate
8.d: स्वादानाद्वर्णसंसर्गात् त्वबलानां च रक्षणात् बलं सञ्जायते राज्ञः स प्रेत्यैह च वर्धते
8.e: By taking what is his due, by the proper adjustment of castes, and by protecting the weak, the power of the king grows, and he prospers here as also after death.

8.s: tasmādyama iva svāmī svayaṃ hitvā priyāpriye varteta yāmyayā vṛttyā jitakrodho jitaindriyaḥ
8.d: तस्माद्यम इव स्वामी स्वयं हित्वा प्रियाप्रिये वर्तेत याम्यया वृत्त्या जितक्रोधो जितैन्द्रियः
8.e: For these reasons, the King shall, like Yama, renounce his likes and dislikes, and behave in the manner of Yama,—his anger suppressed and his senses controlled.

8.s: yastvadharmeṇa kāryāṇi mohāt kuryānnarādhipaḥ acirāt taṃ durātmānaṃ vaśe kurvanti śatravaḥ
8.d: यस्त्वधर्मेण कार्याणि मोहात् कुर्यान्नराधिपः अचिरात् तं दुरात्मानं वशे कुर्वन्ति शत्रवः
8.e: If an evil-minded king, through folly, deal with cases unjustly,—his enemies bring him under their control in no time.

8.s: kāmakrodhau tu saṃyamya yo 'rthān dharmeṇa paśyati prajāstamanuvartante samudramiva sindhavaḥ
8.d: कामक्रोधौ तु संयम्य यो ऽर्थान् धर्मेण पश्यति प्रजास्तमनुवर्तन्ते समुद्रमिव सिन्धवः
8.e: When however, having subdued love and hatred, he deals with cases justly, his subjects turn towards him, as the rivers towards the ocean,

8.s: yaḥ sādhayantaṃ chandena vedayeddhanikaṃ nṛpe sa rājñā tatcaturbhāgaṃ dāpyastasya ca taddhanam
8.d: यः साधयन्तं छन्देन वेदयेद्धनिकं नृपे स राज्ञा तत्चतुर्भागं दाप्यस्तस्य च तद्धनम्
8.e: A person who complains to the king against the creditor trying to accomplish his purpose by his own will,—should be made by the king to pay the fourth part, and also the total amount to him

8.s: karmaṇā 'pi samaṃ kuryāddhanikāyādhamarṇikaḥ samo 'vakṛṣṭajātistu dadyātśreyāṃstu tatśanaiḥ
8.d: कर्मणा ऽपि समं कुर्याद्धनिकायाधमर्णिकः समो ऽवकृष्टजातिस्तु दद्यात्श्रेयांस्तु तत्शनैः
8.e: Even by labour shall the debtor make good what is due to the creditor, if he is of the same or of a lower caste; the superior person shall pay it up gradually.

8.s: anena vidhinā rājā mitho vivadatāṃ nṛṇām sākṣipratyayasiddhāni kāryāṇi samatāṃ nayet
8.d: अनेन विधिना राजा मिथो विवदतां नृणाम् साक्षिप्रत्ययसिद्धानि कार्याणि समतां नयेत्
8.e: In this manner shall the king settle the disputes of men quarrelling among themselves, deciding them with the help of witnesses and other evidence.

8.s: kulaje vṛttasaṃpanne dharmajñe satyavādini mahāpakṣe dhaninyārye nikṣepaṃ nikṣipedbudhaḥ
8.d: कुलजे वृत्तसंपन्ने धर्मज्ञे सत्यवादिनि महापक्षे धनिन्यार्ये निक्षेपं निक्षिपेद्बुधः
8.e: The wise man shall, entrust a deposit to one who is born of good family, is endowed with character, cognisant of the law, and truthful, has a large following, and is wealthy and honourable

8.s: yo yathā nikṣipeddhaste yamarthaṃ yasya mānavaḥ sa tathaiva grahītavyo yathā dāyastathā grahaḥ
8.d: यो यथा निक्षिपेद्धस्ते यमर्थं यस्य मानवः स तथैव ग्रहीतव्यो यथा दायस्तथा ग्रहः
8.e: In the form in which one shall deposit a thing in the hands of another person, in that same form shall that thing be received back; as the delivery so the recovery.

8.s: yo nikṣepaṃ yācyamāno nikṣepturna prayacchati sa yācyaḥ prāḍvivākena tatnikṣepturasaṃnidhau
8.d: यो निक्षेपं याच्यमानो निक्षेप्तुर्न प्रयच्छति स याच्यः प्राड्विवाकेन तत्निक्षेप्तुरसंनिधौ
8.e: When requested to restore the deposit, if the trustee do not restore it to the depositor,—then, on the departure of that depositor, in the event of there being no witnesses, the judge shall actually deposit gold (with the trustee) through spies of proper age and appearance, under some pretexts, and then ask him to restore it.

8.s: sākṣiabhāve praṇidhibhirvayorūpasamanvitaiḥ apadeśaiśca saṃnyasya hiraṇyaṃ tasya tattvataḥ
8.d: साक्षिअभावे प्रणिधिभिर्वयोरूपसमन्वितैः अपदेशैश्च संन्यस्य हिरण्यं तस्य तत्त्वतः
8.e: When requested to restore the deposit, if the trustee do not restore it to the depositor,—then, on the departure of that depositor, in the event of there being no witnesses, the judge shall actually deposit gold (with the trustee) through spies of proper age and appearance, under some pretexts, and then ask him to restore it.

8.s: sa yadi pratipadyeta yathānyastaṃ yathākṛtam na tatra vidyate kiṃ cidyat parairabhiyujyate
8.d: स यदि प्रतिपद्येत यथान्यस्तं यथाकृतम् न तत्र विद्यते किं चिद्यत् परैरभियुज्यते
8.e: If he admits the deposit exactly in the form and shape in which it was entrusted,—then there is nothing in the charge brought against him by others.

8.s: teṣāṃ na dadyādyadi tu taddhiraṇyaṃ yathāvidhi ubhau nigṛhya dāpyaḥ syāditi dharmasya dhāraṇā sa nigṛhyaubhayaṃ dāpya iti dharmasya dhāraṇā
8.d: तेषां न दद्याद्यदि तु तद्धिरण्यं यथाविधि उभौ निगृह्य दाप्यः स्यादिति धर्मस्य धारणा स निगृह्यौभयं दाप्य इति धर्मस्य धारणा
8.e: If, however, he should not restore that gold to them in the proper manner, he should be forced to restore both; such is the decree of the law.

8.s: nikṣepaupanidhī nityaṃ na deyau pratyanantare naśyato vinipāte tāvanipāte tvanāśinau
8.d: निक्षेपौपनिधी नित्यं न देयौ प्रत्यनन्तरे नश्यतो विनिपाते तावनिपाते त्वनाशिनौ
8.e: Deposits, open and sealed, should never be handed over to the next-of-kin; in the event of a mishap occurring, they become lost; though they do not become lost, if no mishap occurs.

8.s: svayameva tu yau dadyān mṛtasya pratyanantare na sa rājñā 'bhiyoktavyo na nikṣeptuśca bandhubhiḥ
8.d: स्वयमेव तु यौ दद्यान् मृतस्य प्रत्यनन्तरे न स राज्ञा ऽभियोक्तव्यो न निक्षेप्तुश्च बन्धुभिः
8.e: If the man restores it himself to the next-of-kin of the deceased depositor,—he should not be harassed by the king, or by the depositor’s relatives.

8.s: acchalenaiva cānvicchet tamarthaṃ prītipūrvakam vicārya tasya vā vṛttaṃ sāmnaiva parisādhayet
8.d: अच्छलेनैव चान्विच्छेत् तमर्थं प्रीतिपूर्वकम् विचार्य तस्य वा वृत्तं साम्नैव परिसाधयेत्
8.e: In doubtful cases he should try to obtain it without artifice and in a friendly manner; or having ascertained his character, he should settle the matter by gentle means.

8.s: nikṣepeṣveṣu sarveṣu vidhiḥ syāt parisādhane samudre nāpnuyāt kiṃ cidyadi tasmānna saṃharet
8.d: निक्षेपेष्वेषु सर्वेषु विधिः स्यात् परिसाधने समुद्रे नाप्नुयात् किं चिद्यदि तस्मान्न संहरेत्
8.e: In the case of all deposits, such should be the method of restoration; but in the case of a sealed deposit, he should incur nothing, if he does not extract anything from it.

8.s: caurairhṛtaṃ jalenauḍhamagninā dagdhameva vā na dadyādyadi tasmāt sa na saṃharati kiṃ cana
8.d: चौरैर्हृतं जलेनौढमग्निना दग्धमेव वा न दद्याद्यदि तस्मात् स न संहरति किं चन
8.e: The depositary shall not hake good what has been stolen by thieves, or carried away by water, or burnt,—if he does not extract anything from it.

8.s: nikṣepasyāpahartāramanikṣeptārameva ca sarvairupāyairanvicchetśapathaiścaiva vaidikaiḥ
8.d: निक्षेपस्यापहर्तारमनिक्षेप्तारमेव च सर्वैरुपायैरन्विच्छेत्शपथैश्चैव वैदिकैः
8.e: The appropriator of a deposit, as also one who has not deposited anything (and yet asks for it),—the king shall test by all methods, as also by means of oaths and ordeals prescribed in the scriptures.

8.s: yo nikṣepaṃ nārpayati yaścānikṣipya yācate tāvubhau cauravatśāsyau dāpyau vā tatsamaṃ damam
8.d: यो निक्षेपं नार्पयति यश्चानिक्षिप्य याचते तावुभौ चौरवत्शास्यौ दाप्यौ वा तत्समं दमम्
8.e: He who does not restore a deposit, and he who, without having made any deposit, asks for it,—both of these should be punished like thieves, or be made to pay a fine equal in value.

8.s: nikṣepasyāpahartāraṃ tatsamaṃ dāpayeddamam tathaupanidhihartāramaviśeṣeṇa pārthivaḥ
8.d: निक्षेपस्यापहर्तारं तत्समं दापयेद्दमम् तथौपनिधिहर्तारमविशेषेण पार्थिवः
8.e: In all cases the king shall make the appropriator of a deposit pay a fine equal in value to it; also the appropriator of a friendly loan.

8.s: upadhābhiśca yaḥ kaścit paradravyaṃ harennaraḥ sasahāyaḥ sa hantavyaḥ prakāśaṃ vividhairvadhaiḥ
8.d: उपधाभिश्च यः कश्चित् परद्रव्यं हरेन्नरः ससहायः स हन्तव्यः प्रकाशं विविधैर्वधैः
8.e: The man who may appropriate, by fraudulent means, the property of another person, should be punished publicly, along with his accomplices, with various modes of death.

8.s: nikṣepo yaḥ kṛto yena yāvāṃśca kulasaṃnidhau tāvāneva sa vijñeyo vibruvan daṇḍamarhati
8.d: निक्षेपो यः कृतो येन यावांश्च कुलसंनिधौ तावानेव स विज्ञेयो विब्रुवन् दण्डमर्हति
8.e: As much of a certain deposit has been entrusted in the presence of a number of men—so much should it be decided to be; the party misrepresenting it becomes liable to punishment.

8.s: mitho dāyaḥ kṛto yena gṛhīto mitha eva vā mitha eva pradātavyo yathā dāyastathā grahaḥ
8.d: मिथो दायः कृतो येन गृहीतो मिथ एव वा मिथ एव प्रदातव्यो यथा दायस्तथा ग्रहः
8.e: When a trust has been created privately and accepted also privately, then it should be restored also secretly: as the delivery so the restoration.

8.s: nikṣiptasya dhanasyaivaṃ prītyaupanihitasya ca rājā vinirṇayaṃ kuryādakṣiṇvannyāsadhāriṇam
8.d: निक्षिप्तस्य धनस्यैवं प्रीत्यौपनिहितस्य च राजा विनिर्णयं कुर्यादक्षिण्वन्न्यासधारिणम्
8.e: Thus shall the king come to a decision regarding property given as ‘deposit’ and that which is given as ‘friendly loan,’—without causing any injury to the keeper of the deposit.

8.s: vikrīṇīte parasya svaṃ yo 'svāmī svāmyasammataḥ na taṃ nayeta sākṣyaṃ tu stenamastenamāninam
8.d: विक्रीणीते परस्य स्वं यो ऽस्वामी स्वाम्यसम्मतः न तं नयेत साक्ष्यं तु स्तेनमस्तेनमानिनम्
8.e: If a man sells another man’s property, without being its owner, and without the owner’s consent, the judge shall not admit him as a witness,—he being a thief; though he may not be regarded as a thief.

8.s: avahāryo bhavetcaiva sānvayaḥ ṣaṭśataṃ damam nir 'nvayo 'napasaraḥ prāptaḥ syāccaurakilbiṣam
8.d: अवहार्यो भवेत्चैव सान्वयः षट्शतं दमम् निर् ऽन्वयो ऽनपसरः प्राप्तः स्याच्चौरकिल्बिषम्
8.e: If a relative, he shall be made to pay the penalty of six hundred; if he is not a relative, nor one having access to him, he shall incur the guilt of theft (specially).

8.s: asvāminā kṛto yastu dāyo vikraya eva vā akṛtaḥ sa tu vijñeyo vyavahāre yathā sthitiḥ
8.d: अस्वामिना कृतो यस्तु दायो विक्रय एव वा अकृतः स तु विज्ञेयो व्यवहारे यथा स्थितिः
8.e: If a gift or sale is made by one who is not the owner, it should be held to be as not-made,—such being the rule of judicial proceedings.

8.s: saṃbhogo dṛśyate yatra na dṛśyetāgamaḥ kva cit āgamaḥ kāraṇaṃ tatra na saṃbhoga iti sthitiḥ
8.d: संभोगो दृश्यते यत्र न दृश्येतागमः क्व चित् आगमः कारणं तत्र न संभोग इति स्थितिः
8.e: Where possession is evident, but no sort of title is perceptible, there title, and not possession, shall be the proof; such is the settled rule.

8.s: vikrayādyo dhanaṃ kiṃ cidgṛhṇīyat kulasaṃnidhau krayeṇa sa viśuddhaṃ hi nyāyato labhate dhanam
8.d: विक्रयाद्यो धनं किं चिद्गृह्णीयत् कुलसंनिधौ क्रयेण स विशुद्धं हि न्यायतो लभते धनम्
8.e: If a man obtains a property from the market, in the presence of witnesses, he acquires that property with a clear title obtained by legal purchase.

8.s: atha mūlamanāhāryaṃ prakāśakrayaśodhitaḥ adaṇḍyo mucyate rājñā nāṣṭiko labhate dhanam
8.d: अथ मूलमनाहार्यं प्रकाशक्रयशोधितः अदण्ड्यो मुच्यते राज्ञा नाष्टिको लभते धनम्
8.e: If the source cannot be traced, the person (buyer), whose conduct has been cleared by the fact of the sale being public, is let off without punishment, but the man who lost the property shall receive it back.

8.s: nānyadanyena saṃsṛṣṭarūpaṃ vikrayamarhati na cāsāraṃ na ca nyūnaṃ na dūreṇa tirohitam na sāvadyaṃ na ca nyūnaṃ na dūre na tirohitaṃ
8.d: नान्यदन्येन संसृष्टरूपं विक्रयमर्हति न चासारं न च न्यूनं न दूरेण तिरोहितम् न सावद्यं न च न्यूनं न दूरे न तिरोहितं
8.e: Any commodity that is mixed up with another should not be sold; nor what is without substance, nor what is deficient, nor what is at a distance, nor what is concealed.

8.s: anyāṃ ceddarśayitvā 'nyā voḍhuḥ kanyā pradīyate ubhe ta ekaśulkena vahedityabravīn manuḥ
8.d: अन्यां चेद्दर्शयित्वा ऽन्या वोढुः कन्या प्रदीयते उभे त एकशुल्केन वहेदित्यब्रवीन् मनुः
8.e: After one damsel has been shown, if another be given to the bridegroom, then he should marry both of them for the same single price,—so Manu has ordained.

8.s: naunmattāyā na kuṣṭhinyā na ca yā spṛṣṭamaithunā pūrvaṃ doṣānabhikhyāpya pradātā daṇḍamarhati
8.d: नौन्मत्ताया न कुष्ठिन्या न च या स्पृष्टमैथुना पूर्वं दोषानभिख्याप्य प्रदाता दण्डमर्हति
8.e: The giver, of a girl who is insane or leprous or has suffered copulation, does not deserve punishment, if he has previously declared her defects.

8.s: ṛtvig yadi vṛto yajñe svakarma parihāpayet tasya karmānurūpeṇa deyo 'ṃśaḥ sahakartṛbhiḥ
8.d: ऋत्विग् यदि वृतो यज्ञे स्वकर्म परिहापयेत् तस्य कर्मानुरूपेण देयो ऽंशः सहकर्तृभिः
8.e: If a priest appointed at a sacrifice abandons his work, his associates shall pay him only such share as may be in keeping with the work actually done by him.

8.s: dakṣiṇāsu ca dattāsu svakarma parihāpayan kṛtsnameva labhetāṃśamanyenaiva ca kārayet
8.d: दक्षिणासु च दत्तासु स्वकर्म परिहापयन् कृत्स्नमेव लभेतांशमन्येनैव च कारयेत्
8.e: He who abandons his work after the fees have been paid, should receive his full share; and the work should be got done by another.

8.s: yasmin karmaṇi yāstu syuruktāḥ pratyaṅgadakṣiṇāḥ sa eva tā ādidīta bhajeran sarva eva vā
8.d: यस्मिन् कर्मणि यास्तु स्युरुक्ताः प्रत्यङ्गदक्षिणाः स एव ता आदिदीत भजेरन् सर्व एव वा
8.e: In connection with a rite, when specific fees are prescribed for its several parts,—will one man take all these, or shall they all share them?

8.s: rathaṃ haret cādhvaryurbrahmā 'dhāne ca vājinam hotā vā 'pi haredaśvamudgātā cāpyanaḥ kraye
8.d: रथं हरेत् चाध्वर्युर्ब्रह्मा ऽधाने च वाजिनम् होता वा ऽपि हरेदश्वमुद्गाता चाप्यनः क्रये
8.e: At Fire-laying, the Adhvaryu shall take the chariot, and the Brahman the horse; or the Hotṛ shall take the house: and the Udgātṛ shall take the cart at the Soma-purchase.

8.s: sarveṣāmardhino mukhyāstadardhenārdhino 'pare tṛtīyinastṛtīyāṃśāścaturthāṃśāśca pādinaḥ
8.d: सर्वेषामर्धिनो मुख्यास्तदर्धेनार्धिनो ऽपरे तृतीयिनस्तृतीयांशाश्चतुर्थांशाश्च पादिनः
8.e: From among all, the chief men shall receive half; the next shall receive half of that; the ‘thirders’ the third part and the ‘fourthers’ the fourth part of it.

8.s: saṃbhūya svāni karmāṇi kurvadbhiriha mānavaiḥ anena vidhiyogena kartavyā 'ṃśaprakalpanā
8.d: संभूय स्वानि कर्माणि कुर्वद्भिरिह मानवैः अनेन विधियोगेन कर्तव्या ऽंशप्रकल्पना
8.e: Among men carrying on their business jointly, the allotment of shares should be done by the application of these principles.

8.s: dharmārthaṃ yena dattaṃ syāt kasmai cidyācate dhanam paścācca na tathā tat syānna deyaṃ tasya tadbhavet
8.d: धर्मार्थं येन दत्तं स्यात् कस्मै चिद्याचते धनम् पश्चाच्च न तथा तत् स्यान्न देयं तस्य तद्भवेत्
8.e: When a man gives money, for a pious purpose, to another who asks for it,—if, subsequently, it is not used for that purpose, then, it shall not be given to him.

8.s: yadi saṃsādhayet tat tu darpātlobhena vā punaḥ rājñā dāpyaḥ suvarṇaṃ syāt tasya steyasya niṣkṛtiḥ
8.d: यदि संसाधयेत् तत् तु दर्पात्लोभेन वा पुनः राज्ञा दाप्यः सुवर्णं स्यात् तस्य स्तेयस्य निष्कृतिः
8.e: If, through arrogance or greed, the man should seek to recover it, he should be made by the King to pay one gold-piece, as an expiation for that theft.

8.s: dattasyaiṣauditā dharmyā yathāvadanapakriyā ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi vetanasyānapakriyām
8.d: दत्तस्यैषौदिता धर्म्या यथावदनपक्रिया अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि वेतनस्यानपक्रियाम्
8.e: Thus has been fully explained the lawful non-misappropriation of gifts; after this I am going to describe the ‘non-misappropriation of Wages.’

8.s: bhṛto nārto na kuryādyo darpāt karma yathā 'uditam 'nārto sa daṇḍyaḥ kṛṣṇalānyaṣṭau na deyaṃ cāsya vetanam
8.d: भृतो नार्तो न कुर्याद्यो दर्पात् कर्म यथा ऽउदितम् ऽनार्तो स दण्ड्यः कृष्णलान्यष्टौ न देयं चास्य वेतनम्
