8.e: If a hireling, without being ill, does not perform the stipulated work, through arrogance,—he should be fined eight ‘Kṛṣṇalas,’ and should not receive his wages.

8.s: ārtastu kuryāt svasthaḥ san yathābhāṣitamāditaḥ sa dīrghasyāpi kālasya tatlabheta(eva vetanam
8.d: आर्तस्तु कुर्यात् स्वस्थः सन् यथाभाषितमादितः स दीर्घस्यापि कालस्य तत्लभेत(एव वेतनम्
8.e: But if he is ill and on recovering, completes the work as originally stipulated, he shall receive his wages for it, even after a long time.

8.s: yathauktamārtaḥ sustho vā yastat karma na kārayet na tasya vetanaṃ deyamalpaunasyāpi karmaṇaḥ
8.d: यथौक्तमार्तः सुस्थो वा यस्तत् कर्म न कारयेत् न तस्य वेतनं देयमल्पौनस्यापि कर्मणः
8.e: When a man, sick or well, does not get the stipulated work done, he shall not receive hi s wages,—even though the work be only slightly incomplete.

8.s: eṣa dharmo 'khilenaukto vetanādānakarmaṇaḥ ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi dharmaṃ samayabhedinām
8.d: एष धर्मो ऽखिलेनौक्तो वेतनादानकर्मणः अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि धर्मं समयभेदिनाम्
8.e: Thus has the entire law bearing upon the action of ‘Non-payment of Wages’ been explained. After this I am going to expound the law relating to Contract-breakers.

8.s: yo grāmadeśasaṅghānāṃ kṛtvā satyena saṃvidam visaṃvadennaro lobhāt taṃ rāṣṭrādvipravāsayet
8.d: यो ग्रामदेशसङ्घानां कृत्वा सत्येन संविदम् विसंवदेन्नरो लोभात् तं राष्ट्राद्विप्रवासयेत्
8.e: If a man, after having entered into a compact under oath with a village, a country or a confederation, should break it, through greed,—him the king shall banish from his kingdom.

8.s: nigṛhya dāpayeccainaṃ samayavyabhicāriṇam catuḥsuvarṇān ṣaṇniṣkāṃśśatamānaṃ ca rājakam
8.d: निगृह्य दापयेच्चैनं समयव्यभिचारिणम् चतुःसुवर्णान् षण्निष्कांश्शतमानं च राजकम्
8.e: Having caught such a breaker of compact, he shall make him pay six ‘niṣkas’ of four ‘suvarṇas’ each, and also one silver ‘śatamāna.’

8.s: etaddaṇḍavidhiṃ kuryāddhārmikaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ grāmajātisamūheṣu samayavyabhicāriṇām
8.d: एतद्दण्डविधिं कुर्याद्धार्मिकः पृथिवीपतिः ग्रामजातिसमूहेषु समयव्यभिचारिणाम्
8.e: This is the law of punishment which the king shall follow in the case of the breakers of compacts relating to villages and caste-federations.

8.s: krītvā vikrīya vā kiṃ cidyasyaihānuśayo bhavet so 'ntardaśāhāt taddravyaṃ dadyāccaivādadīta vā
8.d: क्रीत्वा विक्रीय वा किं चिद्यस्यैहानुशयो भवेत् सो ऽन्तर्दशाहात् तद्द्रव्यं दद्याच्चैवाददीत वा
8.e: If, after having bought or sold anything, one should repent of it, he may return or take back that thing within ten days.

8.s: pareṇa tu daśāhasya na dadyānnāpi dāpayet ādadāno dadat caiva rājñā daṇḍyau śatāni ṣaṭ
8.d: परेण तु दशाहस्य न दद्यान्नापि दापयेत् आददानो ददत् चैव राज्ञा दण्ड्यौ शतानि षट्
8.e: But after ten days, he shall neither return nor take it back; he who takes it back, as well as he who returns it, should be fined by the king six hundred.

8.s: yastu doṣavatīṃ kanyāmanākhyāya prayacchati tasya kuryānnṛpo daṇḍaṃ svayaṃ ṣaṇṇavatiṃ paṇān
8.d: यस्तु दोषवतीं कन्यामनाख्याय प्रयच्छति तस्य कुर्यान्नृपो दण्डं स्वयं षण्णवतिं पणान्
8.e: If a man gives a defective damsel, without mentioning the defects, he should be punished by the king himself with a fine of ninety-six ‘paṇas.’

8.s: akanyaiti tu yaḥ kanyāṃ brūyāddveṣeṇa mānavaḥ sa śataṃ prāpnuyāddaṇḍaṃ tasyā doṣamadarśayan
8.d: अकन्यैति तु यः कन्यां ब्रूयाद्द्वेषेण मानवः स शतं प्राप्नुयाद्दण्डं तस्या दोषमदर्शयन्
8.e: If a man, through malice, speaks of a maiden as ‘not a virgin’ he should receive the punishment of one hundred, if unable to prove her impurity.

8.s: pāṇigrahaṇikā mantrāḥ kanyāsveva pratiṣṭhitāḥ nākanyāsu kva cinnr̥̄ṇāṃ luptadharmakriyā hi tāḥ
8.d: पाणिग्रहणिका मन्त्राः कन्यास्वेव प्रतिष्ठिताः नाकन्यासु क्व चिन्न्र्̥̄णां लुप्तधर्मक्रिया हि ताः
8.e: The marriage-ritual texts are applicable to virgins only, and nowhere among men, to non-virgins; and this because these latter are excluded from religious acts.

8.s: pāṇigrahaṇikā mantrā niyataṃ dāralakṣaṇam teṣāṃ niṣṭhā tu vijñeyā vidvadbhiḥ saptame pade
8.d: पाणिग्रहणिका मन्त्रा नियतं दारलक्षणम् तेषां निष्ठा तु विज्ञेया विद्वद्भिः सप्तमे पदे
8.e: The marriage -texts are clearly conducive to ‘wife-hood’; and these are to be recognised by the learned as completed at the ‘seventh-step.’

8.s: yasmin yasmin kṛte kārye yasyaihānuśayo bhavet tamanena vidhānena dharmye pathi niveśayet
8.d: यस्मिन् यस्मिन् कृते कार्ये यस्यैहानुशयो भवेत् तमनेन विधानेन धर्म्ये पथि निवेशयेत्
8.e: Whenever any person should have repentance in regard to any compact that has been entered into—the king shall bring him to the righteous path, in the manner just described.

8.s: paśuṣu svāmināṃ caiva pālānāṃ ca vyatikrame vivādaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi yathāvaddharmatattvataḥ
8.d: पशुषु स्वामिनां चैव पालानां च व्यतिक्रमे विवादं संप्रवक्ष्यामि यथावद्धर्मतत्त्वतः
8.e: I am going to expound fully the true law relating to disputes between owners and keepers arising from transgressions regarding cattle.

8.s: divā vaktavyatā pāle rātrau svāmini tadgṛhe yogakṣeme 'nyathā cet tu pālo vaktavyatāmiyāt
8.d: दिवा वक्तव्यता पाले रात्रौ स्वामिनि तद्गृहे योगक्षेमे ऽन्यथा चेत् तु पालो वक्तव्यतामियात्
8.e: Responsibility for the safe keeping during the day rests with the keeper, and during the night, with the owner, ip in his own house; if otherwise, the keeper should be responsible.

8.s: gopaḥ kṣīrabhṛto yastu sa duhyāddaśato varām gosvāmyanumate bhṛtyaḥ sā syāt pāle 'bhṛte bhṛtiḥ
8.d: गोपः क्षीरभृतो यस्तु स दुह्याद्दशतो वराम् गोस्वाम्यनुमते भृत्यः सा स्यात् पाले ऽभृते भृतिः
8.e: If the hired cattle-keeper is one paid with milk, he shall, with the owner’s permission, milk the best out of ten; this shall be the ‘wages’ of the keeper, if he receives no other wages.

8.s: naṣṭaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ kṛmibhiḥ śvahataṃ viṣame mṛtam hīnaṃ puruṣakāreṇa pradadyāt pāla eva tu
8.d: नष्टं विनष्टं कृमिभिः श्वहतं विषमे मृतम् हीनं पुरुषकारेण प्रदद्यात् पाल एव तु
8.e: The keeper alone should make good what has strayed, or been destroyed by worms, or killed by dogs, or has perished in an unsafe place,—if it was left without human aid.

8.s: vighuṣya tu hṛtaṃ caurairna pālo dātumarhati yadi deśe ca kāle ca svāminaḥ svasya śaṃsati
8.d: विघुष्य तु हृतं चौरैर्न पालो दातुमर्हति यदि देशे च काले च स्वामिनः स्वस्य शंसति
8.e: But the keeper shall not have to make good what has been taken away by thieves openly,—if he informs his own master of it at the proper place and time.

8.s: karṇau carma ca vālāṃśca bastiṃ snāyuṃ ca rocanām paśuṣu svāmināṃ dadyān mṛteṣvaṅkāni darśayet 'ṅkāṃśca darśayet
8.d: कर्णौ चर्म च वालांश्च बस्तिं स्नायुं च रोचनाम् पशुषु स्वामिनां दद्यान् मृतेष्वङ्कानि दर्शयेत् ऽङ्कांश्च दर्शयेत्
8.e: On the death of the animals, he shall make over to the owner their ears, skin, tail-hairs, bladder and tendons and the concrete bile, and also point out their marks.

8.s: ajāvike tu saṃruddhe vṛkaiḥ pāle tvanāyati yāṃ prasahya vṛko hanyāt pāle tat kilbiṣaṃ bhavet
8.d: अजाविके तु संरुद्धे वृकैः पाले त्वनायति यां प्रसह्य वृको हन्यात् पाले तत् किल्बिषं भवेत्
8.e: When goats and sheep have been surrounded by wolves, and the keeper does not come for ward,—if the wolf forcibly kill any, the blame shall lie with the keeper.

8.s: tāsāṃ cedavaruddhānāṃ carantīnāṃ mitho vane yāmutplutya vṛko hanyānna pālastatra kilbiṣī
8.d: तासां चेदवरुद्धानां चरन्तीनां मिथो वने यामुत्प्लुत्य वृको हन्यान्न पालस्तत्र किल्बिषी
8.e: When however, they are grazing together in the forest, duly protected,—if a wolf pounces upon one and kills it,—the keeper is not to blame.

8.s: dhanuḥśataṃ parīhāro grāmasya syāt samantataḥ śamyāpātāstrayo vā 'pi triguṇo nagarasya tu
8.d: धनुःशतं परीहारो ग्रामस्य स्यात् समन्ततः शम्यापातास्त्रयो वा ऽपि त्रिगुणो नगरस्य तु
8.e: Around the village there should be a pasture-ground, four hundred ‘bows’ or three ‘stick-throws’ (in width); but three times that space around the town.

8.s: tatrāparivṛtaṃ dhānyaṃ vihiṃsyuḥ paśavo yadi na tatra praṇayeddaṇḍaṃ nṛpatiḥ paśurakṣiṇām
8.d: तत्रापरिवृतं धान्यं विहिंस्युः पशवो यदि न तत्र प्रणयेद्दण्डं नृपतिः पशुरक्षिणाम्
8.e: If the cattle damage the unfenced crops therein, the king, in that case, shall not inflict punishment on the cattle-keepers.

8.s: vṛtiṃ tatra prakurvīta yāmuṣtro na vilokayet chidraṃ ca vārayet sarvaṃ śvasūkaramukhānugam
8.d: वृतिं तत्र प्रकुर्वीत यामुष्त्रो न विलोकयेत् छिद्रं च वारयेत् सर्वं श्वसूकरमुखानुगम्
8.e: One should set up an enclosure there which the camel cannot see, and shut up every opening through which the head of a dog ok a boar could be thrust.

8.s: pathi kṣetre parivṛte grāmāntīye 'tha vā punaḥ sapālaḥ śatadaṇḍārho vipālān vārayet paśūn
8.d: पथि क्षेत्रे परिवृते ग्रामान्तीये ऽथ वा पुनः सपालः शतदण्डार्हो विपालान् वारयेत् पशून्
8.e: If cattle attended by the keeper be found in an enclosed field, on the road-side or near the village, the keeper should be fined a hundred; but cattle without a keeper shall be driven off.

8.s: kṣetreṣvanyeṣu tu paśuḥ sapādaṃ paṇamarhati sarvatra tu sado deyaḥ kṣetrikasyaiti dhāraṇā
8.d: क्षेत्रेष्वन्येषु तु पशुः सपादं पणमर्हति सर्वत्र तु सदो देयः क्षेत्रिकस्यैति धारणा
8.e: In the case of other fields, the cattle-keeper should be fined a ‘paṇa’ and a quarter; and in all cases the crop shall be made good to the owner of the field; such is the established rule.

8.s: anirdaśāhāṃ gāṃ sūtāṃ vṛṣān devapaśūṃstathā sapālān vā vipālān vā na daṇḍyān manurabravīt
8.d: अनिर्दशाहां गां सूतां वृषान् देवपशूंस्तथा सपालान् वा विपालान् वा न दण्ड्यान् मनुरब्रवीत्
8.e: But Manu has declared that no punishment shall be inflicted upon a cow within ten days of its calving, or bulls or dedicated cattle,—whether with or without keepers.

8.s: kṣetriyasyātyaye daṇḍo bhāgāddaśaguṇo bhavet kṣetrikasyātyaye tato 'rdhadaṇḍo bhṛtyānāmajñānāt kṣetrikasya tu
8.d: क्षेत्रियस्यात्यये दण्डो भागाद्दशगुणो भवेत् क्षेत्रिकस्यात्यये ततो ऽर्धदण्डो भृत्यानामज्ञानात् क्षेत्रिकस्य तु
8.e: When there is transgression on the part of the farmer himself, his fine shall be ten times the royal share,—half of that in the case of servants, if it is unknown to the farmer.

8.s: etadvidhānamātiṣṭheddhārmikaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ svāmināṃ ca paśūnāṃ ca pālānāṃ ca vyatikrame
8.d: एतद्विधानमातिष्ठेद्धार्मिकः पृथिवीपतिः स्वामिनां च पशूनां च पालानां च व्यतिक्रमे
8.e: This is the rule that the righteous king shall observe, in the case of transgressions by owners, by cattle and by the keepers.

8.s: sīmāṃ prati samutpanne vivāde grāmayordvayoḥ jyeṣṭhe māsi nayet sīmāṃ suprakāśeṣu setuṣu
8.d: सीमां प्रति समुत्पन्ने विवादे ग्रामयोर्द्वयोः ज्येष्ठे मासि नयेत् सीमां सुप्रकाशेषु सेतुषु
8.e: When a dispute regarding boundaries arises between two villages, the king shall settle the boundary during the month of Jyeṣṭha, when the landmarks are distinctly perceptible.

8.s: sīṃāvṛkṣāṃśca kurvīta nyagrodhāśvatthakiṃśukān śālmalīn sālatālāṃśca kṣīriṇaścaiva pādapān
8.d: सींआवृक्षांश्च कुर्वीत न्यग्रोधाश्वत्थकिंशुकान् शाल्मलीन् सालतालांश्च क्षीरिणश्चैव पादपान्
8.e: He shall plant boundary-trees,—such as the Nyagrodha, the Aśvattha, the Kiṃśuka, the Śālmalī, the Sāla and the Tāla,—as also plants with milky juice.

8.s: gulmān veṇūṃśca vividhān śamīvallīsthalāni ca śarān kubjakagulmāṃśca tathā sīmā na naśyati
8.d: गुल्मान् वेणूंश्च विविधान् शमीवल्लीस्थलानि च शरान् कुब्जकगुल्मांश्च तथा सीमा न नश्यति
8.e: Also thickets, bamboos of various kinds, the Śamī-tree, creepers and mounds, reeds and Kubjaka thickets; trees shall not be obliterated.

8.s: taḍāgānyudapānāni vāpyaḥ prasravaṇāni ca sīmāsaṃdhiṣu kāryāṇi devatāyatanāni ca
8.d: तडागान्युदपानानि वाप्यः प्रस्रवणानि च सीमासंधिषु कार्याणि देवतायतनानि च
8.e: Tanks, water-reservoirs, ponds and fountains should be built on boundary-links; as also temples.

8.s: upachannāni cānyāni sīmāliṅgāni kārayet sīmājñāne nṛṇāṃ vīkṣya nityaṃ loke viparyayam
8.d: उपछन्नानि चान्यानि सीमालिङ्गानि कारयेत् सीमाज्ञाने नृणां वीक्ष्य नित्यं लोके विपर्ययम्
8.e: He shall also set up hidden boundary-marks,—seeing that in the world there are constant trespasses, due to the ignorance of boundaries among men.

8.s: aśmano 'sthīni govālāṃstuṣān bhasma kapālikāḥ karīṣamiṣṭakā 'ṅgārāṃśśarkarā vālukāstathā
8.d: अश्मनो ऽस्थीनि गोवालांस्तुषान् भस्म कपालिकाः करीषमिष्टका ऽङ्गारांश्शर्करा वालुकास्तथा
8.e: As also, stones, bones, cow’s hair, chaff, ashes, potsherds, dry cow dung, bricks, cinders, pebbles, and sand.

8.s: yāni caivaṃprakārāṇi kālādbhūmirna bhakṣayet tāni saṃdhiṣu sīmāyāmaprakāśāni kārayet sīmāyā
8.d: यानि चैवंप्रकाराणि कालाद्भूमिर्न भक्षयेत् तानि संधिषु सीमायामप्रकाशानि कारयेत् सीमाया
8.e: Other such-like things which the earth may not eat up in time,—these he shall secretly set up on junctions of boundaries.

8.s: etairliṅgairnayet sīmāṃ rājā vivadamānayoḥ pūrvabhuktyā ca satatamudakasyāgamena ca
8.d: एतैर्लिङ्गैर्नयेत् सीमां राजा विवदमानयोः पूर्वभुक्त्या च सततमुदकस्यागमेन च
8.e: By these signs shall the king determine the boundary between two contending parties; as also by long-continued possession and by flowing streams of water.

8.s: yadi sṃśaya eva syātliṅgānāmapi darśane sākṣipratyaya eva syāt sīmāvādavinirṇayaḥ sīmāvādaviniścayaḥ
8.d: यदि स्ंशय एव स्यात्लिङ्गानामपि दर्शने साक्षिप्रत्यय एव स्यात् सीमावादविनिर्णयः सीमावादविनिश्चयः
8.e: If, even on the inspection of the marks, there should be a doubt, the settlement of the dispute regarding boundaries shall be entirely dependent upon witnesses.

8.s: grāmīyakakulānāṃ ca samakṣaṃ sīmni sākṣiṇaḥ grāmeyaka praṣṭavyāḥ sīmaliṅgāni tayoścaiva vivādinoḥ sīmāliṅgāni
8.d: ग्रामीयककुलानां च समक्षं सीम्नि साक्षिणः ग्रामेयक प्रष्टव्याः सीमलिङ्गानि तयोश्चैव विवादिनोः सीमालिङ्गानि
8.e: Witnesses regarding boundaries shall be questioned in regard to the boundary-marks, in the presence of an assembly of villagers and also of the two contending parties.

8.s: te pṛṣtāstu yathā brūyuḥ samastāḥ sīmni niścayam nibadhnīyāt tathā sīmāṃ sarvāṃstāṃścaiva nāmataḥ
8.d: ते पृष्तास्तु यथा ब्रूयुः समस्ताः सीम्नि निश्चयम् निबध्नीयात् तथा सीमां सर्वांस्तांश्चैव नामतः
8.e: The opinion that, on being questioned, they unanimously declare in regard to the boundary,—according to that he shall lay down the boundary, recording also the names of them all.

8.s: śirobhiste gṛhītvaurvīṃ sragviṇo raktavāsasaḥ sukṛtaiḥ śāpithāḥ svaiḥ svairnayeyuste samañjasam
8.d: शिरोभिस्ते गृहीत्वौर्वीं स्रग्विणो रक्तवाससः सुकृतैः शापिथाः स्वैः स्वैर्नयेयुस्ते समञ्जसम्
8.e: Placing earth upon their heads, wearing garlands and red clothes, and being sworn by their respective meritorious deeds, they shall decide honestly.

8.s: yathauktena nayantaste pūyante satyasākṣiṇaḥ viparītaṃ nayantastu dāpyāḥ syurdviśataṃ damam
8.d: यथौक्तेन नयन्तस्ते पूयन्ते सत्यसाक्षिणः विपरीतं नयन्तस्तु दाप्याः स्युर्द्विशतं दमम्
8.e: If they decide in the right manner, they, being truthful witnesses, become purified; but if they decide contrariwise, they should be made to pay a fine of two hundred.

8.s: sākṣyabhāve tu catvāro grāmāḥ sāmantavāsinaḥ grāmasīmāntavāsinaḥ sīmāvinirṇayaṃ kuryuḥ prayatā rājasaṃnidhau
8.d: साक्ष्यभावे तु चत्वारो ग्रामाः सामन्तवासिनः ग्रामसीमान्तवासिनः सीमाविनिर्णयं कुर्युः प्रयता राजसंनिधौ
8.e: In the absence of witnesses four honest inhabitants of neighbouring villages shall make the determination of the boundary, in the presence of the king.

8.s: sāmantānāmabhāve tu maulānāṃ sīmni sākṣiṇām imānapyanuyuñjīta puruṣān vanagocarān
8.d: सामन्तानामभावे तु मौलानां सीम्नि साक्षिणाम् इमानप्यनुयुञ्जीत पुरुषान् वनगोचरान्
8.e: In the absence of such original inhabitants of neighbouring villages as could be witnesses in regard to the boundary, the king may examine these (following) frequenters of forests also.

8.s: vyādhāṃśākunikān gopān kaivartān mūlakhānakān vyālagrāhānuñchavṛttīnanyāṃśca vanacāriṇaḥ
8.d: व्याधांशाकुनिकान् गोपान् कैवर्तान् मूलखानकान् व्यालग्राहानुञ्छवृत्तीनन्यांश्च वनचारिणः
8.e: Hunters, Fowlers, Cowherds, Fishermen, Root-diggers, Snake-catchers, Gleaners and other Foresters.

8.s: te pṛṣṭāstu yathā brūyuḥ sīmāsaṃdhiṣu lakṣaṇam tat tathā sthāpayedrājā dharmeṇa grāmayordvayoḥ
8.d: ते पृष्टास्तु यथा ब्रूयुः सीमासंधिषु लक्षणम् तत् तथा स्थापयेद्राजा धर्मेण ग्रामयोर्द्वयोः
8.e: As they, on being questioned in fairness, declare the marks of boundary-lines between two villages, even so shall the king fix it.

8.s: kṣetrakūpataḍāgānāmārāmasya gṛhasya ca sāmantapratyayo jñeyaḥ sīmāsetuvinirṇayaḥ
8.d: क्षेत्रकूपतडागानामारामस्य गृहस्य च सामन्तप्रत्ययो ज्ञेयः सीमासेतुविनिर्णयः
8.e: In the case of fields, walls, tanks, gardens and houses, the decision regarding boundary-marks is dependent upon the neighbours.

8.s: sāmantāścetmṛṣā brūyuḥ setau vivādatāṃ nṛṇām sarve pṛthak pṛthag daṇḍyā rājñā madhyamasāhasam
8.d: सामन्ताश्चेत्मृषा ब्रूयुः सेतौ विवादतां नृणाम् सर्वे पृथक् पृथग् दण्ड्या राज्ञा मध्यमसाहसम्
8.e: In the case of men disputing about boundary-marks, if the neighbours depose falsely, all of them should be severally punished by the king with the ‘middle amercement.’

8.s: gṛhaṃ taḍāgamārāmaṃ kṣetraṃ vā bhīṣayā haran śatāni pañca daṇḍyaḥ syādajñānāddviśato damaḥ
8.d: गृहं तडागमारामं क्षेत्रं वा भीषया हरन् शतानि पञ्च दण्ड्यः स्यादज्ञानाद्द्विशतो दमः
8.e: If a person, by intimidation, appropriates a house, a tank, a garden, or a field, he shall be fined five hundred; but only two hundred, if he does it in ignorance.

8.s: sīmāyāmaviṣahyāyāṃ svayaṃ rājaiva dharmavit pradiśedbhūmimekeṣāmupakārāditi sthitiḥ
8.d: सीमायामविषह्यायां स्वयं राजैव धर्मवित् प्रदिशेद्भूमिमेकेषामुपकारादिति स्थितिः
8.e: In the event of the boundary being unascertainable, the righteous king shall himself assign to them their lands, on the basis of advantages. Such is the established law.

8.s: eṣo 'khilenābhihito dharmaḥ sīmāvinirṇaye ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi vākpāruṣyavinirṇayam
8.d: एषो ऽखिलेनाभिहितो धर्मः सीमाविनिर्णये अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि वाक्पारुष्यविनिर्णयम्
8.e: Thus has the whole law relating to the demarcation of boundaries been propounded. After this I am going to expound that relating to verbal assault.

8.s: śataṃ brāhmaṇamākruśya kṣatriyo daṇḍamarhati vaiśyo 'pyardhaśataṃ dve vā śūdrastu vadhamarhati
8.d: शतं ब्राह्मणमाक्रुश्य क्षत्रियो दण्डमर्हति वैश्यो ऽप्यर्धशतं द्वे वा शूद्रस्तु वधमर्हति
8.e: On abusing a Brāhmaṇa the Kṣatriya should be fined one hundred; and the Vaiśya one hundred and fifty; or two hundred; the Śūdra however deserves immolation.

8.s: pañcāśadbrāhmaṇo daṇḍyaḥ kṣatriyasyābhiśaṃsane vaiśye syādardhapañcāśatśūdre dvādaśako damaḥ
8.d: पञ्चाशद्ब्राह्मणो दण्ड्यः क्षत्रियस्याभिशंसने वैश्ये स्यादर्धपञ्चाशत्शूद्रे द्वादशको दमः
8.e: For abusing a Kṣatriya, the Brāhmaṇa should be fined fifty; and in the case of a Vaiśya, the fine shall be twenty-five; and in that of a Shudra, twelve.

8.s: samavarṇe dvijātīnāṃ dvādaśaiva vyatikrame vādeṣvavacanīyeṣu tadeva dviguṇaṃ bhavet
8.d: समवर्णे द्विजातीनां द्वादशैव व्यतिक्रमे वादेष्ववचनीयेषु तदेव द्विगुणं भवेत्
8.e: Among twice-born men, when there is offence against an equal, the fine is twelve only in the case of unutterable abuses, it shall be double.

8.s: ekajātirdvijātīṃstu vācā dāruṇayā kṣipan jihvāyāḥ prāpnuyācchedaṃ jaghanyaprabhavo hi saḥ
8.d: एकजातिर्द्विजातींस्तु वाचा दारुणया क्षिपन् जिह्वायाः प्राप्नुयाच्छेदं जघन्यप्रभवो हि सः
8.e: If a once-born person insults a twice-born one with gross abuse, he should suffer the cutting off of his tongue; as he is of low origin.

8.s: nāmajātigrahaṃ tveṣāmabhidroheṇa kurvataḥ nikṣepyo 'yomayaḥ śaṅkurjvalannāsye daśāṅgulaḥ
8.d: नामजातिग्रहं त्वेषामभिद्रोहेण कुर्वतः निक्षेप्यो ऽयोमयः शङ्कुर्ज्वलन्नास्ये दशाङ्गुलः
8.e: If he mentions the name and caste of these men with scorn, a burning iron nail ten inches long shall be thrust into his mouth.

8.s: dharmaupadeśaṃ darpeṇa viprāṇāmasya kurvataḥ taptamāsecayet tailaṃ vaktre śrotre ca pārthivaḥ śrautre
8.d: धर्मौपदेशं दर्पेण विप्राणामस्य कुर्वतः तप्तमासेचयेत् तैलं वक्त्रे श्रोत्रे च पार्थिवः श्रौत्रे
8.e: If through arrogance, he teaches brāhmaṇas their duty, the king shall pour heated oil into his mouth and ears.

8.s: śrutaṃ deśaṃ ca jātiṃ ca karma śarīrameva ca vitathena bruvan darpāddāpyaḥ syāddviśataṃ damam
8.d: श्रुतं देशं च जातिं च कर्म शरीरमेव च वितथेन ब्रुवन् दर्पाद्दाप्यः स्याद्द्विशतं दमम्
8.e: He who, through arrogance, speaks falsely regarding the learning, the habitat, the caste, the occupation, or the bodily details (of another person), should be made to pay a pine of two hundred.

8.s: kāṇaṃ vā 'pyatha vā khañjamanyaṃ vā 'pi tathāvidham tathyenāpi bruvan dāpyo daṇḍaṃ kārṣāpaṇāvaram
8.d: काणं वा ऽप्यथ वा खञ्जमन्यं वा ऽपि तथाविधम् तथ्येनापि ब्रुवन् दाप्यो दण्डं कार्षापणावरम्
8.e: If a man, even truly, calls another ‘one-eyed’ or ‘lame’ or something else like it,—he should be made to pay a fine of at least one ‘Kārṣāpaṇa.’

8.s: mātaraṃ pitaraṃ jāyāṃ bhrātaraṃ tanayaṃ gurum ākṣārayaṃśataṃ dāpyaḥ panthānaṃ cādadadguroḥ
8.d: मातरं पितरं जायां भ्रातरं तनयं गुरुम् आक्षारयंशतं दाप्यः पन्थानं चाददद्गुरोः
8.e: He who alienates the mother, the father, the wife, the brother, the child or the preceptor, should be made to pay a hundred; as also one who does not give the way to his preceptor.

8.s: brāhmaṇakṣatriyābhyāṃ tu daṇḍaḥ kāryo vijānatā brāhmaṇe sāhasaḥ pūrvaḥ kṣatriye tveva madhyamaḥ
8.d: ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियाभ्यां तु दण्डः कार्यो विजानता ब्राह्मणे साहसः पूर्वः क्षत्रिये त्वेव मध्यमः
8.e: The discerning king shall inflict this punishment upon the Brāhmaṇa and the Kṣatriya: the brāhmaṇa shall be fined the lowest amercement and the kṣatriya the middlemost

8.s: viśśūdrayorevameva svajātiṃ prati tattvataḥ chedavarjaṃ praṇayanaṃ daṇḍasyaiti viniścayaḥ
8.d: विश्शूद्रयोरेवमेव स्वजातिं प्रति तत्त्वतः छेदवर्जं प्रणयनं दण्डस्यैति विनिश्चयः
8.e: On the Vaiśya and the Śūdra also, the inflicting of punishment shall be of the same kind, according to their respective castes,—barring mutilation; such is the decision.

8.s: eṣa daṇḍavidhiḥ prokto vākpāruṣyasya tattvataḥ ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi daṇḍapāruṣyanirṇayam
8.d: एष दण्डविधिः प्रोक्तो वाक्पारुष्यस्य तत्त्वतः अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि दण्डपारुष्यनिर्णयम्
8.e: Thus the law relating to punishments in connection with verbal assaults been truly expounded; after thisI am going to profound the law relating to physical assault.

8.s: yena kena cidaṅgena hiṃsyāccetśreṣṭhamantyajaḥ chettavyaṃ tadtadevāsya tan manoranuśāsanam
8.d: येन केन चिदङ्गेन हिंस्याच्चेत्श्रेष्ठमन्त्यजः छेत्तव्यं तद्तदेवास्य तन् मनोरनुशासनम्
8.e: With whatever limb the low-born man hurts a superior person, every such limb of his shall be cut off; this is the teaching of Manu.

8.s: pāṇimudyamya daṇḍaṃ vā pāṇicchedanamarhati pādena praharan kopāt pādacchedanamarhati
8.d: पाणिमुद्यम्य दण्डं वा पाणिच्छेदनमर्हति पादेन प्रहरन् कोपात् पादच्छेदनमर्हति
8.e: If he raises his hand or a stick, he should have his hand cut off; if he strikes in anger with the foot, his foot shall be cut off.

8.s: sahāsanamabhiprepsurutkṛṣṭasyāpakṛṣṭajaḥ kaṭyāṃ kṛtāṅko nirvāsyaḥ sphicaṃ vā 'syāvakartayet
8.d: सहासनमभिप्रेप्सुरुत्कृष्टस्यापकृष्टजः कट्यां कृताङ्को निर्वास्यः स्फिचं वा ऽस्यावकर्तयेत्
8.e: If a low-born person tries to occupy the same seat with his superior, he should be branded on the hip and banished; or the king shall have his buttocks cut off.

8.s: avaniṣṭhīvato darpāddvāvoṣṭhau chedayennṛpaḥ avamūtrayato meḍhramavaśardhayato gudam
8.d: अवनिष्ठीवतो दर्पाद्द्वावोष्ठौ छेदयेन्नृपः अवमूत्रयतो मेढ्रमवशर्धयतो गुदम्
8.e: If, out of arrogance, he spits, the king should have his two lips cut off; if he urinates, then his penis; and if he breaks wind, his anus.

8.s: keśeṣu gṛhṇato hastau chedayedavicārayan pādayordāḍhikāyāṃ ca grīvāyāṃ vṛṣaṇeṣu ca
8.d: केशेषु गृह्णतो हस्तौ छेदयेदविचारयन् पादयोर्दाढिकायां च ग्रीवायां वृषणेषु च
8.e: If he catches hold of the hair, the king shall unhesitatingly have his hands out off; also if he lays hold of the feet, the beard, the neck, or the scrotum.

8.s: tvagbhedakaḥ śataṃ daṇḍyo lohitasya ca darśakaḥ māṃsabhettā tu ṣaṭniṣkān pravāsyastvasthibhedakaḥ
8.d: त्वग्भेदकः शतं दण्ड्यो लोहितस्य च दर्शकः मांसभेत्ता तु षट्निष्कान् प्रवास्यस्त्वस्थिभेदकः
8.e: One who bruises the skin should be fined one hundred; as also one who fetches blood; he who cuts the flesh, six ‘niṣkas’ and the bone-breaker should be banished.

8.s: vanaspatīnāṃ sarveṣāmupabhogo yathā yathā yathā tathā damaḥ kāryo hiṃsāyāmiti dhāraṇā
8.d: वनस्पतीनां सर्वेषामुपभोगो यथा यथा यथा तथा दमः कार्यो हिंसायामिति धारणा
8.e: In the case of all trees, as their usefulness so should be the punishment inflicted for injuring them; this is the settled rule.

8.s: manuṣyāṇāṃ paśūnāṃ ca duḥkhāya prahṛte sati yathā yathā mahadduḥkhaṃ daṇḍaṃ kuryāt tathā tathā
8.d: मनुष्याणां पशूनां च दुःखाय प्रहृते सति यथा यथा महद्दुःखं दण्डं कुर्यात् तथा तथा
8.e: When a hurt has been inflicted on men or animals, with the motive of causing pain, the king shall inflict punishment in proportion to the greatness of the pain caused.

8.s: aṅgāvapīḍanāyāṃ ca vraṇaśonitayostathā prāṇaśonitayoḥ samutthānavyayaṃ dāpyaḥ sarvadaṇḍamathāpi vā
8.d: अङ्गावपीडनायां च व्रणशोनितयोस्तथा प्राणशोनितयोः समुत्थानव्ययं दाप्यः सर्वदण्डमथापि वा
8.e: In the case of injury to limbs, as also of strength and of blood,—the man should be made to pay the expenses of recovery, or the whole amount as ‘fine.’

8.s: dravyāṇi hiṃsyādyo yasya jñānato 'jñānato 'pi vā sa tasyautpādayet tuṣṭiṃ rājñe dadyācca tatsamam
8.d: द्रव्याणि हिंस्याद्यो यस्य ज्ञानतो ऽज्ञानतो ऽपि वा स तस्यौत्पादयेत् तुष्टिं राज्ञे दद्याच्च तत्समम्
8.e: When a man, either intentionally or unintentionally, damages the goods of another, he shall give satisfaction to him and pay to the king a fine equal to it.

8.s: carmacārmikabhāṇḍeṣu kāṣṭhaloṣṭamayeṣu mūlyāt pañcaguṇo daṇḍaḥ puṣpamūlaphaleṣu ca
8.d: चर्मचार्मिकभाण्डेषु काष्ठलोष्टमयेषु मूल्यात् पञ्चगुणो दण्डः पुष्पमूलफलेषु च
8.e: In the case or leather and leathern vessels, and in that of those made of wood or clay, the fine shall be five times their value; as also in the case of flowers, roots and fruits.

8.s: yānasya caiva yātuśca yānasvāmina eva ca daśātivartanānyāhuḥ śeṣe daṇḍo vidhīyate
8.d: यानस्य चैव यातुश्च यानस्वामिन एव च दशातिवर्तनान्याहुः शेषे दण्डो विधीयते
8.e: In the case of the conveyance, its rider and its owner, they lay down ten exclusions; for the rest penalties are prescribed.

8.s: chinnanāsye bhagnayuge tiryakpratimukhāgate akṣabhaṅge ca yānasya cakrabhaṅge tathaiva ca
8.d: छिन्ननास्ये भग्नयुगे तिर्यक्प्रतिमुखागते अक्षभङ्गे च यानस्य चक्रभङ्गे तथैव च
8.e: When there is snapping of the nose-string, when the yoke is broken, when it turns sideways or backwards, when the axle breaks, and when the wheel is broken; (291) when the fittings or the yoking strap or the bridle are torn, and when there has been the loud cry ‘get out of the way,’—there is no punishment; so has Manu declared

8.s: chedane caiva yantrāṇāṃ yoktraraśmyostathaiva ca ākrande cāpyapaihīti na daṇḍaṃ manurabravīt
8.d: छेदने चैव यन्त्राणां योक्त्ररश्म्योस्तथैव च आक्रन्दे चाप्यपैहीति न दण्डं मनुरब्रवीत्
8.e: When there is snapping of the nose-string, when the yoke is broken, when it turns sideways or backwards, when the axle breaks, and when the wheel is broken; (291) when the fittings or the yoking strap or the bridle are torn, and when there has been the loud cry ‘get out of the way,’—there is no punishment; so has Manu declared

8.s: yatrāpavartate yugyaṃ vaiguṇyāt prājakasya tu tatra svāmī bhaveddaṇḍyo hiṃsāyāṃ dviśataṃ damam
8.d: यत्रापवर्तते युग्यं वैगुण्यात् प्राजकस्य तु तत्र स्वामी भवेद्दण्ड्यो हिंसायां द्विशतं दमम्
8.e: When however, on account of the driver’s ineptitude, the cart turns off and causes injury, the owner shall be punished with a fine of two hundred.—(293) If the driver is a trained one, it is he that should be punished; if the driver is untrained, all the occupants of the cart should be fined a hundred each.

8.s: prājakaścedbhavedāptaḥ prājako daṇḍamarhati yugyasthāḥ prājake 'nāpte sarve daṇḍyāḥ śataṃ śatam
8.d: प्राजकश्चेद्भवेदाप्तः प्राजको दण्डमर्हति युग्यस्थाः प्राजके ऽनाप्ते सर्वे दण्ड्याः शतं शतम्
8.e: When however, on account of the driver’s ineptitude, the cart turns off and causes injury, the owner shall be punished with a fine of two hundred.—(293) If the driver is a trained one, it is he that should be punished; if the driver is untrained, all the occupants of the cart should be fined a hundred each.

8.s: sa cet tu pathi saṃruddhaḥ paśubhirvā rathena vā pramāpayet prāṇabhṛtastatra daṇḍo 'vicāritaḥ
8.d: स चेत् तु पथि संरुद्धः पशुभिर्वा रथेन वा प्रमापयेत् प्राणभृतस्तत्र दण्डो ऽविचारितः
8.e: But if he happens to be stopped on the road and causes the death of a living being, either through animals or through the cart,—in such a case there is no doubt regarding punishment.

8.s: manuṣyamāraṇe kṣipraṃ cauravat kilbiṣaṃ bhavet prāṇabhṛtsu mahatsvardhaṃ gogajauṣṭrahayādiṣu
8.d: मनुष्यमारणे क्षिप्रं चौरवत् किल्बिषं भवेत् प्राणभृत्सु महत्स्वर्धं गोगजौष्ट्रहयादिषु
8.e: If the case of a man being killed, on the spot, the guilt would be similar to that of the thief; and half of that in the case of the larger animals, such as cows, elephants, camels, horses and the like.

8.s: kṣudrakāṇāṃ paśūnāṃ tu hiṃsāyāṃ dviśato damaḥ pañcāśat tu bhaveddaṇḍaḥ śubheṣu mṛgapakṣiṣu
8.d: क्षुद्रकाणां पशूनां तु हिंसायां द्विशतो दमः पञ्चाशत् तु भवेद्दण्डः शुभेषु मृगपक्षिषु
8.e: In the case of hurting petty animals, the fine is two h undred; and fifty in the case of the auspicious quadrupeds and birds.

8.s: gardhabhājāvikānāṃ tu daṇḍaḥ syāt pañcamāṣikaḥ pāñcamāṣikaḥ māṣikastu bhaveddaṇḍaḥ śvasūkaranipātane
8.d: गर्धभाजाविकानां तु दण्डः स्यात् पञ्चमाषिकः पाञ्चमाषिकः माषिकस्तु भवेद्दण्डः श्वसूकरनिपातने
8.e: In the case of donkeys, goat and sheep the fine shall consist of five ‘māṣas’; and the fine shall be one ‘māṣa’ for the killing of a dog ok a pig.

8.s: bhāryā putraśca dāsaśca preṣyo bhrātrā ca saudaraḥ prāptāparādhāstāḍyāḥ syū rajjvā veṇudalena vā
8.d: भार्या पुत्रश्च दासश्च प्रेष्यो भ्रात्रा च सौदरः प्राप्तापराधास्ताड्याः स्यू रज्ज्वा वेणुदलेन वा
8.e: The wife, the son, the slave, the servant and the uterine brother shall be beaten with a rope or a split bamboo, when they have committed a fault.

8.s: pṛṣṭhatastu śarīrasya nauttamāṅge kathaṃ cana ato 'nyathā tu praharan prāptaḥ syāccaurakilbiṣam
8.d: पृष्ठतस्तु शरीरस्य नौत्तमाङ्गे कथं चन अतो ऽन्यथा तु प्रहरन् प्राप्तः स्याच्चौरकिल्बिषम्
8.e: But only on the back part of the body, and never on the upper part; he who strikes otherwise than this incurs the guilt of a thief.

8.s: eṣo 'khilenābhihito daṇḍapāruṣyanirṇayaḥ stenasyātaḥ pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ daṇḍavinirṇaye
8.d: एषो ऽखिलेनाभिहितो दण्डपारुष्यनिर्णयः स्तेनस्यातः प्रवक्ष्यामि विधिं दण्डविनिर्णये
8.e: Thus has the law relating to physical assault been fully explained; after this I am going to expound the law for the regulating of punishments in cases of theft.

8.s: paramaṃ yatnamātiṣṭhet stenānāṃ nigrahe nṛpaḥ stenānāṃ nigrahādasya yaśo rāṣṭraṃ ca vardhate
8.d: परमं यत्नमातिष्ठेत् स्तेनानां निग्रहे नृपः स्तेनानां निग्रहादस्य यशो राष्ट्रं च वर्धते
8.e: The King shall, make the best efforts for suppressing thieves; by the suppression of thieves comes fame and the kingdom prospers.

8.s: abhayasya hi yo dātā sa pūjyaḥ satataṃ nṛpaḥ sattraṃ hi vardhate tasya sadaivābhayadakṣiṇam
8.d: अभयस्य हि यो दाता स पूज्यः सततं नृपः सत्त्रं हि वर्धते तस्य सदैवाभयदक्षिणम्
8.e: The King who imparts security is ever to be honoured; his sacrificial session constantly prospers, accompanied as it is by the gift of ‘security.’

8.s: sarvato dharmaṣaḍbhāgo rājño bhavati rakṣataḥ adharmādapi ṣaḍbhāgo bhavatyasya hyarakṣataḥ
8.d: सर्वतो धर्मषड्भागो राज्ञो भवति रक्षतः अधर्मादपि षड्भागो भवत्यस्य ह्यरक्षतः
8.e: To the King who protects (his people) accrues the sixth part of the spiritual merit of all persons; and the sixth of their demerit also accrues to him, if he protects them not

8.s: yadadhīte yadyajate yaddadāti yadarcati tasya ṣaḍbhāgabhāg rājā samyag bhavati rakṣaṇāt
8.d: यदधीते यद्यजते यद्ददाति यदर्चति तस्य षड्भागभाग् राजा सम्यग् भवति रक्षणात्
8.e: When one reads the Veda, when one performs a sacrifice, when one makes gifts, when one worships,—to the sixth part of each of those the king becomes entitled, in consequence of properly protecting the people

8.s: rakṣan dharmeṇa bhūtāni rājā vadhyāṃśca ghātayan yajate 'haraharyajñaiḥ sahasraśatadakṣiṇaiḥ
8.d: रक्षन् धर्मेण भूतानि राजा वध्यांश्च घातयन् यजते ऽहरहर्यज्ञैः सहस्रशतदक्षिणैः
8.e: The king who, according to the law, protects all creatures and strikes them who deserve to be struck, offers, day by day, sacrifices at which hundreds of thousands are given away.

8.s: yo 'rakṣan balimādatte karaṃ śulkaṃ ca pārthivaḥ pratibhāgaṃ ca daṇḍaṃ ca sa sadyo narakaṃ vrajet
8.d: यो ऽरक्षन् बलिमादत्ते करं शुल्कं च पार्थिवः प्रतिभागं च दण्डं च स सद्यो नरकं व्रजेत्
8.e: The king, who, without affording protection, takes tributes, taxes, duties, presents and fines, would immediately sink into hell.

8.s: arakṣitāraṃ rājānaṃ baliṣaḍbhāgahāriṇam arakṣitāramattāraṃ tamāhuḥ sarvalokasya samagramalahārakam
8.d: अरक्षितारं राजानं बलिषड्भागहारिणम् अरक्षितारमत्तारं तमाहुः सर्वलोकस्य समग्रमलहारकम्
8.e: He who affords no protection and devours the people, grabbing his tribute of the sixth part of the produce,—him they declare to be the imbiber of the filth of the whole people.

8.s: anapekṣitamaryādaṃ nāstikaṃ vipraluṃpakam 'navekṣitamaryādaṃ arakṣitāramattāraṃ nṛpaṃ vidyādadhogatim
8.d: अनपेक्षितमर्यादं नास्तिकं विप्रलुंपकम् ऽनवेक्षितमर्यादं अरक्षितारमत्तारं नृपं विद्यादधोगतिम्
8.e: He who heeds not the bounds of morality, who is a disbeliever, who is extortionate, who does not afford protection, and is grabbing,—such a king one should regard as doomed to perdition.

8.s: adhārmikaṃ tribhirnyāyairnigṛhṇīyāt prayatnataḥ nirodhanena bandhena vividhena vadhena ca
8.d: अधार्मिकं त्रिभिर्न्यायैर्निगृह्णीयात् प्रयत्नतः निरोधनेन बन्धेन विविधेन वधेन च
8.e: He shall carefully suppress the unrighteous by three modes (of restraint)—by imprisonment, by enchaining and by various forms of ‘immolation.’

8.s: nigraheṇa hi pāpānāṃ sādhūnāṃ saṅgraheṇa ca dvijātaya ivaijyābhiḥ pūyante satataṃ nṛpāḥ
8.d: निग्रहेण हि पापानां साधूनां सङ्ग्रहेण च द्विजातय इवैज्याभिः पूयन्ते सततं नृपाः
8.e: For by suppressing the vicious and postering the virtuous, kings become purified, just as twice-born men by the daily sacrifices.

8.s: kṣantavyaṃ prabhuṇā nityaṃ kṣipatāṃ kāryiṇāṃ nṛṇām bālavṛddhāturāṇāṃ ca kurvatā hitamātmanaḥ
8.d: क्षन्तव्यं प्रभुणा नित्यं क्षिपतां कार्यिणां नृणाम् बालवृद्धातुराणां च कुर्वता हितमात्मनः
8.e: The king should always forgive the partisans of litigants who abuse him, as also the young, the aged and the infirm,—thereby accomplishing his own welfare.

8.s: yaḥ kṣipto marṣayatyārtaistena svarge mahīyate yastvaiśvaryānna kṣamate narakaṃ tena gacchati
8.d: यः क्षिप्तो मर्षयत्यार्तैस्तेन स्वर्गे महीयते यस्त्वैश्वर्यान्न क्षमते नरकं तेन गच्छति
8.e: He who, on being abused by men in distress, forgives, becomes exalted to heaven, by that act; while he who, through kingly pride, does not forgive, goes, by that act, to hell.

8.s: rājā stenena gantavyo muktakeśena dhāvatā dhīmatā ācakṣāṇena tat steyamevaṅkarmā 'smi śādhi mām
8.d: राजा स्तेनेन गन्तव्यो मुक्तकेशेन धावता धीमता आचक्षाणेन तत् स्तेयमेवङ्कर्मा ऽस्मि शाधि माम्
8.e: The wise thief shall approach the king, with flying hair, confessing the theft, with the words—‘I have done this, punish me’;

8.s: skandhenādāya musalaṃ laguḍaṃ vā 'pi khādiram muśalaṃ śaktiṃ caubhayatastīkṣṇāmāyasaṃ daṇḍameva vā
8.d: स्कन्धेनादाय मुसलं लगुडं वा ऽपि खादिरम् मुशलं शक्तिं चौभयतस्तीक्ष्णामायसं दण्डमेव वा
8.e: —Carrying on his shoulder a pestle, or a Club of khadira wood, or a spear sharp at both ends, or an iron staff.

8.s: śāsanādvā vimokṣādvā stenaḥ steyādvimucyate aśāsitvā tu taṃ rājā stenasyāpnoti kilbiṣam
8.d: शासनाद्वा विमोक्षाद्वा स्तेनः स्तेयाद्विमुच्यते अशासित्वा तु तं राजा स्तेनस्याप्नोति किल्बिषम्
8.e: The thief becomes absolved from the theft, either through punishment or through acquittal. By not punishing the thief, the king imbibes the guilt of the thief.

8.s: annāde bhrūṇahā mārṣṭi patyau bhāryā 'pacāriṇī gurau śiṣyaśca yājyaśca steno rājani kilbiṣam
8.d: अन्नादे भ्रूणहा मार्ष्टि पत्यौ भार्या ऽपचारिणी गुरौ शिष्यश्च याज्यश्च स्तेनो राजनि किल्बिषम्
8.e: The Embryo-killer expurgates his guilt on him who eats his food, the misbehaving wife on her husband, the disciple and the sacrificer on the preceptor, and the thief on the king.

8.s: rājabhiḥ kṛtadaṇḍāstu kṛtvā pāpāni mānavāḥ rājabhirdhṛtadaṇḍāstu nirmalāḥ svargamāyānti santaḥ sukṛtino yathā
8.d: राजभिः कृतदण्डास्तु कृत्वा पापानि मानवाः राजभिर्धृतदण्डास्तु निर्मलाः स्वर्गमायान्ति सन्तः सुकृतिनो यथा
8.e: Men who, having committed crimes, have been punished by Kings, become freed from guilt and go to heaven, just like well-behaved good men.

8.s: yastu rajjuṃ ghaṭaṃ kūpāddharedbhindyācca yaḥ prapām sa daṇḍaṃ prāpnuyān māṣaṃ tacca tasmin samāharet
8.d: यस्तु रज्जुं घटं कूपाद्धरेद्भिन्द्याच्च यः प्रपाम् स दण्डं प्राप्नुयान् माषं तच्च तस्मिन् समाहरेत्
8.e: When one steals the rope or the water-pot from the well, or damages a water-drinking establishment, he should be punished with a fine of one ‘māṣa,’ and should restore the article to the place.

8.s: dhānyaṃ daśabhyaḥ kumbhebhyo harato 'bhyadhikaṃ vadhaḥ śeṣe 'pyekādaśaguṇaṃ dāpyastasya ca taddhanam
8.d: धान्यं दशभ्यः कुम्भेभ्यो हरतो ऽभ्यधिकं वधः शेषे ऽप्येकादशगुणं दाप्यस्तस्य च तद्धनम्
8.e: There shall be ‘immolation’ for one who steals more than ten jars of grain; in other cases he should he made to pay eleven times as much, as also make good the property to the owner.

8.s: tathā dharimameyānāṃ śatādabhyadhike vadhaḥ suvarṇarajatādīnāmuttamānāṃ ca vāsasām
8.d: तथा धरिममेयानां शतादभ्यधिके वधः सुवर्णरजतादीनामुत्तमानां च वाससाम्
8.e: In the case or articles weighed by scales,—gold, silver and the rest,—if more than a hundred (are stolen),

8.s: pañcāśatastvabhyadhike hastacchedanamiṣyate śeṣe tvekādaśaguṇaṃ mūlyāddaṇḍaṃ prakalpayet
8.d: पञ्चाशतस्त्वभ्यधिके हस्तच्छेदनमिष्यते शेषे त्वेकादशगुणं मूल्याद्दण्डं प्रकल्पयेत्
8.e: In the case of more than fifty, the cutting off of the hands is prescribed. In other cases, the king shall inflict a fine of eleven times the value.

8.s: puruṣāṇāṃ kulīnānāṃ nārīṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ mukhyānāṃ caiva ratnānāṃ haraṇe vadhamarhati
8.d: पुरुषाणां कुलीनानां नारीणां च विशेषतः मुख्यानां चैव रत्नानां हरणे वधमर्हति
8.e: For stealing noble men, and specially women, and the precious gems, the thief deserves ‘immolation.’

8.s: mahāpaśūnāṃ haraṇe śastrāṇāmauṣadhasya ca kālamāsādya kāryaṃ ca daṇḍaṃ rājā prakalpayet
8.d: महापशूनां हरणे शस्त्राणामौषधस्य च कालमासाद्य कार्यं च दण्डं राजा प्रकल्पयेत्
8.e: For the stealing of large animals, of weapons or medicines, the king shall determine the punishment, after considering the time and the purpose.

8.s: goṣu brāhmaṇasaṃsthāsu churikāyāśca bhedane kharikāyāśca paśūnāṃ haraṇe caiva sadyaḥ kāryo 'rdhapādikaḥ
8.d: गोषु ब्राह्मणसंस्थासु छुरिकायाश्च भेदने खरिकायाश्च पशूनां हरणे चैव सद्यः कार्यो ऽर्धपादिकः
8.e: For stealing cows belonging to a Brāhmaṇa, and for piercing them with the goad, and for stealing animals, the thief should be immediately made half-footed.

8.s: sūtrakārpāsakiṇvānāṃ gomayasya guḍasya ca dadhnaḥ kṣīrasya takrasya pānīyasya tṛṇasya ca
8.d: सूत्रकार्पासकिण्वानां गोमयस्य गुडस्य च दध्नः क्षीरस्य तक्रस्य पानीयस्य तृणस्य च
8.e: In the case of the theft of yarns, cotton, fermenting drug, cowdung, molasses, curds, milk, skimmed curd, water and grass (326),—of vessels made of bamboo or cane, as also of salts, earthenware, earth and ashes (327)—of fish, birds, oil, clarified butter, meat, honey, and other animal-products (328)—of other things of this kind, spirituous liquors, cooked rice and all kinds of cooked food,—the fine shall be double the value of the thing (stolen).

8.s: veṇuvaidalabhāṇḍānāṃ lavaṇānāṃ tathaiva ca mṛṇmayānāṃ ca haraṇe mṛdo bhasmana eva ca
8.d: वेणुवैदलभाण्डानां लवणानां तथैव च मृण्मयानां च हरणे मृदो भस्मन एव च
8.e: In the case of the theft of yarns, cotton, fermenting drug, cowdung, molasses, curds, milk, skimmed curd, water and grass (326),—of vessels made of bamboo or cane, as also of salts, earthenware, earth and ashes (327)—of fish, birds, oil, clarified butter, meat, honey, and other animal-products (328)—of other things of this kind, spirituous liquors, cooked rice and all kinds of cooked food,—the fine shall be double the value of the thing (stolen).

8.s: matsyānāṃ pakṣiṇāṃ caiva tailasya ca ghṛtasya ca māṃsasya madhunaścaiva yaccānyat paśusaṃbhavam
8.d: मत्स्यानां पक्षिणां चैव तैलस्य च घृतस्य च मांसस्य मधुनश्चैव यच्चान्यत् पशुसंभवम्
8.e: In the case of the theft of yarns, cotton, fermenting drug, cowdung, molasses, curds, milk, skimmed curd, water and grass (326),—of vessels made of bamboo or cane, as also of salts, earthenware, earth and ashes (327)—of fish, birds, oil, clarified butter, meat, honey, and other animal-products (328)—of other things of this kind, spirituous liquors, cooked rice and all kinds of cooked food,—the fine shall be double the value of the thing (stolen).

8.s: anyeṣāṃ caivamādīnāṃ madyānāmodanasya ca caivamādīnāmadyānām pakvānnānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ tanmulyāddviguṇo damaḥ
8.d: अन्येषां चैवमादीनां मद्यानामोदनस्य च चैवमादीनामद्यानाम् पक्वान्नानां च सर्वेषां तन्मुल्याद्द्विगुणो दमः
8.e: In the case of the theft of yarns, cotton, fermenting drug, cowdung, molasses, curds, milk, skimmed curd, water and grass (326),—of vessels made of bamboo or cane, as also of salts, earthenware, earth and ashes (327)—of fish, birds, oil, clarified butter, meat, honey, and other animal-products (328)—of other things of this kind, spirituous liquors, cooked rice and all kinds of cooked food,—the fine shall be double the value of the thing (stolen).

8.s: puṣpeṣu harite dhānye gulmavallīnageṣu ca anyeṣvaparipūteṣu daṇḍaḥ syāt pañcakṛṣṇalaḥ
8.d: पुष्पेषु हरिते धान्ये गुल्मवल्लीनगेषु च अन्येष्वपरिपूतेषु दण्डः स्यात् पञ्चकृष्णलः
8.e: For flowers, green corns, shrubs, creepers, trees and other unhusked (grains), the fine shall consist of five ‘kṛṣṇalas.’

8.s: paripūteṣu dhānyeṣu śākamūlaphaleṣu ca niranvaye śataṃ daṇḍaḥ sānvaye 'rdhaśataṃ damaḥ
8.d: परिपूतेषु धान्येषु शाकमूलफलेषु च निरन्वये शतं दण्डः सान्वये ऽर्धशतं दमः
8.e: For husked grains, for vegetables, roots and fruits, there shall be a fine of a hundred, in a case where there has been no propitiation; and fifty, where there has been propitiation.

8.s: syāt sāhasaṃ tvanvayavat prasabhaṃ karma yat kṛtam niranvayaṃ bhavet steyaṃ hṛtvā 'pavyayate ca yat
8.d: स्यात् साहसं त्वन्वयवत् प्रसभं कर्म यत् कृतम् निरन्वयं भवेत् स्तेयं हृत्वा ऽपव्ययते च यत्
8.e: If the act is committed with violence and in the presence of men, it is ‘robbery’; it is ‘theft’ when done in the absence of men, and when it is denied after having been done.

8.s: yastvetānyupakḷptāni dravyāṇi stenayennaraḥ tamādyaṃ daṇḍayedrājā yaścāgniṃ corayedgṛhāt taṃ śataṃ
8.d: यस्त्वेतान्युपकॢप्तानि द्रव्याणि स्तेनयेन्नरः तमाद्यं दण्डयेद्राजा यश्चाग्निं चोरयेद्गृहात् तं शतं
8.e: If a man steals these things when they have been prepared, the king should fine him one hundred; as also him who steals the fire from the house.

8.s: yena yena yathāṅgena steno nṛṣu viceṣṭate tat tadeva haret tasya pratyādeśāya pārthivaḥ
8.d: येन येन यथाङ्गेन स्तेनो नृषु विचेष्टते तत् तदेव हरेत् तस्य प्रत्यादेशाय पार्थिवः
8.e: By whatever limb the thief operates against men, that shall the king take off, by way of retribution.

8.s: pitā 'cāryaḥ suhṛtmātā bhāryā putraḥ purohitaḥ nādaṇḍyo nāma rājño 'sti yaḥ svadharme na tiṣṭhati
8.d: पिता ऽचार्यः सुहृत्माता भार्या पुत्रः पुरोहितः नादण्ड्यो नाम राज्ञो ऽस्ति यः स्वधर्मे न तिष्ठति
8.e: Neither the father or the preceptor or the friend or the mother or the wife or the son or the priest is unpunishable for the King, when they do not keep within their duty.

8.s: kārṣāpaṇaṃ bhaveddaṇḍyo yatrānyaḥ prākṛto janaḥ tatra rājā bhaveddaṇḍyaḥ sahasramiti dhāraṇā
8.d: कार्षापणं भवेद्दण्ड्यो यत्रान्यः प्राकृतो जनः तत्र राजा भवेद्दण्ड्यः सहस्रमिति धारणा
8.e: When an ordinary man would be fined one ‘Kārṣāpaṇa,’ the king should be fined one thousand; such is the established rule.

8.s: aṣṭāpādyaṃ tu śūdrasya steye bhavati kilbiṣam ṣoḍaśaiva tu vaiśyasya dvātriṃśat kṣatriyasya ca
8.d: अष्टापाद्यं तु शूद्रस्य स्तेये भवति किल्बिषम् षोडशैव तु वैश्यस्य द्वात्रिंशत् क्षत्रियस्य च
8.e: In the case of theft, the guilt of a Śūdra is eightfold, that of the Vaiśya sixteen-fold, and that of the Kṣatriya thirty-two-fold;—(337) that of the Brāhmaṇa sixty-four-fold, or fully hundred-fold, or twice sixty-four-fold; when he is cognisant of the good or bad quality of the act.

8.s: brāhmaṇasya catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ pūrṇaṃ vā 'pi śataṃ bhavet dviguṇā vā catuḥṣaṣṭistaddoṣaguṇaviddhi saḥ
8.d: ब्राह्मणस्य चतुःषष्टिः पूर्णं वा ऽपि शतं भवेत् द्विगुणा वा चतुःषष्टिस्तद्दोषगुणविद्धि सः
8.e: In the case of theft, the guilt of a Śūdra is eightfold, that of the Vaiśya sixteen-fold, and that of the Kṣatriya thirty-two-fold;—(337) that of the Brāhmaṇa sixty-four-fold, or fully hundred-fold, or twice sixty-four-fold; when he is cognisant of the good or bad quality of the act.

8.s: vānaspatyaṃ mūlaphalaṃ dāruagny 'rthaṃ tathaiva ca tṛṇaṃ ca gobhyo grāsārthamasteyaṃ manurabravīt
8.d: वानस्पत्यं मूलफलं दारुअग्न्य् ऽर्थं तथैव च तृणं च गोभ्यो ग्रासार्थमस्तेयं मनुरब्रवीत्
8.e: Fuel for fire and trees, roots and fruits, and grass, for feeding cows,—the taking of these Manu has declared to be no theft.

8.s: yo 'dattādāyino hastātlipseta brāhmaṇo dhanam yājanādhyāpanenāpi yathā stenastathaiva saḥ
8.d: यो ऽदत्तादायिनो हस्तात्लिप्सेत ब्राह्मणो धनम् याजनाध्यापनेनापि यथा स्तेनस्तथैव सः
8.e: If a Brāhmaṇa seeks, even by sacrificing and teaching, to obtain wealth from one who has taken what has not been given to him,—he is just like a thief.

8.s: dvijo 'dhvagaḥ kṣīṇavṛttirdvāvikṣū dve ca mūlake ādadānaḥ parakṣetrātna daṇḍaṃ dātumarhati
8.d: द्विजो ऽध्वगः क्षीणवृत्तिर्द्वाविक्षू द्वे च मूलके आददानः परक्षेत्रात्न दण्डं दातुमर्हति
8.e: If a twice-born person, running short of provisions while on a journey, takes two sugar-cane stalks, or two roots, from another man’s field, he does not deserve to be made to pay a fine.

8.s: asaṃditānāṃ saṃdātā saṃditānāṃ ca mokṣakaḥ dāsāśvarathahartā ca prāptaḥ syāccorakilbiṣam
8.d: असंदितानां संदाता संदितानां च मोक्षकः दासाश्वरथहर्ता च प्राप्तः स्याच्चोरकिल्बिषम्
8.e: One who enchains the unchained, or sets free the enchained, as also one who takes away a slave, a horse or a chariot, incurs the guilt of the thief.

8.s: anena vidhinā rājā kurvāṇaḥ stenanigraham yaśo 'smin prāpnuyātloke pretya cānuttamaṃ sukham
8.d: अनेन विधिना राजा कुर्वाणः स्तेननिग्रहम् यशो ऽस्मिन् प्राप्नुयात्लोके प्रेत्य चानुत्तमं सुखम्
8.e: By punishing thieves in accordance with th is law, the king obtains fame in this world, and after death, unsurpassable bliss.

8.s: aindraṃ sthānamabhiprepsuryaśaścākṣayamavyayam naupekṣeta kṣaṇamapi rājā sāhasikaṃ naram
8.d: ऐन्द्रं स्थानमभिप्रेप्सुर्यशश्चाक्षयमव्ययम् नौपेक्षेत क्षणमपि राजा साहसिकं नरम्
8.e: The king who is desirous of indra’s eternal place, as also of imperishable fame, shall not ignore the desperado even for a moment.

8.s: vāgduṣṭāt taskarāccaiva daṇḍenaiva ca hiṃsataḥ sāhasasya naraḥ kartā vijñeyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ
8.d: वाग्दुष्टात् तस्कराच्चैव दण्डेनैव च हिंसतः साहसस्य नरः कर्ता विज्ञेयः पापकृत्तमः
8.e: He who commits violence is to be regarded as the worst offender, as compared to one who is wicked of speech, to a thief and to one who hurts with a staff.

8.s: sāhase vartamānaṃ tu yo marṣayati pārthivaḥ sa vināśaṃ vrajatyāśu vidveṣaṃ cādhigacchati
8.d: साहसे वर्तमानं तु यो मर्षयति पार्थिवः स विनाशं व्रजत्याशु विद्वेषं चाधिगच्छति
8.e: The king who condones the perpetrator of violence quickly falls into destruction and incurs hatred.

8.s: na mitrakāraṇādrājā vipulādvā dhanāgamāt samutsṛjet sāhasikān sarvabhūtabhayāvahān
8.d: न मित्रकारणाद्राजा विपुलाद्वा धनागमात् समुत्सृजेत् साहसिकान् सर्वभूतभयावहान्
8.e: Neither for the sake of friendship, nor for the sake of a large gain of money, should the king let off the perpetrators of violence, who cause terror to all living beings.

8.s: śastraṃ dvijātibhirgrāhyaṃ dharmo yatrauparudhyate dvijātīnāṃ ca varṇānāṃ viplave kālakārite
8.d: शस्त्रं द्विजातिभिर्ग्राह्यं धर्मो यत्रौपरुध्यते द्विजातीनां च वर्णानां विप्लवे कालकारिते
8.e: Twice-born persons shall carry arms: When religion is interfered with, when there is confusion among the twice-born castes caused by the exigencies of time,—(348) in his own defence, in cases of hindrance of sacrificial fees, in the case of outrages upon Brāhmaṇas and women,—if one strikes in the cause of right, he incurs no sin.

8.s: ātmanaśca paritrāṇe dakṣiṇānāṃ ca saṅgare strīviprābhyupapattau ca ghnan dharmeṇa na duṣyati
8.d: आत्मनश्च परित्राणे दक्षिणानां च सङ्गरे स्त्रीविप्राभ्युपपत्तौ च घ्नन् धर्मेण न दुष्यति
8.e: Twice-born persons shall carry arms: When religion is interfered with, when there is confusion among the twice-born castes caused by the exigencies of time,—(348) in his own defence, in cases of hindrance of sacrificial fees, in the case of outrages upon Brāhmaṇas and women,—if one strikes in the cause of right, he incurs no sin.

8.s: guruṃ vā bālavṛddhau vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā bahuśrutam ātatāyinamāyāntaṃ hanyādevāvicārayan
8.d: गुरुं वा बालवृद्धौ वा ब्राह्मणं वा बहुश्रुतम् आततायिनमायान्तं हन्यादेवाविचारयन्
8.e: Without hesitation one should strike an approaching desperado,—be he a preceptor, a child, or an aged man, or a highly learned Brāhmaṇa.

8.s: nātatāyivadhe doṣo hanturbhavati kaścana prakāśaṃ vā 'prakāśaṃ vā manyustaṃ manyuṃ ṛcchati
8.d: नाततायिवधे दोषो हन्तुर्भवति कश्चन प्रकाशं वा ऽप्रकाशं वा मन्युस्तं मन्युं ऋच्छति
8.e: No evil of any kind accrues to the slayer for killing a desperado, either openly or secretly; as it is only Fury recoiling upon Fury.

8.s: paradārābhimarśeṣu pravṛttānnr̥̄n mahīpatiḥ udvejanakarairdaṇḍaiśchinnayitvā pravāsayet cihnayitvā
8.d: परदाराभिमर्शेषु प्रवृत्तान्न्र्̥̄न् महीपतिः उद्वेजनकरैर्दण्डैश्छिन्नयित्वा प्रवासयेत् चिह्नयित्वा
8.e: Those men who are addicted to intercourse with the wives of other men, the king shall banish after having branded them with terror-inspiring punishments.

8.s: tatsamuttho hi lokasya jāyate varṇasaṅkaraḥ yena mūlaharo 'dharmaḥ sarvanāśāya kalpate
8.d: तत्समुत्थो हि लोकस्य जायते वर्णसङ्करः येन मूलहरो ऽधर्मः सर्वनाशाय कल्पते
8.e: For out of that arises the admixture of castes among people;—whence follows root-rending unrighteousness, tending to total destruction.

8.s: parasya patnyā puruṣaḥ saṃbhāṣāṃ yojayan rahaḥ pūrvamākṣārito doṣaiḥ prāpnuyāt pūrvasāhasam
8.d: परस्य पत्न्या पुरुषः संभाषां योजयन् रहः पूर्वमाक्षारितो दोषैः प्राप्नुयात् पूर्वसाहसम्
8.e: A man who engages in secret conversation with the wife of another person,—if he is one who has been previously accused of similar offences,—should receive the penalty of the ‘first amercement.’

8.s: yastvanākṣāritaḥ pūrvamabhibhāṣate kāraṇāt na doṣaṃ prāpnuyāt kiṃ cinna hi tasya vyatikramaḥ
8.d: यस्त्वनाक्षारितः पूर्वमभिभाषते कारणात् न दोषं प्राप्नुयात् किं चिन्न हि तस्य व्यतिक्रमः
8.e: If, however, he is one who has not been previously accused, and converses with her for some good reason, he does not incur any guilt; as in his case there has been no transgression.

8.s: parastriyaṃ yo 'bhivadet tīrthe 'raṇye vane 'pi vā nadīnāṃ vā 'pi saṃbhede sa saṅgrahaṇamāpnuyāt
8.d: परस्त्रियं यो ऽभिवदेत् तीर्थे ऽरण्ये वने ऽपि वा नदीनां वा ऽपि संभेदे स सङ्ग्रहणमाप्नुयात्
8.e: He who converses with ‘another’s woman’ at a watering place, or in a wilderness, or in a forest, or at the confluence of rivers,—incurs the guilt of ‘adultery.’

8.s: upacārakriyā keliḥ sparśo bhūṣaṇavāsasām upakārakriyā saha khaṭvā 'sanaṃ caiva sarvaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam
8.d: उपचारक्रिया केलिः स्पर्शो भूषणवाससाम् उपकारक्रिया सह खट्वा ऽसनं चैव सर्वं सङ्ग्रहणं स्मृतम्
8.e: Offering help, flirting, touching of ornaments and clothes, sitting on the same bed,—all this has been declared to be ‘adultery.’

8.s: striyaṃ spṛśedadeśe yaḥ spṛṣṭo vā marṣayet tayā parasparasyānumate sarvaṃ saṅgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam
8.d: स्त्रियं स्पृशेददेशे यः स्पृष्टो वा मर्षयेत् तया परस्परस्यानुमते सर्वं सङ्ग्रहणं स्मृतम्
8.e: If one touches a woman in an improper place, or condones it when touched by her,—all this, when done with mutual consent, has been declared to be ‘adultery’

8.s: abrāhmaṇaḥ saṅgrahaṇe prāṇāntaṃ daṇḍamarhati caturṇāmapi varṇānāṃ dārā rakṣyatamāḥ sadā
8.d: अब्राह्मणः सङ्ग्रहणे प्राणान्तं दण्डमर्हति चतुर्णामपि वर्णानां दारा रक्ष्यतमाः सदा
8.e: In a case of adultery, a non-Brāhmaṇa deserves the penalty ending in death; as the wives of all the four castes are always the most deserving of protection.

8.s: bhikṣukā bandinaścaiva dīkṣitāḥ kāravastathā saṃbhāṣanaṃ saha strībhiḥ kuryuraprativāritāḥ
8.d: भिक्षुका बन्दिनश्चैव दीक्षिताः कारवस्तथा संभाषनं सह स्त्रीभिः कुर्युरप्रतिवारिताः
8.e: Mendicants, bards, persons initiated for a rite and craftsmen may converse with women, unchecked.

8.s: na saṃbhāṣāṃ parastrībhiḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ samācaret niṣiddho bhāṣamāṇastu suvarṇaṃ daṇḍamarhati
8.d: न संभाषां परस्त्रीभिः प्रतिषिद्धः समाचरेत् निषिद्धो भाषमाणस्तु सुवर्णं दण्डमर्हति
8.e: One should not converse with the wives of other men, when forbidden. If, on being forbidden, he does converse, he becomes liable to be fined one ‘suvarṇa.’

8.s: naiṣa cāraṇadāreṣu vidhirnātmaupajīviṣu sajjayanti hi te nārīrnigūḍhāścārayanti ca
8.d: नैष चारणदारेषु विधिर्नात्मौपजीविषु सज्जयन्ति हि ते नारीर्निगूढाश्चारयन्ति च
8.e: This rule does not apply to the case of the wives of dancers and singers, or of those who make a living of themselves; for these men secretly bring their women into contact (with other men), and tempt them on.

8.s: kiṃ cideva tu dāpyaḥ syāt saṃbhāṣāṃ tābhirācaran praiṣyāsu caikabhaktāsu rahaḥ pravrajitāsu ca preṣyāsu
8.d: किं चिदेव तु दाप्यः स्यात् संभाषां ताभिराचरन् प्रैष्यासु चैकभक्तासु रहः प्रव्रजितासु च प्रेष्यासु
8.e: Yet he who secretly carries on conversation with these women, or with maidservants devoted to one master, or with female ascetics, should be made to pay something.

8.s: yo 'kāmāṃ dūṣayet kanyāṃ sa sadyo vadhamarhati sakāmāṃ dūṣayaṃstulyo na vadhaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ
8.d: यो ऽकामां दूषयेत् कन्यां स सद्यो वधमर्हति सकामां दूषयंस्तुल्यो न वधं प्राप्नुयान्नरः
8.e: If a man of equal status violates an unwilling maiden, he deserves immediate death; but if he violates a willing one, he shall not suffer death.

8.s: kanyāṃ bhajantīmutkṛṣṭaṃ na kiṃ cidapi dāpayet jaghanyaṃ sevamānāṃ tu saṃyatāṃ vāsayedgṛhe
8.d: कन्यां भजन्तीमुत्कृष्टं न किं चिदपि दापयेत् जघन्यं सेवमानां तु संयतां वासयेद्गृहे
8.e: If a maiden approaches a superior person, she shall not be made to pay anything; if however she courts an inferior person, she shall be kept confined in the house.

8.s: uttamāṃ sevamānastu jaghanyo vadhamarhati śulkaṃ dadyāt sevamānaḥ samāmicchet pitā yadi
8.d: उत्तमां सेवमानस्तु जघन्यो वधमर्हति शुल्कं दद्यात् सेवमानः समामिच्छेत् पिता यदि
8.e: An inferior man courting a superior maiden deserves death; he who courts a maiden of equal status, shall pay the nuptial fee, if her father so wishes.

8.s: abhiṣahya tu yaḥ kanyāṃ kuryāddarpeṇa mānavaḥ tasyāśu kartye aṅgulyau daṇḍaṃ cārhati ṣaṭśatam kartyā aṅgulyo
8.d: अभिषह्य तु यः कन्यां कुर्याद्दर्पेण मानवः तस्याशु कर्त्ये अङ्गुल्यौ दण्डं चार्हति षट्शतम् कर्त्या अङ्गुल्यो
8.e: But if any man wantonly defiles a maiden through sheer audacity, his fingers should be instantly clipped off, or he should be fined six hundred.

8.s: sakāmāṃ dūṣayaṃstulyo nāṅgulichedamāpnuyāt dviśataṃ tu damaṃ dāpyaḥ prasaṅgavinivṛttaye
8.d: सकामां दूषयंस्तुल्यो नाङ्गुलिछेदमाप्नुयात् द्विशतं तु दमं दाप्यः प्रसङ्गविनिवृत्तये
8.e: A man of equal status defiling a willing maiden shall not suffer amputation of fingers; he should be made to pay the fine of two hundred with a view to prevent repetition.

8.s: kanyaiva kanyāṃ yā kuryāt tasyāḥ syāddviśato damaḥ śulkaṃ ca dviguṇaṃ dadyātśiphāścaivāpnuyāddaśa
8.d: कन्यैव कन्यां या कुर्यात् तस्याः स्याद्द्विशतो दमः शुल्कं च द्विगुणं दद्यात्शिफाश्चैवाप्नुयाद्दश
8.e: If a maiden pollutes another maiden, her fine shall be two hundred; she shall also pay the double of her nuptial fee and shall receive ten lashes.

8.s: yā tu kanyāṃ prakuryāt strī sā sadyo mauṇḍyamarhati aṅgulyoreva vā chedaṃ khareṇaudvahanaṃ tathā
8.d: या तु कन्यां प्रकुर्यात् स्त्री सा सद्यो मौण्ड्यमर्हति अङ्गुल्योरेव वा छेदं खरेणौद्वहनं तथा
8.e: But if a woman pollutes a maiden, she deserves immediate shaving off, or the amputation of two fingers, and also being carried by a donkey.

8.s: bhartāraṃ laṅghayedyā tu strī jñātiguṇadarpitā tāṃ śvabhiḥ khādayedrājā saṃsthāne bahusaṃsthite
8.d: भर्तारं लङ्घयेद्या तु स्त्री ज्ञातिगुणदर्पिता तां श्वभिः खादयेद्राजा संस्थाने बहुसंस्थिते
8.e: If a woman, proud of relations and her qualities, passes over her husband, the king shall have her devoured by dogs in a place frequented by many.

8.s: pumāṃsaṃ dāhayet pāpaṃ śayane tapta āyase abhyādadhyuśca kāṣṭhāni tatra dahyeta pāpakṛt
8.d: पुमांसं दाहयेत् पापं शयने तप्त आयसे अभ्यादध्युश्च काष्ठानि तत्र दह्येत पापकृत्
8.e: The offending male he should make to lie down upon a redhot iron bed; they shall put wooden-logs over him, so that the sinner may be burnt.

8.s: saṃvatsarābhiśastasya duṣṭasya dviguṇo damaḥ saṃvatsare 'bhiśastasya vrātyayā saha saṃvāse cāṇḍālyā tāvadeva tu
8.d: संवत्सराभिशस्तस्य दुष्टस्य द्विगुणो दमः संवत्सरे ऽभिशस्तस्य व्रात्यया सह संवासे चाण्डाल्या तावदेव तु
8.e: If the convicted man is accused again within a year, he shall be punished with a double fine. the same also in the case of intercourse with a ‘vrātyā’ or a ‘chāṇḍālī.’

8.s: śūdro guptamaguptaṃ vā dvaijātaṃ varṇamāvasan aguptamaṅgasarvasvairguptaṃ sarveṇa hīyate 'ṅgasarvasvī
8.d: शूद्रो गुप्तमगुप्तं वा द्वैजातं वर्णमावसन् अगुप्तमङ्गसर्वस्वैर्गुप्तं सर्वेण हीयते ऽङ्गसर्वस्वी
8.e: A śūdra having intercourse with a twice-born woman, protected or unprotected, shall be deprived of his limb and his whole property, in the case of the unprotected woman, and of everything in that of the protected.

8.s: vaiśyaḥ sarvasvadaṇḍaḥ syāt saṃvatsaranirodhataḥ sahasraṃ kṣatriyo daṇḍyo mauṇḍyaṃ mūtreṇa cārhati
8.d: वैश्यः सर्वस्वदण्डः स्यात् संवत्सरनिरोधतः सहस्रं क्षत्रियो दण्ड्यो मौण्ड्यं मूत्रेण चार्हति
8.e: The Vaiśya should be fined his entire property after a year’s imprisonment; the Kṣatriya is to be fined one thousand, and be shaved with urine.

8.s: brāhmaṇīṃ yadyaguptāṃ tu gacchetāṃ vaiśyapārthivau vaiśyaṃ pañcaśataṃ kuryāt kṣatriyaṃ tu sahasriṇam
8.d: ब्राह्मणीं यद्यगुप्तां तु गच्छेतां वैश्यपार्थिवौ वैश्यं पञ्चशतं कुर्यात् क्षत्रियं तु सहस्रिणम्
8.e: If the Vaiśya and the Kṣatriya have intercourse with an unprotected Brāhmaṇa woman, the Vaiśya should be committed with five hundred and the Kṣatriya with one thousand.

8.s: ubhāvapi tu tāveva brāhmaṇyā guptayā saha viplutau śūdravaddaṇḍyau dagdhavyau vā kaṭāgninā
8.d: उभावपि तु तावेव ब्राह्मण्या गुप्तया सह विप्लुतौ शूद्रवद्दण्ड्यौ दग्धव्यौ वा कटाग्निना
8.e: But both these, when offending against a protected Brāhmaṇa woman, should be punished like a Śūdra, or burnt in a fire of dry grass.

8.s: sahasraṃ brāhmaṇo daṇḍyo guptāṃ viprāṃ balādvrajan śatāni pañca daṇḍyaḥ syādicchantyā saha saṅgataḥ
8.d: सहस्रं ब्राह्मणो दण्ड्यो गुप्तां विप्रां बलाद्व्रजन् शतानि पञ्च दण्ड्यः स्यादिच्छन्त्या सह सङ्गतः
8.e: The Brāhmaṇa who has intercourse with a protected Brāhmaṇa woman by force should be fined one thousand; he who has connection with a willing one, should be fined five hundred.

8.s: mauṇḍyaṃ prāṇāntikaṃ daṇḍo brāhmaṇasya vidhīyate prāṇāntako] "prāṇāntika " itareṣāṃ tu varṇānāṃ daṇḍaḥ prāṇāntiko bhavet prāṇāntako
8.d: मौण्ड्यं प्राणान्तिकं दण्डो ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते प्राणान्तको] "प्राणान्तिक " इतरेषां तु वर्णानां दण्डः प्राणान्तिको भवेत् प्राणान्तको
8.e: Tonsure has been prescribed as the death-penalty for the Brāhmaṇa; for other castes the penalty would be actual death.

8.s: na jātu brāhmaṇaṃ hanyāt sarvapāpeṣvapi sthitam rāṣṭrādenaṃ bahiḥ kuryāt samagradhanamakṣatam
8.d: न जातु ब्राह्मणं हन्यात् सर्वपापेष्वपि स्थितम् राष्ट्रादेनं बहिः कुर्यात् समग्रधनमक्षतम्
8.e: Verily he shall not kill the Brāhmaṇa, even though he be steeped in all crimes; he should banish him from the kingdom, with all his property and unhurt.

8.s: na brāhmaṇavadhādbhūyānadharmo vidyate bhuvi tasmādasya vadhaṃ rājā manasā 'pi na cintayet
8.d: न ब्राह्मणवधाद्भूयानधर्मो विद्यते भुवि तस्मादस्य वधं राजा मनसा ऽपि न चिन्तयेत्
8.e: There is no greater crime on earth than the slaying of a Brāhmaṇa; the king shall, therefore, not even think of his death in his mind.

8.s: vaiśyaścet kṣatriyāṃ guptāṃ vaiśyāṃ vā kṣatriyo vrajet yo brāhmaṇyāmaguptāyāṃ tāvubhau daṇḍamarhataḥ
8.d: वैश्यश्चेत् क्षत्रियां गुप्तां वैश्यां वा क्षत्रियो व्रजेत् यो ब्राह्मण्यामगुप्तायां तावुभौ दण्डमर्हतः
8.e: If a Vaiśya approaches a protected Kṣatriya woman, or the Kṣatriya a Vaiśya woman,—both these deserve the same punishment as that in the case of an unprotected Brāhmaṇa woman.

8.s: sahasraṃ brāhmaṇo daṇḍaṃ dāpyo gupte tu te vrajan śūdrāyāṃ kṣatriyaviśoḥ sāhasro vai bhaveddamaḥ śūdrāyā
8.d: सहस्रं ब्राह्मणो दण्डं दाप्यो गुप्ते तु ते व्रजन् शूद्रायां क्षत्रियविशोः साहस्रो वै भवेद्दमः शूद्राया
8.e: The Brāhmaṇa having intercourse with the said two, when protected, should be made to pay a fine of one thousand; the fine for the Kṣatriya and the Vaiśya approaching a Śūdra woman, should be one thousand.

8.s: kṣatriyāyāmaguptāyāṃ vaiśye pañcaśataṃ damaḥ mūtreṇa mauṇḍyamicchet tu kṣatriyo daṇḍameva vā ṛcchet tu
8.d: क्षत्रियायामगुप्तायां वैश्ये पञ्चशतं दमः मूत्रेण मौण्ड्यमिच्छेत् तु क्षत्रियो दण्डमेव वा ऋच्छेत् तु
8.e: In the case of the Vaiśya approaching an unprotected Kṣatriya woman, the fine shall be five hundred; but the Kṣatriya may suffer tonsure or the fine.

8.s: agupte kṣatriyāvaiśye śūdrāṃ vā brāhmaṇo vrajan śatāni pañca daṇḍyaḥ syāt sahasraṃ tvantyajastriyam
8.d: अगुप्ते क्षत्रियावैश्ये शूद्रां वा ब्राह्मणो व्रजन् शतानि पञ्च दण्ड्यः स्यात् सहस्रं त्वन्त्यजस्त्रियम्
8.e: The Brāhmaṇa, approaching an unprotected Vaiśya or Kṣatriya woman, should be fined five hundred, and one thousand for approaching a woman of the lowest order.

8.s: yasya stenaḥ pure nāsti nānyastrīgo na duṣṭavāk na sāhasikadaṇḍaghno sa rājā śakralokabhāk
8.d: यस्य स्तेनः पुरे नास्ति नान्यस्त्रीगो न दुष्टवाक् न साहसिकदण्डघ्नो स राजा शक्रलोकभाक्
8.e: That king in whose town there is no thief, no adulterer, no defamer, no criminal, no assaulter,—attains the regions of Indra.

8.s: eteṣāṃ nigraho rājñaḥ pañcānāṃ viṣaye svake sāṃrājyakṛt sajātyeṣu loke caiva yaśaskaraḥ
8.d: एतेषां निग्रहो राज्ञः पञ्चानां विषये स्वके सांराज्यकृत् सजात्येषु लोके चैव यशस्करः
8.e: The suppression of these five in his own dominions secures to the king paramount sovereignty among his peers and fame in the world.

8.s: ṛtvijaṃ yastyajedyājyo yājyaṃ ca rtvik tyajedyadi śaktaṃ karmaṇyaduṣṭaṃ ca tayordaṇḍaḥ śataṃ śatam
8.d: ऋत्विजं यस्त्यजेद्याज्यो याज्यं च र्त्विक् त्यजेद्यदि शक्तं कर्मण्यदुष्टं च तयोर्दण्डः शतं शतम्
8.e: If a sacrificer forsakes an officiating priest, and if an officiating priest forsakes a sacrificer,—each being capable of doing the work and free from disqualifications,—their punishment is one hundred each

8.s: na mātā na pitā na strī na putrastyāgamarhati tyajannapatitānetān rājñā daṇḍyaḥ śatāni ṣaṭ
8.d: न माता न पिता न स्त्री न पुत्रस्त्यागमर्हति त्यजन्नपतितानेतान् राज्ञा दण्ड्यः शतानि षट्
8.e: Neither the mother, nor the father, nor the wife, nor the son deserve to be forsaken; he who forsakes these, unless they are outcasts, should be fined six hundred by the king.

8.s: āśrameṣu dvijātīnāṃ kārye vivadatāṃ mithaḥ na vibrūyānnṛpo dharmaṃ cikīrṣan hitamātmanaḥ
8.d: आश्रमेषु द्विजातीनां कार्ये विवदतां मिथः न विब्रूयान्नृपो धर्मं चिकीर्षन् हितमात्मनः
8.e: For twice-born men disputing among themselves regarding any point relating to the orders, the king, desirous of his own welfare, shall not determine the law.

8.s: yathārhametānabhyarcya brāhmaṇaiḥ saha pārthivaḥ sāntvena praśamayyādau svadharmaṃ pratipādayet
8.d: यथार्हमेतानभ्यर्च्य ब्राह्मणैः सह पार्थिवः सान्त्वेन प्रशमय्यादौ स्वधर्मं प्रतिपादयेत्
8.e: Having, with the assistance of Brāhmaṇas, received them with due honour, the king shall, at first, pacify them with soothing words, and then explain to them their duty.

8.s: prativeśyānuveśyau ca kalyāṇe viṃśatidvije arhāvabhojayan vipro daṇḍamarhati māṣakam
8.d: प्रतिवेश्यानुवेश्यौ च कल्याणे विंशतिद्विजे अर्हावभोजयन् विप्रो दण्डमर्हति माषकम्
8.e: If, at a festival where twenty twice-born men are invited, a Brāhmaṇa does not entertain his frontal and back neighbours, who are quite worthy,—he deserves to be fined one ‘māṣa.’

8.s: śrotriyaḥ śrotriyaṃ sādhuṃ bhūtikṛtyeṣvabhojayan tadannaṃ dviguṇaṃ dāpyo hiraṇyaṃ caiva māṣakam airaṇyaṃ
8.d: श्रोत्रियः श्रोत्रियं साधुं भूतिकृत्येष्वभोजयन् तदन्नं द्विगुणं दाप्यो हिरण्यं चैव माषकम् ऐरण्यं
8.e: The Vedic scholar who does not entertain a worthy Vedic scholar at such auspicious rites, should be made to pay twice the quantity of that meal, and also a ‘māṣa’ of gold.

8.s: andho jaḍaḥ pīṭhasarpī saptatyā sthaviraśca yaḥ śrotriyeṣūpakurvaṃśca na dāpyāḥ kena cit karam
8.d: अन्धो जडः पीठसर्पी सप्तत्या स्थविरश्च यः श्रोत्रियेषूपकुर्वंश्च न दाप्याः केन चित् करम्
8.e: A blind man, an idiot, a cripple, an old man of seventy, and one who attends upon Vedic scholars should not be made to pay any taxes by any one.

8.s: śrotriyaṃ vyādhitārtau ca bālavṛddhāvakiñcanam mahākulīnamāryaṃ ca rājā saṃpūjayet sadā
8.d: श्रोत्रियं व्याधितार्तौ च बालवृद्धावकिञ्चनम् महाकुलीनमार्यं च राजा संपूजयेत् सदा
8.e: The king should always respect the Vedic scholar, the sick and the distressed, the infant and the aged, the indigent, the man of high family and the gentleman.

8.s: śālmalīphalake ślakṣṇe nenijyānnejakaḥ śanaiḥ na ca vāsāṃsi vāsobhirnirharenna ca vāsayet
8.d: शाल्मलीफलके श्लक्ष्णे नेनिज्यान्नेजकः शनैः न च वासांसि वासोभिर्निर्हरेन्न च वासयेत्
8.e: The washerman shall wash (clothes) gently on a smooth board of cotton-tree wood; he shall not carry clothes in other clothes; nor shall he allow them to be worn.

8.s: tantuvāyo daśapalaṃ dadyādekapalādhikam ato 'nyathā vartamāno dāpyo dvādaśakaṃ damam
8.d: तन्तुवायो दशपलं दद्यादेकपलाधिकम् अतो ऽन्यथा वर्तमानो दाप्यो द्वादशकं दमम्
8.e: The weaver shall repay ten ‘palas’ with one ‘pala’ added to it; if he acts otherwise than this, he should be made to pay a fine of twelve.

8.s: śulkasthāneṣu kuśalāḥ sarvapaṇyavicakṣaṇāḥ kuryurarghaṃ yathāpaṇyaṃ tato viṃśaṃ nṛpo haret
8.d: शुल्कस्थानेषु कुशलाः सर्वपण्यविचक्षणाः कुर्युरर्घं यथापण्यं ततो विंशं नृपो हरेत्
8.e: The king shall take one-twentieth of the price of saleable commodities, that may be fixed by men who have experience of custom-houses and are experts in all kinds of merchandise.

8.s: rājñaḥ prakhyātabhāṇḍāni pratiṣiddhāni yāni ca tāṇi nirharato lobhāt sarvahāraṃ harennṛpaḥ
8.d: राज्ञः प्रख्यातभाण्डानि प्रतिषिद्धानि यानि च ताणि निर्हरतो लोभात् सर्वहारं हरेन्नृपः
8.e: Those commodities that have been proclaimed as the ‘king’s monopoly,’ and those that are forbidden,—if any one, through greed, exports these, the king shall confiscate all his property.

8.s: śulkasthānaṃ pariharannakāle krayavikrayī mithyāvādī ca saṅkhyāne dāpyo 'ṣṭaguṇamatyayam
8.d: शुल्कस्थानं परिहरन्नकाले क्रयविक्रयी मिथ्यावादी च सङ्ख्याने दाप्यो ऽष्टगुणमत्ययम्
8.e: If one who buts and sells avoids a custom-house, and at the improper time, or makes a wrong statement in counting,—he shall be made to pay a fine eight times the amount evaded.

8.s: āgamaṃ nirgamaṃ sthānaṃ tathā vṛddhikṣayāvubhau vicārya sarvapaṇyānāṃ kārayet krayavikrayau
8.d: आगमं निर्गमं स्थानं तथा वृद्धिक्षयावुभौ विचार्य सर्वपण्यानां कारयेत् क्रयविक्रयौ
8.e: The king shall regulate the purchase and sale of all marketable commodities after having taken into consideration their source, destination and detention, as also profit and loss.

8.s: pañcarātre pañcarātre pakṣe pakṣe 'tha vā gate kurvīta caiṣāṃ pratyakṣamarghasaṃsthāpanaṃ nṛpaḥ
8.d: पञ्चरात्रे पञ्चरात्रे पक्षे पक्षे ऽथ वा गते कुर्वीत चैषां प्रत्यक्षमर्घसंस्थापनं नृपः
8.e: After the lapse of every five days, or after that of every fortnight, the king shall publicly fix the prices of things.

8.s: tulāmānaṃ pratīmānaṃ sarvaṃ ca syāt sulakṣitam ṣaṭsu ṣaṭsu ca māseṣu punareva parīkṣayet
8.d: तुलामानं प्रतीमानं सर्वं च स्यात् सुलक्षितम् षट्सु षट्सु च मासेषु पुनरेव परीक्षयेत्
8.e: Scales, weights and measures should be duly marked; and they should be re-examined after every six months.

8.s: paṇaṃ yānaṃ tare dāpyaṃ pauruṣo 'rdhapaṇaṃ tare pādaṃ paśuśca yoṣitca pādārdhaṃ riktakaḥ pumān pāde
8.d: पणं यानं तरे दाप्यं पौरुषो ऽर्धपणं तरे पादं पशुश्च योषित्च पादार्धं रिक्तकः पुमान् पादे
8.e: At a ferry-crossing, a cart shall be made to pay one ‘paṇa’; one man’s burden half a ‘paṇa,’ an animal and a woman a quarter ‘paṇa,’ and an unloaded man one half of a quarter.

8.s: bhāṇḍapūrṇāni yānāni tāryaṃ dāpyāni sārataḥ riktabhāṇḍāni yat kiṃ cit pumāṃsaścaparicchadāḥ
8.d: भाण्डपूर्णानि यानानि तार्यं दाप्यानि सारतः रिक्तभाण्डानि यत् किं चित् पुमांसश्चपरिच्छदाः
8.e: Carts laden with commodities should be made to pay the ferry-toll according to their value; those not laden with commodities may pay a triple, as also men without luggage.

8.s: dīrghādhvani yathādeśaṃ yathākālaṃ taro bhavet nadītīreṣu tadvidyāt samudre nāsti lakṣaṇam
8.d: दीर्घाध्वनि यथादेशं यथाकालं तरो भवेत् नदीतीरेषु तद्विद्यात् समुद्रे नास्ति लक्षणम्
8.e: For a long passage, the boat-fare should be in propor tion to the time and place; this should be understood to be the rule regarding the banks of rivers; in connection with the sea, there is no fixed rule.

8.s: garbhiṇī tu dvimāsādistathā pravrajito muniḥ brāhmaṇā liṅginaścaiva na dāpyāstārikaṃ tare
8.d: गर्भिणी तु द्विमासादिस्तथा प्रव्रजितो मुनिः ब्राह्मणा लिङ्गिनश्चैव न दाप्यास्तारिकं तरे
8.e: But a woman who is pregnant two months or more, an ascetic, a hermit, and brāhmaṇas in holy orders shall not be made to pay the toll at a ferry-crossing.

8.s: yannāvi kiṃ ciddāśānāṃ viśīryetāparādhataḥ taddāśaireva dātavyaṃ samāgamya svato 'ṃśataḥ
8.d: यन्नावि किं चिद्दाशानां विशीर्येतापराधतः तद्दाशैरेव दातव्यं समागम्य स्वतो ऽंशतः
8.e: If anything on the boat happen to be damaged by the fault of the boatmen,—it shall be made good by the boatmen collectively, each according to his share.

8.s: eṣa nauyāyināmukto vyavahārasya nirṇayaḥ dāśāparādhatastoye daivike nāsti nigrahaḥ
8.d: एष नौयायिनामुक्तो व्यवहारस्य निर्णयः दाशापराधतस्तोये दैविके नास्ति निग्रहः
8.e: This law has been laid down in connection with suits by boat-passengers relating to the negligence of boatmen in water; there is no punishment in the case of accidents due to heaven.

8.s: vāṇijyaṃ kārayedvaiśyaṃ kusīdaṃ kṛṣimeva ca paśūnāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ caiva dāsyaṃ śūdraṃ dvijanmanām
8.d: वाणिज्यं कारयेद्वैश्यं कुसीदं कृषिमेव च पशूनां रक्षणं चैव दास्यं शूद्रं द्विजन्मनाम्
8.e: He shall make the Vaiśya to carry on trade, money-lending, agriculture,—and cattle-trading; and the Śūdra to perform service for the twice-born castes.

8.s: kṣatriyaṃ caiva vaiśyaṃ ca brāhmaṇo vṛttikarśitau bibhṛyādānṛśaṃsyena svāni karmāṇi kārayet
8.d: क्षत्रियं चैव वैश्यं च ब्राह्मणो वृत्तिकर्शितौ बिभृयादानृशंस्येन स्वानि कर्माणि कारयेत्
8.e: A Brāhmaṇa shall, through compassion, support a Vaiśya and a Kṣatriya, who are distressed for a livelihood, and should make them do his own work.

8.s: dāsyaṃ tu kārayanlobhādbrāhmaṇaḥ saṃskṛtān dvijān anicchataḥ prābhavatyādrājñā daṇḍyaḥ śatāni ṣaṭ
8.d: दास्यं तु कारयन्लोभाद्ब्राह्मणः संस्कृतान् द्विजान् अनिच्छतः प्राभवत्याद्राज्ञा दण्ड्यः शतानि षट्
8.e: If the Brāhmaṇa, through the sense of mastery, and out of greed, makes sanctified twice-born persons do fertile work, against their will,—he should be fined by the king six hundred.

8.s: śūdraṃ tu kārayeddāsyaṃ krītamakrītameva vā dāsyāyaiva hi sṛṣṭo 'sau brāhmaṇasya svayaṃbhuvā
8.d: शूद्रं तु कारयेद्दास्यं क्रीतमक्रीतमेव वा दास्यायैव हि सृष्टो ऽसौ ब्राह्मणस्य स्वयंभुवा
8.e: But a Śūdra, whether bought or unbought, he shall make to do servile work; since it is for doing servile work for the Brāhmaṇa that he has been created by the self-born one.

8.s: na svāminā nisṛṣṭo 'pi śūdro dāsyādvimucyate nisargajaṃ hi tat tasya kastasmāt tadapohati
8.d: न स्वामिना निसृष्टो ऽपि शूद्रो दास्याद्विमुच्यते निसर्गजं हि तत् तस्य कस्तस्मात् तदपोहति
8.e: Even though set free by the master, the Śūdra is not released from service; since that is innate in him, and who can release him from it?

8.s: dhvajāhṛto bhaktadāso gṛhajaḥ krītadattrimau paitriko daṇḍadāsaśca saptaite dāsayonayaḥ
8.d: ध्वजाहृतो भक्तदासो गृहजः क्रीतदत्त्रिमौ पैत्रिको दण्डदासश्च सप्तैते दासयोनयः
8.e: There are seven kinds of slaves—(1) captured under a banner, (2) slave on food, (3) born in the house, (4) bought, (5) presented, (6) hereditary, and (7) slave by punishment.

8.s: bhāryā putraśca dāsaśca traya evādhanāḥ smṛtāḥ yat te samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya taddhanam
8.d: भार्या पुत्रश्च दासश्च त्रय एवाधनाः स्मृताः यत् ते समधिगच्छन्ति यस्य ते तस्य तद्धनम्
8.e: The wive, the son and the slave,—these three are declared to have no property; whatever they acquire is the property of him to whom they belong.

8.s: visrabdhaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ śūdrāddravyaupādānamācaret na hi tasyāsti kiṃ cit svaṃ bhartṛhāryadhano hi saḥ
8.d: विस्रब्धं ब्राह्मणः शूद्राद्द्रव्यौपादानमाचरेत् न हि तस्यास्ति किं चित् स्वं भर्तृहार्यधनो हि सः
8.e: The Brāhmaṇa may confidently have recourse to seizing the goods of the Śūdra; as the latter has no property, and his property is meant to be seized by the master.

8.s: vaiśyaśūdrau prayatnena svāni karmāṇi kārayet tau hi cyutau svakarmabhyaḥ kṣobhayetāmidaṃ jagat
8.d: वैश्यशूद्रौ प्रयत्नेन स्वानि कर्माणि कारयेत् तौ हि च्युतौ स्वकर्मभ्यः क्षोभयेतामिदं जगत्
8.e: The king shall make the Vaiśya and the Shudra carefully to perform their duties; for by swerving from their duties they would disturb this world.

8.s: ahanyahanyavekṣeta karmāntān vāhanāni ca āyavyayau ca niyatāvākarān kośameva ca
8.d: अहन्यहन्यवेक्षेत कर्मान्तान् वाहनानि च आयव्ययौ च नियतावाकरान् कोशमेव च
8.e: Day after day he shall look after his business-centres, his conveyances, his income and expenditure regularly, and mines and treasury.
